children.translated_text: <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsasūtram</s> (The Sūtra of Golden Light)

body.text: // suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Supreme King of Sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s> (Most Excellent Golden Light) //

body.text: // nidānaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Nidāna</s> (Introduction) Chapter //

body.text:
om namaḥ śrīsarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ /
om namaḥ śrībhagavatyai āryaprajñāpāramitāyai // tadyathā /
om śrutismṛtigativijaye svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to all the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the blessed noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)! That is to say: <s>Oṃ</s>, victory to hearing, memory, understanding, and mastery! <s>Svāhā</s>!

children.translated_text: In which the ten supreme <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) with their respective methods are indicated,

children.text: sarvajñena jagaddhitāya daśa ca prakhyāpitā bhūmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: and the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) have been proclaimed by the Omniscient One for the welfare of the world;
and the Middle Way (<s>madhyamā gati</s>), pure, free from [the extremes of] annihilation and eternalism, has been taught —
let those who seek awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) listen to that sūtra, proclaimed as the Golden Light!

body.text: śrutaṃ mayaikasamaye gṛdhrakūṭe tathāgataḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard at one time: on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), the <s>Tathāgata</s>

body.text: vijahāra dharmadhātau gambhīre buddhagocare // Suv_1.1 //
body.translated_text: dwelt in the profound <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>Dharma</s>), the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>. // Suv_1.1 //

body.text: bodhisattvasamuccayayā mahākuladevatayā, sarasvatyā ca mahādevatayā, śriyā ca mahādevatayā, dṛḍhayā ca mahāpṛthivīdevatayā, hārītyā ca mahādevatayā, evaṃ pramukhābhirmahādevatābhiranekadevanāgayakṣarākṣasagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ sārdham / athāyuṣmānānando bhagavantametadavocat / kiṃ tāsāṃ bhagavandharmavinayaṃ bhaviṣyatīti?
body.translated_text: Together with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly, the great deity <s>Mahākuladevī</s>, the great deity <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the great deity <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the great earth-deity <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, the great deity <s>Hārītī</s> — preceded by these and other great deities — along with multitudes of gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said to the Blessed One: 'What, O Blessed One, will be the <s>Dharma</s>-discipline for them?'

body.text: bhagavānāha gāthābhiḥ / bhāvanaṃ ca na duḥpṛcchayā virajaskaṃ samādhiṃ dharmasāraṃ pratiṣṭhitam /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One spoke in verses: 'The cultivation, through respectful inquiry, of the stainless <s>samādhi</s> established in the essence of the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.translated_text: among the pure and stainless, the most excellent <s>Bodhisattvas</s> —
this <s>nidāna</s> (introduction) to the king of sūtras, the most excellent <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> (Golden Light), is this. // Suv_1.2 //
Then, through profound hearing and profound investigation,
it was blessed by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the four directions with their empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>). // Suv_1.3 //
King <s>Akṣobhya</s> in the east; <s>Ratnaketu</s> in the south;
<s>Amitābha</s> in the west; <s>Dundubhisvara</s> in the north. // Suv_1.4 //
I shall proclaim that empowerment, the supreme auspicious teaching,
for the destruction of all sins, which causes the extinction of all evil. // Suv_1.5 //
The bestower of all happiness, the destroyer of all suffering,
the root of omniscient truth, adorned with all glory. // Suv_1.6 //

children.text: upahatendriyā ye hi sattvā naṣṭā hatāyuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those beings whose faculties are impaired, who are ruined and whose lifespan is destroyed,

children.text: alakṣmyā pariviṣṭā hi devatāsu parāṅmukhāḥ // Suv_1.7 //
children.translated_text: who are beset by misfortune and turned away from the deities; // Suv_1.7 //
those people who are hated by their loved ones, afflicted by family troubles and the like,
or mutually hostile, or afflicted by loss of wealth; // Suv_1.8 //

children.text: śokāyāseṣvanarthe ca bhaye vyasana eva ca /
children.translated_text: in grief, distress, calamity, fear, and disaster,
when tormented by planetary and stellar afflictions, by terrible and fierce evil influences (<s>grahas</s>); // Suv_1.9 //
one who sees evil dreams, arisen from grief and distress —

children.text: tena ca snānaśucinā śrotavyaṃ sūtramuttamam // Suv_1.10 //
children.translated_text: by that person, having bathed and being pure, this supreme sūtra should be heard. // Suv_1.10 //

children.text: śṛṇvanti ya idaṃ sūtraṃ gambhīraṃ buddhagocaram /
children.translated_text: Those who hear this sūtra, profound, the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
with clear minds, with joyful hearts, adorned with clean garments — // Suv_1.11 //
for them, all those terribly severe afflictions,

children.text: tejasā cāsya sūtrasya śāmyante sarvaprāṇinām // Suv_1.12 //
children.translated_text: by the power of this sūtra, are pacified for all beings. // Suv_1.12 //
The <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians) themselves, together with their ministers and retinues,
will provide protection for them, with many tens of millions of <s>yakṣas</s>. // Suv_1.13 //
The great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and the one who dwells at <s>Nairañjanā</s>,

children.text: hārītī bhūtamātā ca dṛḍhā pṛthivīdevatā // Suv_1.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hārītī</s> the mother of spirits, and <s>Dṛḍhā</s> the earth-goddess; // Suv_1.14 //
with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the lords of the thirty [gods], the lords of the <s>kinnaras</s> of great magical power,
together with <s>Garuḍa</s>-lords, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>nāgas</s> — // Suv_1.15 //
they shall approach there, with their armies, forces, and vehicles,

children.text: teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti divārātrau samāhitāḥ // Suv_1.16 //
children.translated_text: and provide protection for them, day and night, with concentrated mind. // Suv_1.16 //
I shall illuminate this sūtra, profound, the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
the secret of all <s>Buddhas</s>, difficult to obtain in tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s>. // Suv_1.17 //

children.text: śṛṇvanti ya idaṃ sūtraṃ ye cānye śrāvayanti ca /
children.translated_text: Those who hear this sūtra, and those others who cause it to be heard,

children.text: ye kecidanumodante ye ca pūjāṃ karonti hi // Suv_1.18 //
children.translated_text: those who rejoice [in it], and those who perform worship of it — // Suv_1.18 //

body.text:
te pūjitā bhaviṣyanti hyanekaiḥ kalpakoṭibhiḥ /
devanāgamanuṣyaiśca kinnarāsuraguhyakaiḥ // Suv_1.19 // puṇyaskandhamaparyantamasaṃkhyeyamacintitam /

children.text: yatteṣāṃ prasṛtaṃ bhoti kṛtapuṇyāna prāṇinām // Suv_1.20 //
children.translated_text: flows forth for those beings who have made merit. // Suv_1.20 //

body.translated_text: they shall be worshipped for many tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s> by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, humans, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>guhyakas</s>. // Suv_1.19 // An immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable mass of merit

children.translated_text: They shall be taken hold of by all the <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions,
and likewise by the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of profound conduct. // Suv_1.21 //
Covering oneself with clean robes, [and using] fragrant, purifying water,
having generated a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), one should worship [this sūtra] diligently. // Suv_1.22 //
A vast and stainless mind will develop itself;
generating joy in [all] minds, listen to this supreme sūtra! // Suv_1.23 //

children.text: svāgataṃ ca manuṣyeṣu sulabdhaṃ manuṣaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: Welcome [is it] among humans, and well-obtained is the fruit of human [birth];

children.text: sujīvitāśca jīvanti sūtraṃ śṛṇvanti ye tvidam // Suv_1.24 //
children.translated_text: they have truly lived well who hear this sūtra. // Suv_1.24 //
Their roots of merit have been planted, illuminated by many <s>Buddhas</s>,
for those into whose ear-openings this teaching enters. // Suv_1.25 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje nidānaparivartto nāma prathamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the first chapter, the <s>Nidāna</s> (Introduction) Chapter, in the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Tathāgatāyuḥpramāṇanirdeśaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Chapter on the Measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Lifespan (<s>Tathāgatāyuḥpramāṇanirdeśa</s>) //

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ kālena tena samayena rājagṛhe mahānagare ruciraketurnāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prativasati pūrvajinakṛtādhikāro 'varopitakuśalamūlo bahubuddhakoṭiniyutaśatasahasraparyupāsitaḥ / tasyaitadabhavat, ko hetu kaḥ pratyayo yadbhagavataḥ śākyamunerevaṃ parīttamāyuḥ pramāṇaṃ yadutāśītivarṣāṇīti /
body.translated_text: Now at that time, in the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there dwelt a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Ruciraketu</s>, who had performed meritorious acts under former <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), had planted roots of merit, and had attended upon many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Buddhas</s>. This thought occurred to him: 'What is the cause, what is the condition, that the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>'s lifespan is so limited — namely, eighty years?'

body.text: punastasyaitadabhavat, uktaṃ caiva bhagavatā dvau hetū dvau ca pratyayau dīrghāyuṣkatāyām / katamau dvau prāṇātipātaviramaṇaṃ bhojanapradānaṃ ca / atha bahunyasaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi bhagavāñchākyamuniḥ prāṇātipātavirato babhūva / yāvaddaśakuśalakarmapathaṃ samādāpayet, tāvadbhagavatā bhojanamādhyātmikaṃ bāhyāni ca vastūni sattvānāṃ parityaktāni / antaśaḥ svaśarīramāṃsarudhirāsthimajjayā bubhukṣitāḥ sattvāḥ saṃtarpitāḥ prāgevānyena bhojanena /
body.translated_text: Then this further thought occurred to him: 'The Blessed One has indeed said that there are two causes and two conditions for longevity: abstaining from the taking of life, and the giving of food.' Now, for innumerable hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>kalpas</s>, the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s> had abstained from the taking of life. And as far as he would establish [beings] in the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśa-kuśala-karmapatha</s>), so far did the Blessed One relinquish to beings his own internal food, external possessions — and even his own body's flesh, blood, bones, and marrow, satisfying hungry beings; how much more so with other food!

body.text: atha tasya puruṣasya buddhānusmṛtimanasikārasyemāmevaṃrūpāṃ cintāṃ cintayamānasya gṛhaṃ vipulaṃ vistīrṇaṃ saṃpravṛttamabhavat / vaiḍūryamayamanekadivyaratnapratyuptaṃ tathāgatavigrahaṃ divyātikrāntena gandhena sphuṭam / tasmiṃśca gṛhe caturdiśi catvāri divyaratnamayānyāsanāni prādurbhutānyabhūvan / teṣu cāsaneṣu divyāni paryaṅkāni divyaratnapuṣpapatraiḥ prajñaptāni prādurbhūtāni babhūvaḥ / teṣu paryaṅkeṣu divyānyanekaratnapratyuptāni tathāgatavigrahāṇi padmāni prādurbhūtāni / teṣu ca padmeṣu catvāro buddhā bhagavantaḥ prādurbhūtāḥ babhuvuḥ / purāntikena tvakṣobhyastathāgataḥ prādurbhūto dakṣiṇena ratnaketustathāgataḥ prādurbhūtaḥ paścimenāmitāyustathāgataḥ prādurbhūta uttareṇa dundubhisvarastathāgataḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / samanantaraprādurbhūtāśca te buddhā bhagavantasteṣu siṃhāsaneṣu /
body.translated_text: Then, while that man, with his mind directed toward the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>), was contemplating this very thought, a vast and spacious house appeared. It was made of beryl (<s>vaiḍūrya</s>), set with many divine jewels, filled with the fragrance of a divine, transcendent scent, in the form of a <s>Tathāgata</s> image. And in that house, in the four directions, four divine jeweled seats appeared. Upon those seats, divine couches spread with divine jeweled flower-petals appeared. Upon those couches, divine lotuses set with many jewels appeared, in the form of <s>Tathāgata</s> images. And upon those lotuses, four <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, appeared: in the east, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s> appeared; in the south, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaketu</s> appeared; in the west, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> appeared; in the north, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dundubhisvara</s> appeared. And immediately upon their appearance, those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, [were seated] upon those lion-thrones.

body.text: atha tāvadeva rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ mahatāvabhāsenāvabhāsitaṃ sphuṭaṃ babhūvu / yāvatrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhāturyāvatsamantāddaśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā lokadhātavastenāvabhāsena sphuṭā babhūvaḥ / divyāni ca puṣpāṇi prāvarṣurdivyāni ca tūryāṇi pravādayāmāsuḥ / sarve cāsmiṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau sattvā buddhānubhāvena divyasukhena samanvāgatā babhūvuḥ / jātyandhāśca sattvā rūpāṇi paśyanti sma / vadhirāśca sattvāḥ sattvebhyaḥ śabdāni śṛṇvanti / unmattāśca sattvāḥ smṛtiṃ pratilabhante 'vikṣiptacittāśca smṛtimanto babhūvuḥ / nagnāśca sattvāścīvaraprāvṛtā
body.translated_text: Then, at that very moment, the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> was pervaded and filled with a great radiance. As far as the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra-lokadhātu</s>), as far as world-systems in the ten directions equal [in number] to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> — all were pervaded by that radiance. Divine flowers rained down, and divine musical instruments sounded. And all beings in this great trichiliocosm, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, became endowed with divine happiness. Those born blind could see forms; the deaf could hear sounds from beings; the insane regained mindfulness, and those of distracted mind became mindful. The naked became clothed in robes.

body.text: babhūvuḥ / jighatsitāśca sattvāḥ paripūrṇagātrā babhūvuḥ / tṛṣitāśca sattvā vigatatṛṣṇā babhūvaḥ / rogaspṛṣṭāśca sattvā vigatarogā babhūvuḥ / hīnakāyāśca sattvāḥ paripūrṇendriyā babhūvuḥ / vistareṇa bahūnāmāścaryādbhutadharmāṇāṃ loke prādurbhāvo 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: The hungry became full-bodied. The thirsty became free from thirst. The sick became free from illness. Those of deficient body became complete in their faculties. In brief, there was the appearance of many marvelous and wondrous phenomena in the world.

body.text: atha khalu ruciraketurbodhiosattvo mahāsattvastānbuddhānbhagavato dṛṣṭvāścaryaprāpto babhūva / kathametaditi santuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto yena te buddhā bhagavantastenāñjāliṃ praṇāmyakāratastānbuddhānbhagavato 'nusmaramāṇo bhagavataḥ śākyamunerguṇānanusmaramāṇo bhagavataḥ śākyamunerāyuḥpramāṇasaṃśayaprāptastāṃ cintāṃ cintayamānaḥ sthito babhuva / kathametat,kimetad yadbhagavataḥ śākyamunerevaṃ parīttamāyuḥpramāṇaṃ yadutāśīti varṣāṇi /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Ruciraketu</s>, having seen those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, was filled with wonder. Thinking 'How is this?', satisfied, elated, delighted, and filled with joy and gladness, he joined his palms in the direction of those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, and bowed. Recollecting those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, and recollecting the qualities of the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>, having arrived at doubt regarding the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>'s lifespan, he stood contemplating that thought: 'How is this? What is this, that the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>'s lifespan is so limited — namely, eighty years?'

body.text: atha khalu te buddhā bhagavantaḥ smṛtāḥ saṃprajānāstaṃ ruciraketuṃ bodhisattvametadavocan / mā tvaṃ kulaputraivaṃ cintaya evaṃ parīttaṃ bhagavataḥ śākyamunerāyuḥpramāṇam / tatkasya hetoḥ / na ca vai kulaputra taṃ samanupaśyāmaḥ sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāṃ prajāyāṃ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāṃ yaḥ samarthaḥ syādbhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasyāyuḥpramāṇaparyantamadhigantuṃ yāvadaparāntakoṭibhiḥ sthāpayitvā tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksambuddhaiḥ / samanantarodāhṛte tairbuddhairbhagavadbhistathāgatāyuḥpramāṇanirdeśe /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, being mindful and fully aware, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ruciraketu</s>: 'Do not, O son of good family, think thus — that the lifespan of the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s> is so limited. Why is that? For indeed, O son of good family, we do not see anyone in this world with its gods, <s>Māras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, among ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, among gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, who would be capable of reaching the limit of the lifespan of the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, even in ultimate <s>kalpas</s> — except for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones.' Immediately after those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, had uttered the teaching on the measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan,

body.text: atha tāvadbuddhānubhāvena kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarāśca devaputrāḥ saṃnipatitā yāvannāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā anekāni ca bodhisattvakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi tasmin ruciraketubodhisattvasya gṛhe samāgatā āsan / atha te tathāgatāḥ sarvaparṣado bhagavataḥ śākyamunerāyuḥpramāṇanirdeśaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣan /
body.translated_text: then, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, the gods of the realm of desire (<s>Kāmāvacara</s>) and the realm of form (<s>Rūpāvacara</s>) assembled, along with <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>, and many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> came together in the house of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ruciraketu</s>. Then those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, before the entire assembly, addressed the teaching on the measure of the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>'s lifespan in verses:

children.translated_text: The drops in all the oceans of water can be counted,

children.text: na tu śākyamunerāyuḥ śakyaṃ gaṇayituṃ kvacit // Suv_2.1 //
children.translated_text: but the lifespan of <s>Śākyamuni</s> can never be reckoned. // Suv_2.1 //

children.text: sumeruṃ paramāṇavaḥ kṛtvā śakyaṃ ca saṃkhyayā /
children.translated_text: Even <s>Sumeru</s> could be reduced to atoms and counted,

children.text: na tu śākyamunerāyuḥ śakyaṃ gaṇayituṃ kvacit // Suv_2.2 //
children.translated_text: but the lifespan of <s>Śākyamuni</s> can never be reckoned. // Suv_2.2 //

children.text: yāḥ kāścit pṛthivīḥ santi yāvantaḥ paramāṇavaḥ /
children.translated_text: However many earths there are, however many atoms [they contain] —

children.text: śakyaṃ gaṇayituṃ sarvā na tu cāyurjinasya vai // Suv_2.3 //
children.translated_text: all those could be counted, but not the lifespan of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror). // Suv_2.3 //
If someone were to wish to measure space by some [means],

children.text: na tu śākyamunerāyuḥ śakyaṃ gaṇayituṃ kvacit // Suv_2.4 //
children.translated_text: yet the lifespan of <s>Śākyamuni</s> can never be reckoned. // Suv_2.4 //
Even if such <s>kalpas</s> and hundreds of tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s> were spoken of,

children.text: eṣa tiṣṭhecca saṃbuddhaḥ saṃkhyāto na hi labhyate // Suv_2.5 //
children.translated_text: this Perfectly Awakened One endures — he cannot be reckoned by number. // Suv_2.5 //

children.text: yasmād dve kāraṇe tasya tathaiva dvau ca pratyayau /
children.translated_text: Since there are two causes and likewise two conditions for him:

children.text: virataḥ parahiṃsāyā bahu dattaṃ ca bhojanam // Suv_2.6 //
children.translated_text: he abstained from harming others, and gave food abundantly. // Suv_2.6 //
Since the measure of the lifespan of that great being cannot be obtained,

children.text: ityuktāni ca kalpāni saṃkhyāyāṃ na tathaiva ca // Suv_2.7 //
children.translated_text: the <s>kalpas</s> that have been spoken of likewise cannot be numbered. // Suv_2.7 //

children.text: tasmānna saṃśayo bho hi mā kiñcit kuru saṃśayam /
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no doubt, O noble one — do not entertain any doubt!
No number can be found for the limit of the <s>Jina</s>'s (Conqueror's) lifespan. // Suv_2.8 //

body.text: atha khalu tasminsamaye tatra parṣadyācāryavyākaraṇaprāptaḥ kauṇḍinyo nāma brāhmaṇo 'nekairbrāhmaṇasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhagavataḥ pūjākarma kṛtvā tathāgatasya mahāparinirvāṇaśabdaṃ śrutvā sahasotthāya bhagavataścaraṇayornipatya bhagavantamevamāha / sacetkila bhagavansarvasattvānukampako mahākāruṇiko hitaiṣī sarvasattvānāṃ mātāpitṛbhūto 'samasamabhūtaścandrabhūta ālokakaro mahāprajñājñānasūryasamudgataḥ / yadi tvaṃ sarvasattvān rāhulaṃ svaṃ saṃpaśyasi mahyamekaṃ varaṃ dehi / bhagavāṃstūṣṇīmbhūto 'bhūt /
body.translated_text: Now at that time, in that assembly, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, who had received the teacher's prediction, together with many thousands of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having performed worship of the Blessed One and having heard the words of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, suddenly rose up, fell at the feet of the Blessed One, and spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'If indeed, O Blessed One, you are compassionate toward all beings, greatly merciful, desirous of welfare, like a mother and father to all beings, incomparably equal, like the moon, a maker of light, arisen as a sun of great wisdom and knowledge — if you regard all beings as your own <s>Rāhula</s>, then grant me one boon!' The Blessed One remained silent.

body.text: atha buddhānubhāvena tasyāṃ parṣadi sarvasattvapriyadarśano nāma litsavikumāraḥ / tasya pratibhānamutpannam / sa ācāryavyākaraṇaprāptaṃ kauṇḍinyaṃ brāhmaṇamevamāha / kiṃ nu tvaṃ mahābrāhmaṇa bhagavantamekaṃ varaṃ yācase / ahaṃ te varaṃ dadāmi / brāhmaṇa āha / ahamasmiṃllitsavikumāra
body.translated_text: Then, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, in that assembly, a <s>Licchavi</s> prince named <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s> had an inspiration arise in him. He spoke thus to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> who had received the teacher's prediction: 'Why do you, O great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, request one boon from the Blessed One? I shall grant you the boon!' The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'I, O <s>Licchavi</s> prince —'

body.text: bhagavataḥ pūjopasthānāya bhagavataḥ sarṣapaphalamātraṃ dhātumicchāmi nikṣepituṃ cūrṇaṃ dhātumabhiprayojanāyainaṃ sarṣapaphalamātraṃ dhātumabhipūjayitvā tridaśādhipatyaṃ labhyata ityevaṃ śrūūyate / śṛṇu tvaṃ litsavikumāra suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtraṃ durvijñeyaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ tādṛśairlakṣaṇaguṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ kila suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtraṃ bhāvayiṣyati / evaṃ bho litsavikumāra durvijñeyaṃ duranubodhaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtram / asmākameva pratyantadvīpikānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sarṣapaphalamātraṃ dhātuṃ karaṇḍake nikṣipya dhāraṇamucitam / ahaṃ te varaṃ yāce yena sattvāḥ kṣiprameva tridaśādhipatyaṃ pratilambhino bhaviṣyanti / tvaṃ kila bho litsavikumāra sarṣapaphalamātraṃ dhātuṃ tathāgatasya yācitum / dhātuṃ ratnakaraṇḍake nikṣipya dhāraṇāt sarvasattvānāṃ tridaśādhipatyeśvaralābha itīcchase / evaṃ mayā ca litsavikumāra iṣṭaṃ varam /
body.translated_text: '— wish to deposit for the worship and service of the Blessed One a mustard-seed-sized relic of the Blessed One, a powdered relic, for the purpose of [venerating] it. It is heard that by worshipping a mustard-seed-sized relic, one obtains lordship over the thirty [gods]. Listen, O <s>Licchavi</s> prince: the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama Sūtra</s> is difficult to comprehend for all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; endowed with such marks and qualities, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama Sūtra</s> shall be cultivated. Thus, O <s>Licchavi</s> prince, difficult to comprehend and difficult to understand is the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama Sūtra</s>. For us <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of the outlying islands, it is fitting to deposit a mustard-seed-sized relic in a casket and preserve it. I ask you for the boon by which beings shall quickly attain lordship over the thirty [gods]. You, O <s>Licchavi</s> prince, have [come to] request a mustard-seed-sized relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. By depositing the relic in a jeweled casket and preserving it, you wish for all beings to attain the lordship of sovereignty over the thirty [gods]. Thus is the boon desired by me also, O <s>Licchavi</s> prince.'

body.text: atha sarvasattvapriyadarśano nāma litsavikumāra ācāryavyākaraṇaprāptaṃ kauṇḍinyabrāhmaṇaṃ gāthābhirabhyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Licchavi</s> prince named <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s> addressed the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, who had received the teacher's prediction, in verses:

children.text: yadā strotaḥsu gaṅgāyā roheyuḥ kumudāni ca /
children.translated_text: When in the currents of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, night-lotuses would grow,

children.text: raktāḥ kākā bhaviṣyanti śaṅkhavarṇāśca kokilāḥ // Suv_2.9 //
children.translated_text: and crows would become red, and cuckoos conch-white — // Suv_2.9 //
when the rose-apple tree would yield palm fruits, and the date-palm mango blossoms,

children.text: tadā sarṣapamātraṃ ca vyaktaṃ dhāturbhaviṣyati // Suv_2.10 //
children.translated_text: then indeed a mustard-seed-sized relic would appear! // Suv_2.10 //
When one could be well-wrapped in cloaks made from the hairs of tortoises,
removing the cold in winter — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.11 //
When from the feet of mosquitoes a watchtower-support could be made,

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ cāpyaprakampi ca tadā dhāturbhaviṣyati // Suv_2.12 //
children.translated_text: firm and unshakeable — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.12 //

children.text: yadā tīkṣṇā mahāntaśca dantā jāyanti pāṇḍurāḥ /
children.translated_text: When sharp, large, and white teeth would grow

children.text: jalaukānāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ tadā dhāturbhaviṣyati // Suv_2.13 //
children.translated_text: for all leeches — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.13 //
When from a hare's horn a sturdy ladder could be made
for the purpose of ascending to heaven — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.14 //

children.text: tāṃ niśreṇīṃ yadāruhya candraṃ bhakṣati mūṣikaḥ /
children.translated_text: When, climbing that ladder, a mouse would devour the moon

children.text: rāhuṃ ca paridhāveta tadā dhāturbhaviṣyati // Suv_2.15 //
children.translated_text: and chase <s>Rāhu</s> — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.15 //
When flies, having drunk a pot of liquor, wandering through the village,
would arrange lodging in a house — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.16 //
When a donkey endowed with <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips would be happy,
skilled in dancing and singing — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.17 //
When owls and crows, having come together, would delight in each other's company
with mutual affection — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.18 //

children.text: yadā palāśapatrāṇāṃ chatraṃ hi vipulaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: When from <s>palāśa</s> leaves a vast parasol could be made
for protection against the rains — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.19 //
When sea-going ships, with their mechanisms and banners,
would climb onto dry land and travel — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.20 //
When owls would carry Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>
in their beaks and fly away — then there would be a relic! // Suv_2.21 //

body.text: etāśca gāthāḥ śrutvācāryavyākaraṇaprāptaḥ kauṇḍinyo brāhmaṇaḥ sarvalokapriyadarśanaṃ litsavikumāraṃ gāthābhiḥ pratyabhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Having heard these verses, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, who had received the teacher's prediction, replied to the <s>Licchavi</s> prince <s>Sarvalokapriyadarśana</s> in verses:

children.translated_text: Excellent, excellent, O foremost of princes, O son of the <s>Jina</s>, of great speech!
A hero skilled in expedient means, who has attained the supreme prediction! // Suv_2.22 //
O prince, hear from me about the Protector, the Lord of the World —
the inconceivable greatness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in due order. // Suv_2.23 //
Inconceivable is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and incomparable are the <s>Tathāgatas</s>;

children.text: sarvabuddhāḥ śivā nityaṃ sarvabuddhāḥ samācarāḥ // Suv_2.24 //
children.translated_text: all <s>Buddhas</s> are eternally auspicious, all <s>Buddhas</s> are of equal conduct. // Suv_2.24 //
All <s>Buddhas</s> are of equal complexion — this is the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things) among <s>Buddhas</s>;
the Blessed One is not fabricated, nor is the <s>Tathāgata</s> produced. // Suv_2.25 //
Having a body of adamantine constitution, he displays an emanation body (<s>nirmitakāya</s>);

children.text: nāpi sarṣapamātraṃ ca dhāturnāma maharṣiṇām // Suv_2.26 //
children.translated_text: there is not even a mustard-seed-sized thing called a relic of the great sages. // Suv_2.26 //
In a body without bones or blood, how could there be a relic?
The depositing of relics is an expedient means (<s>upāya</s>), for the benefit of beings. // Suv_2.27 //
For the Perfectly Awakened One is the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body); the <s>Tathāgata</s> is the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (truth-realm).
Such is the body of the Blessed One; such is the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. // Suv_2.28 //
Having heard and known this, the boon was requested by me
for the purpose of the prediction of the truth; the request for the boon was made of the Sage. // Suv_2.29 //

body.text: atha khalu dvātriṃśaddevaputrasahasrāṇi tathāgatasya yaṃ gambhīramāyuḥpramāṇanirdeśaṃ śrutvā sarvairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittānyutpāditāni te prahṛṣṭamanaḥsaṃkalpā ekasvaranirghoṣeṇa gāthāmabhāṣan /
body.translated_text: Then thirty-two thousand sons of the gods (<s>devaputra</s>), having heard this profound teaching on the measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan, all generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>). With joyful minds and resolve, they spoke this verse in a single harmonious voice:

children.text: na buddhaḥ parinirvāti na dharma parihīyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> does not pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, nor does the <s>Dharma</s> diminish;
he displays <s>parinirvāṇa</s> for the ripening of beings. // Suv_2.30 //
Inconceivable is the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>; the <s>Tathāgata</s> has an eternal body.
He teaches various manifestations for the benefit of beings. // Suv_2.31 //

body.text: atha khalu ruciraketurbodhisattvasteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ tayośca dvayoḥ satpuruṣayorantikādbhagavataḥ śākyamunerāyuḥpramāṇanirdeśaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaścodāreṇa prītiprāmodyena sphuṭo 'bhūt / asmiṃstathāgatāyuḥpramāṇanirdeśe nirdiśyamāne 'prameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / te ca tathāgatā antaritā iti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ruciraketu</s>, having heard from those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, and from those two good men, the teaching on the measure of the lifespan of the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>, was satisfied, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness, and was suffused with a noble joy and delight. When this teaching on the measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan was being delivered, immeasurable and innumerable beings generated the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>). And those <s>Tathāgatas</s> disappeared.

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsoottamasūtrendrarāje tathāgatāyuḥpramāṇa nirdeśaparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the second chapter, the Chapter on the Teaching of the Measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Lifespan (<s>Tathāgatāyuḥpramāṇanirdeśaparivarta</s>), in the supreme king of <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Svapnaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Dream Chapter (<s>Svapnaparivarta</s>) //

body.text: atha khalu ruciraketurnāma bodhisattvaḥ svuptaḥ svapnāntaragataḥ suvarṇāṃ suvarṇamayīṃ bherīmadrākṣīt / samantādavabhāsamānāṃ tadyathāpi nāma sūryamaṇḍalaṃ sarvāsu dikṣvaprameyānasaṃkhyeyānbuddhānadrākṣīdratnavṛkṣamūle siṃhāsane vaiḍūryamaye pratiniṣaṇṇānanekaśatasahasrikāyāṃ pariṣadāyāṃ parivṛtāyāṃ puraskṛtāyāṃ dharmadeśayamānān / tatra ca brāhmaṇarūpeṇa puruṣamadrākṣīt tāṃ bherīṃ parāhantam / tatra bherīśabdādimāmevaṃrūpāṃ gāthāṃ niścaramāṇāmaśrauṣīt /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Ruciraketu</s>, having fallen asleep and entered into a dream, beheld a golden drum made of gold, shining forth in all directions like the orb of the sun. In all directions he saw immeasurable and innumerable <s>Buddhas</s> seated upon lion-thrones of beryl (<s>vaiḍūrya</s>) at the bases of jewel-trees, surrounded and honored by assemblies of many hundreds of thousands, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. And there he saw a man in the form of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> striking that drum. And from the sound of that drum, he heard verses of the following nature issuing forth:

body.text: atha khalu ruciraketurbodhisattvaḥ prativibuddhaḥ samanantaraṃ tāṃ dharmadeśanāgāthāmanusmarati sma / anusmaramāṇastasyā rātryā atyayena rājagṛhānmahānagarānniṣkramyānekaiḥ prāṇisahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ yena gṛdhrakūṭaḥ parvatarājo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtyaikānte nyaṣīdat /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ruciraketu</s>, having awakened, immediately recalled those verses of <s>Dharma</s> teaching. Recollecting them, when that night had passed, he departed from the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> together with many thousands of living beings, and approached the king of mountains, <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), where the Blessed One was. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and sat down to one side.

body.text: atha khalu ruciraketurbodhisattvo yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya yāścaiva tāḥ svapnāntare dundubhiśabdena deśanāgāthāḥ śrutāstā uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ruciraketu</s>, joining his palms in the direction of the Blessed One, recited the teaching-verses that he had heard through the sound of the drum within the dream:

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje svapnaparivarto nāma tṛtīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the third chapter, the Dream Chapter (<s>Svapnaparivarta</s>), in the supreme king of <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Deśanāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Confession Chapter (<s>Deśanāparivarta</s>) //

children.translated_text: During a single night, without drowsiness, within a dream by me,
a beautiful drum was seen, with golden radiance on all sides. // Suv_4.1 //
Blazing like the sun, illuminating all around,

children.text: prabhāsitā daśa diśo dṛṣṭā buddhāḥ samantataḥ // Suv_4.2 //
children.translated_text: the ten directions were illumined; <s>Buddhas</s> were seen everywhere. // Suv_4.2 //
Seated at jewel-trees, upon radiant beryl [thrones],
illuminated, with assemblies of many hundreds of thousands — // Suv_4.3 //
a drum was seen being struck by one in the form of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;
and as it was being beaten by him, these verses were heard: // Suv_4.4 //
By the supreme golden-radiance drum, may sufferings be pacified in the trichiliocosm!

children.text: apāyaduḥkhā yamalokaduḥkhā dāridraduḥkhāni tathaiva loke // Suv_4.5 //
children.translated_text: The sufferings of the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>), the sufferings of <s>Yama</s>'s world, and likewise the sufferings of poverty in the world! // Suv_4.5 //

children.text: anena co dundubhiśabdanādinā śāmyantu sarvavyasanāni loke /
children.translated_text: By this sound of the drum and so forth, may all calamities in the world be pacified!

children.text: samantasattvā hṛdayāhatā tathā tathābhayā śāntabhayā munīndra // Suv_4.6 //
children.translated_text: May all beings whose hearts are afflicted, O Lord of Sages (<s>Munīndra</s>), be likewise free from fear, their fears pacified! // Suv_4.6 //
Just as the great Lord of Sages, endowed with all noble qualities, omniscient regarding <s>saṃsāra</s> —

children.text: tathaiva bhontu guṇasāgarāḥ prajāḥ samādhibodhyaṅgaguṇairupetāḥ // Suv_4.7 //
children.translated_text: so too may beings become oceans of virtues, endowed with the qualities of <s>samādhi</s> and the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>)! // Suv_4.7 //

children.text: anena co dundubhighoṣanādinā bhavantu brahmasvara sarvasattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: By this reverberating sound of the drum and so forth, may all beings become <s>Brahmā</s>-voiced!
May they touch the excellent supreme awakening of Buddhahood, and set in motion the auspicious wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>! // Suv_4.8 //

children.text: tiṣṭhantu kalpāni acintiyāni deśentu dharmaṃ jagato hitāya /
children.translated_text: May they remain for inconceivable <s>kalpas</s>, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of the world!

children.text: hanantu kleśānvidhamantu duḥkhāṃ śamentu rāgaṃ tatha doṣamoham // Suv_4.9 //
children.translated_text: May they destroy the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), dispel suffering, and pacify passion, hatred, and delusion! // Suv_4.9 //
Those beings who dwell in the realms of woe (<s>apāya</s>), their bodies ablaze with burning fire —

children.text: śṛṇvantu te dundubhisaṃpravāditāṃ namo 'stu buddhāya vaco labhantu // Suv_4.10 //
children.translated_text: may they hear the drum being sounded! Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>! May they obtain [these] words! // Suv_4.10 //

children.text: jātismarāḥ sattva bhavantu sarve jātīśatā jātisahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: May all beings become rememberers of past lives — for hundreds, thousands, and tens of millions of births;

children.text: anusmarantaḥ satataṃ munīndraṃ śṛṇvantu teṣāṃ vacanaṃ hyudāram // Suv_4.11 //
children.translated_text: constantly recollecting the Lord of Sages, may they hear their noble words! // Suv_4.11 //

children.text: anena co dundibhi ghoṣanādinā labhantu buddhehi sadā samāgamam /
children.translated_text: By this reverberating sound of the drum and so forth, may they always obtain meetings with the <s>Buddhas</s>!

children.text: vivarjayantū khalu pāpakarma carantu kuśalāni śubhakriyāṇi // Suv_4.12 //
children.translated_text: May they abandon evil deeds and practice wholesome, meritorious actions! // Suv_4.12 //
For all beings, both human and <s>asura</s>, may they beseech [the <s>Buddhas</s>] with the prayer for this teaching!

children.text: anena co dundubhighoṣanādinā tatsarvi teṣāṃ paripūrayeyam // Suv_4.13 //
children.translated_text: By this reverberating sound of the drum and so forth, may I fulfill all of that for them! // Suv_4.13 //
Those beings reborn in the terrible hells, their bodies ablaze with burning fire —

children.text: nistīrṇaśokāśca paribhramanti nirvāpaṇaṃ bheṣyati teṣu cāmunā // Suv_4.14 //
children.translated_text: freed from grief, they shall wander [freely]; and by this [drum sound], cooling relief shall come to them! // Suv_4.14 //

children.text: ye duḥkhasattvāḥ sudāruṇārśca ghorā narakeṣu preteṣu manuṣyaloke /
children.translated_text: Those suffering beings who are terribly afflicted, in hells, among hungry ghosts, and in the human world —

children.text: anena ca dundubhighoṣanādinā sarve ca teṣāṃ praśamantu duḥkhāḥ // Suv_4.15 //
children.translated_text: by this sound of the drum-voice (<s>dundubhi-ghoṣa</s>) and the like, may all their sufferings be pacified! // Suv_4.15 //
For those who have no rescuer, no protector, no refuge —

children.text: trātā teṣāṃ bhaveyaṃ ca śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇottamaḥ // Suv_4.16 //
children.translated_text: may I become their savior, their refuge, their supreme shelter! // Suv_4.16 //
May the <s>Buddhas</s>, with minds of compassion and mercy, attend to me;
may they accept my transgressions — [the <s>Buddhas</s>] established in the ten directions! // Suv_4.17 //

children.text: yacca me pāpakaṃ karma kṛtapūrvaṃ sudāruṇam /
children.translated_text: Whatever terribly evil <s>karma</s> was formerly committed by me —
I shall confess all of it, standing before the Ten-Powered Ones (<s>Daśabala</s>). // Suv_4.18 //
Disrespecting my mother and father, not knowing the <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: kuśalaṃ cāprajānantā yattu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // Suv_4.19 //
children.translated_text: not knowing what is wholesome — whatever sin was committed by me; // Suv_4.19 //
intoxicated by the pride of wealth, by the pride of family and beauty,

children.text: tāruṇyamadamattena yattu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // Suv_4.20 //
children.translated_text: intoxicated by the pride of youth — whatever sin was committed by me; // Suv_4.20 //
by evil thoughts, evil speech, and evil deeds as well,

children.text: anādīnavadṛṣṭena yattu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // Suv_4.21 //
children.translated_text: by one who did not see the danger — whatever sin was committed by me; // Suv_4.21 //
through the conduct of a foolish mind, with consciousness enveloped by ignorance,
under the influence of evil companions, with a mind agitated by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); // Suv_4.22 //
through sport and amusement, through grief and disease,

children.text: atṛptadhanadoṣeṇa yattu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // Suv_4.23 //
children.translated_text: through the fault of insatiable greed — whatever sin was committed by me; // Suv_4.23 //
through association with ignoble people, through the cause of envy and jealousy,

children.text: śāṭhyadāridradoṣeṇa yattu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // Suv_4.24 //
children.translated_text: through the faults of deceit and poverty — whatever sin was committed by me; // Suv_4.24 //
in this time of the coming of misfortune, through fear of [losing] pleasures,

children.text: anaiśvaryagatenāpi yattu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // Suv_4.25 //
children.translated_text: and even in a state of powerlessness — whatever sin was committed by me; // Suv_4.25 //
under the sway of a fickle mind, under the sway of desire and anger,

children.text: kṣuptipāsārditenāpi yattu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā // Suv_4.26 //
children.translated_text: and even when tormented by hunger and thirst — whatever sin was committed by me; // Suv_4.26 //
for the sake of drink, for the sake of food, for the sake of clothing, for the sake of desiring women,
through the burning of various <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — whatever sin was committed by me; // Suv_4.27 //
sin of body, speech, and mind, and that practiced in the three realms (<s>tridhātu</s>) —
all that which was committed in such forms, I confess all of it. // Suv_4.28 //
Whatever disrespect may have been shown toward the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: agauravaṃ kṛtaṃ syāddhi tatsarvaṃ deśayāmyaham // Suv_4.29 //
children.translated_text: and likewise toward the <s>Śrāvakas</s> — all of that I confess. // Suv_4.29 //
Whatever disrespect may have been shown toward the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>

children.text: agauravaṃ kṛtaṃ syāddhi tatsarvaṃ deśayāmyaham // Suv_4.30 //
children.translated_text: or toward the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — all of that I confess. // Suv_4.30 //
If the true <s>Dharma</s> has been rejected by me, not knowing, at all times,
and disrespect toward mother and father — all of that I confess. // Suv_4.31 //
Through foolishness, through childishness, with mind covered by pride and arrogance,
through passion, hatred, and delusion — all of that I confess. // Suv_4.32 //
Having worshipped the Ten-Powered <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) in the ten directions of the world,
I shall lift up beings from all suffering in the ten directions. // Suv_4.33 //
I shall establish inconceivable beings upon the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages);

children.text: daśabhūmau hi sthitvā ca sarve bhontu tathāgatāḥ // Suv_4.34 //
children.translated_text: and having stood upon the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, may all become <s>Tathāgatas</s>! // Suv_4.34 //
For the sake of each single being, I would practice for tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: yāvacchakyaṃ hi tatsarvaṃ mokṣituṃ duḥkhasāgarāt // Suv_4.35 //
children.translated_text: until it is possible to liberate all of them from the ocean of suffering. // Suv_4.35 //
To those beings I would teach this profound teaching,
called the Most Excellent Golden Light (<s>Suvarṇaprabhottamā</s>), which causes the destruction of all <s>karma</s>. // Suv_4.36 //
The terribly evil <s>karma</s> committed over thousands of <s>kalpas</s> —

children.text: ekavelaṃ prakāśantu sarve vrajantu saṃkṣayam // Suv_4.37 //
children.translated_text: may it be illuminated all at once; may it all come to extinction! // Suv_4.37 //
I shall teach this unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>, the Golden Light (<s>Suvarṇaprabhā</s>);

children.text: ye śṛṇvanti śubhāṃ teṣāṃ saṃyāntu pāpasaṃkṣayam // Suv_4.38 //
children.translated_text: may those who hear this auspicious [teaching] have all their sins come to extinction! // Suv_4.38 //
I shall stand upon the ten <s>bhūmis</s>, [immersed in] those ten supreme jewel-oceans,
illuminating with the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, and shall cross [beings] over the ocean of existence. // Suv_4.39 //
That flood of the ocean of <s>Buddhas</s>, the profound ocean of qualities —
with the inconceivable qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, I shall fulfill omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>). // Suv_4.40 //
With hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhis</s> and inconceivable <s>dhāraṇīs</s>,
with the faculties, powers, and limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>), may I become the supreme Ten-Powered One. // Suv_4.41 //
Look upon me, O <s>Buddha</s>, with attentive mind;

children.text: atyayaṃ pratigṛhṇātu vimocayatu māṃ bhayāt // Suv_4.42 //
children.translated_text: accept my transgression and liberate me from fear! // Suv_4.42 //

children.text: yattu pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā kalpaśateṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Whatever sin was formerly committed by me over hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> —
because of that, I am grief-stricken, wretched, and tormented by craving. // Suv_4.43 //
I, the evil-doer, am ever fearful, with a dejected mind;

children.text: yatra yatra cariṣyāmi na cāsti maṅgalaṃ kvacit // Suv_4.44 //
children.translated_text: wherever I shall go, there is no auspiciousness anywhere. // Suv_4.44 //
All the compassionate <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Jinas</s> who remove the fear of beings —

children.text: atyayaṃ pratigṛhṇantu mocayantu ca māṃ bhayāt // Suv_4.45 //
children.translated_text: may they accept my transgression and free me from fear! // Suv_4.45 //
May the <s>Tathāgatas</s> wash away the fruit of my afflictions and <s>karma</s>;

children.text: snāpayantu ca māṃ buddhāḥ kāruṇyavimalodakaiḥ // Suv_4.46 //
children.translated_text: may the <s>Buddhas</s> bathe me with the stainless water of compassion! // Suv_4.46 //

children.text: sarvapāpaṃ deśayāmi yattu pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: I confess all the sin that was formerly committed by me;

children.text: yacca hyetarhi me pāpaṃ tatsarvaṃ deśayāmyaham // Suv_4.47 //
children.translated_text: and whatever sin is mine at present — all of that I confess. // Suv_4.47 //
Acknowledging in the future all evil deeds and all wrongdoing,

children.text: na cchādayāmi tatpāpaṃ yadbhavenmama duṣkṛtam // Suv_4.48 //
children.translated_text: I do not conceal that sin which constitutes my wrongdoing. // Suv_4.48 //

children.text: trividhaṃ kāyikaṃ karma vācikaṃ tu caturvidham /
children.translated_text: The threefold <s>karma</s> of the body, the fourfold of speech,

children.text: mānasaṃ triprakāraṃ ca tatsarvaṃ deśayāmyaham // Suv_4.49 //
children.translated_text: and the threefold of the mind — all of that I confess. // Suv_4.49 //

children.text: kāyakṛtaṃ ca vākkṛtaṃ manasā ca vicintitam /
children.translated_text: That which was done by the body, done by speech, and thought by the mind —

children.text: kṛtaṃ daśavidhaṃ karma tatsarvaṃ deśayāmyaham // Suv_4.50 //
children.translated_text: the tenfold <s>karma</s> that was done — all of that I confess. // Suv_4.50 //
Having abandoned the ten unwholesome [courses of action] and practiced the ten wholesome ones,

children.text: sthāsyāmi daśabhūmau ca paśye daśabalottamam // Suv_4.51 //
children.translated_text: I shall stand upon the ten <s>bhūmis</s> and behold the supreme Ten-Powered One. // Suv_4.51 //
Whatever evil <s>karma</s> of mine brings undesirable fruit —

children.text: tatsarvaṃ deśayiṣyāmi buddhānāṃ purataḥ sthitaḥ // Suv_4.52 //
children.translated_text: I shall confess all of that, standing before the <s>Buddhas</s>. // Suv_4.52 //
And whatever wholesome <s>karma</s> is performed in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and in other world-systems —
I rejoice (<s>anumodaye</s>) in all of that. // Suv_4.53 //
And whatever merit has been earned by me through body, speech, and mind —
by that root of merit, may I attain the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)! // Suv_4.54 //

children.text: bhavagatisaṃkaṭabālabuddhinā pāpaṃ hyapi yacca kṛtaṃ sudāruṇam /
children.translated_text: By one of foolish mind in the straits of existence (<s>bhavagati</s>), even the terribly evil sin that was committed —
standing before the Ten-Powered Ones, face to face, I confess all that sin. // Suv_4.55 //
That sin accumulated in the straits of birth, in the straits of the pursuit of various desires,
in the straits of the world, in the straits of existence, in the straits of afflictions committed by all the foolish — // Suv_4.56 //
in the straits of the intoxicated mind of fickleness and passion, in the straits of the approach of evil companions,
in the straits of <s>saṃsāra</s> and passion, in the straits of hatred, delusion, and darkness — // Suv_4.57 //
in the inexhaustible straits and the straits of time, in the straits of not earning merit —
standing before the incomparable <s>Jinas</s>, I confess all that sin. // Suv_4.58 //
I worship the <s>Buddhas</s>, who are like oceans of qualities, golden-hued, who illuminate the horizons;

children.text: teṣāṃ jinānāṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi mūrdhrā ca tānsarvajinānnamāmi // Suv_4.59 //
children.translated_text: I go for refuge to those <s>Jinas</s>, and with my head I bow to all the Conquerors. // Suv_4.59 //
Golden-hued, ---- resembling a mountain of gold, with limbs of pure, stainless beryl (<s>vaiḍūrya</s>) and beautiful eyes,
a <s>Buddha</s>-sun, the source of blazing glory, fame, and splendor, with the radiance of compassion, dispeller of the darkness of blindness — // Suv_4.60 //
supremely stainless, supremely beautiful, with brilliantly shining limbs, with body emerging from the Perfectly Awakened Sun, stainless as gold,
like blazing fire for those whose minds are burnt by the fire of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) — a cooling network of moonlight rays of the Sage. // Suv_4.61 //

body.text: dvātriṃśalakṣaṇadharaṃ lalitendriyāṅgam anuvyañjanaḥ suruciraṃ suvirājitāṅgam / śrīpuṇyatejajvalanākularaśmijālaṃ saṃtiṣṭhase tamasi sūrya iva triloke // Suv_4.62 //
body.translated_text: Bearer of the thirty-two marks, with graceful faculties and limbs, beautifully radiant with the secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjanas</s>), with brilliantly shining limbs, with a network of rays pervaded by the blazing splendor of glory and merit — you abide in the darkness [of the world] like a sun in the three realms. // Suv_4.62 //

children.translated_text: Of stainless, vast, and variegated color like beryl (<s>vaiḍūrya</s>), with limbs of copper-red, silver, crystal, and crimson,

children.text: nānāvicitrasamalaṅkṛtaraśmijālaṃ tvaṃ saṃvirocasi mahāmuni sūryakalpaḥ // Suv_4.63 //
children.translated_text: with a network of rays adorned with various adornments — you shine forth, O great Sage, like the sun. // Suv_4.63 //
In the midst of those fallen into the river of <s>saṃsāra</s>, amid the flood of calamity, in the grief-stricken waters with waves of death and old age,
in the ocean of suffering, with extremely turbulent and fierce currents — carry [us] across with the network of rays of the <s>Sugata</s>-sun! // Suv_4.64 //
I worship the <s>Buddhas</s> with bodies blazing like gold, with limbs radiant with golden hue,
oceans of knowledge, the essence of all three worlds, of variegated forms, with auspicious marks on their limbs. // Suv_4.65 //

children.text: yathā samudre jalamaprameyaṃ yathā mahī cāṇurajairanantā /
children.translated_text: Just as the water in the ocean is immeasurable, just as the earth is infinite with its particles of dust,
just as <s>Meru</s> with its stones is of incomparable [extent], just as space is boundless — // Suv_4.66 //

body.text: tathaiva buddhasya guṇā anantāḥ na śakya jñātuṃ khalu sarvasattvaiḥ /
body.translated_text: even so, the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> are infinite; they cannot be known by all beings;

body.text: anekakalpāni tu cintayante na śakya paryantaguṇāni jñātum // Suv_4.67 //
body.translated_text: even if they reflect for many <s>kalpas</s>, the limits of his qualities cannot be known. // Suv_4.67 //

children.text: mahī saśailā sagiriḥ sasāgarā gaṇaṃ tu kalpairapi śakya jānitum /
children.translated_text: The earth with its mountains, hills, and oceans — its measure could be known even in <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: jalaṃ ca vālāgramapi pramāṇaṃ na śakya buddhasya guṇāgrapāram // Suv_4.68 //
children.translated_text: and water, even to the tip of a hair, is measurable — but the summit of the <s>Buddha</s>'s qualities cannot [be reached]. // Suv_4.68 //

children.text: etādṛśī sattva bhavantu sarve guṇena varṇena yaśena koṭyā /
children.translated_text: May all beings become such — in quality, in splendor, in fame, by the tens of millions,
with bodies adorned with those beautiful marks and ornamented with the eighty secondary characteristics! // Suv_4.69 //

children.text: anena cāhaṃ kuśalena karmaṇā bhaveya buddho na cireṇa loke /
children.translated_text: By this wholesome deed, may I before long become a <s>Buddha</s> in the world;

children.text: deśeya dharmaṃ jagato hitāya moceya sattvānbahuduḥkhapīḍitān // Suv_4.70 //
children.translated_text: may I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the welfare of the world and liberate beings afflicted by many sufferings! // Suv_4.70 //

children.text: jayeya māraṃ sabalaṃ sasainyaṃ pravartayeyaṃ śubhadharmacakram /
children.translated_text: May I conquer <s>Māra</s> with his forces and armies; may I turn the auspicious Wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: tiṣṭheya kalpāni acintiyāni tarpeya sattvānamṛtena pāṇinā // Suv_4.71 //
children.translated_text: may I remain for inconceivable <s>kalpas</s> and satisfy beings with the nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) of my hand! // Suv_4.71 //

children.text: pūreya ṣaṭpāramitā anuttarā yathaiva pūrvaṃ jinapūrvakānām /
children.translated_text: May I fulfill the six supreme <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), as did the predecessors of former <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: haneya kleśānvidhameya duḥkhān śameya rāgāṃstatha dveṣamohān // Suv_4.72 //
children.translated_text: may I destroy the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), eliminate suffering, and pacify passion, hatred, and delusion! // Suv_4.72 //

children.text: jātismaro nitya bhaveya cāhaṃ jātiśatā jātisahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: May I always have remembrance of my [former] births — hundreds of births, tens of millions of births;

children.text: anusmareyaṃ satataṃ munīndraṃ śṛṇvīya teṣāṃ vacanaṃ hyudāram // Suv_4.73 //
children.translated_text: may I constantly recollect the lord of sages and hear their noble words! // Suv_4.73 //

children.text: anena cāhaṃ kuśalena karmaṇā labheya buddhehi sadā samāgamam /
children.translated_text: By this wholesome deed, may I always obtain the meeting with <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: vivarjayeyaṃ khalu pāpakarma careya puṇyāni śubhākarāṇi // Suv_4.74 //
children.translated_text: may I truly avoid evil <s>karma</s> and perform meritorious deeds that are sources of good! // Suv_4.74 //

children.text: sarvatra kṣetreṣu ca sarvaprāṇināṃ sarve ca pāpāḥ praśamantu loke /
children.translated_text: In all fields, may all sins of all beings be pacified in the world;

children.text: ye sattvā vikalendriya aṅgahīnāḥ te sarvi kuśalendriya bhontu sāṃpratam // Suv_4.75 //
children.translated_text: those beings whose faculties are deficient and whose limbs are impaired — may all of them now become complete in their wholesome faculties! // Suv_4.75 //
Those who are weak, emaciated, and of wasted body due to disease, who are without protection in the ten directions —

children.text: te sarvi mucyantu ca vyādhito laghu labhantu cārogyabalendriyāni // Suv_4.76 //
children.translated_text: may all of them be quickly freed from illness and obtain health, strength, and faculties! // Suv_4.76 //
Those seized [for execution] by evil kings and thieves, those condemned to death, those beset by various hundreds of calamities —

children.text: te sarvi sattvā vyasanāgataduḥkhitā hi mucyantu te bhayaśataiḥ paramaiḥ sughoraiḥ // Suv_4.77 //
children.translated_text: may all those beings, distressed and afflicted by calamity, be freed from hundreds of supremely terrible fears! // Suv_4.77 //

children.text: ye pīḍitā bandhanabaddhapīḍitā vividheṣu vyasaneṣu saṃsthitā hi /
children.translated_text: Those who are tormented, bound in chains and fetters, situated in various misfortunes,
agitated by thousands of many tribulations, beset by terrible fears and dreadful grief — // Suv_4.78 //

children.text: te sarve mucyantu ca bandhanebhyaḥ saṃtāḍitā mucyantu ca tāḍanebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: may all of them be freed from their bonds; may those who are beaten be freed from beatings;

children.text: vadhyāśca mucyantu jīvitebhyo vyasanāgatā nirbhayā bhontu sarve // Suv_4.79 //
children.translated_text: may those condemned to death be freed with their lives; may all who are beset by calamity become fearless! // Suv_4.79 //

body.text: ye sattva kṣuttarṣanipīḍitāśca labhantu te bhojanapānacitram /
body.translated_text: Those beings who are tormented by hunger and thirst — may they obtain various food and drink;

body.text: andhāśca paśyantu vicitrarūpān vadhirāśca śṛṇvantu manojñaghoṣān // Suv_4.80 //
body.translated_text: may the blind see variegated forms; may the deaf hear pleasing sounds! // Suv_4.80 //

children.text: nagnāśca vastrāṇi labhantu citrā daridrasattvāśca dhanāṃllabhantu /
children.translated_text: May the naked obtain beautiful garments; may the poor obtain wealth;

children.text: prabhūtadhanadhānyavicitraratnāḥ sarve ca sattvāḥ sukhino bhavantu // Suv_4.81 //
children.translated_text: abundant in wealth, grain, and various jewels — may all beings be happy! // Suv_4.81 //

children.text: mā kasyaciddhāvatu duḥkhavedanā sudarśanāḥ sattva bhavantu sarve /
children.translated_text: May the sensation of suffering not arise for anyone; may all beings be of beautiful appearance.
May they be handsome, pleasing, and gentle in form, and may they always be endowed with manifold accumulated happiness. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.82 //

children.text: manaḥśāntapaurāḥ susamṛddhapuṇyāḥ vīṇā mṛdaṅgā paṭahā sughoṣā /
children.translated_text: May the citizens have peaceful minds and abundant merit; may lutes, drums, and kettledrums resound sweetly;

children.text: utsāḥ sarāḥ puṣkariṇī taḍāgāḥ suvarṇapadmotpalapadminībhiḥ // Suv_4.83 //
children.translated_text: May springs, lakes, ponds, and reservoirs [be adorned] with golden lotuses, water-lilies, and lotus plants. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.83 //

children.text: sahacittamātreṇa tu teṣa bhontu annaṃ ca pānaṃ ca tathaiva vastram /
children.translated_text: May food, drink, and likewise clothing arise for them by the mere wish of the mind;
May wealth, gold, gems, pearls, ornaments, and jewels of gold and lapis lazuli of wondrous variety [appear for them]. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.84 //

children.text: mā duḥkhaśabdāḥ kvaci loki bhontu bhā caikasattvaḥ pratikūladarśī /
children.translated_text: May the word 'suffering' never be heard anywhere in the world; may not even a single being have an adverse appearance.

children.text: sarve ca te bhontu udāravarṇāḥ prabhākarā bhontu paraspareṇa // Suv_4.85 //
children.translated_text: May all of them be of noble complexion and may they be radiant toward one another. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.85 //

body.text: yā kāci saṃpatti manuṣyaloke sā teṣu bhotū manasopapattiḥ /
body.translated_text: Whatever prosperity exists in the human world—may it arise for them as a mental attainment;

body.text: sarvābhiprāyā sahacittamātraiḥ puṇyena phalena paripūrayantu // Suv_4.86 //
body.translated_text: May all their aspirations, by the mere wish of the mind, be fulfilled through the fruit of merit. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.86 //

children.text: gandhaṃ ca mālyaṃ ca vilepanaṃ ca dhūpaṃ ca cūrṇaṃ kusumaṃ ca pūrṇam /
children.translated_text: May fragrance, garlands, ointments, incense, powders, and abundant flowers

children.text: trikāle vṛkṣehi pravarṣayantu gṛhṇantu te sattva bhavantu tuṣṭāḥ // Suv_4.87 //
children.translated_text: Rain down from the trees three times a day; may those beings receive them and be contented. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.87 //

children.text: kurvantu pūjāṃ daśasū diśāsu acintiyāṃ sarvatathāgatānām /
children.translated_text: May they perform inconceivable worship of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions,
Together with the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and of the <s>Dharma</s> established in <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening). // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.88 //

children.text: nīcāṃ gatiṃ sarvi vivarjayantu tarantu aṣṭāṅgikavīcivṛttāḥ /
children.translated_text: May they all avoid the lower realms of existence; may they cross beyond, [freed from] the currents of the eight-fold [hells];

children.text: āsādayantu jinarājamūrti labhantu buddhehi sadā samāgamam // Suv_4.89 //
children.translated_text: May they reach the form of the King of <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors); may they always attain the meeting with <s>Buddhas</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.89 //

children.text: uccaiḥ kulīnā hi bhavantu nityaṃ prabhūtadhanadhānyasamṛddhakośāḥ /
children.translated_text: May they always be of high birth, with abundant wealth, grain, and prosperous treasuries;

children.text: rūpeṇa śauryeṇa yaśena kīrtyā samalaṅkṛtā bhontu anekakalpān // Suv_4.90 //
children.translated_text: May they be adorned with beauty, valor, fame, and glory for countless aeons. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.90 //

children.text: sarvā striyo nitya narā bhavantu śūrāśca vīrāśca vijñapaṇḍitāśca /
children.translated_text: May all women always become men—heroic, valiant, learned, and wise;

children.text: te sarvi bodhāya carantu nityaṃ carantu te pāramitāsu ṣaṭsu // Suv_4.91 //
children.translated_text: May they all always strive toward <s>Bodhi</s> and practice the six <s>Pāramitās</s> (Perfections). // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.91 //

body.text: paśyantu buddhān daśasū diśāsu ratnottamavṛkṣasukhopaviṣṭān /
body.translated_text: May they behold the <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions, seated happily beneath the most excellent jewel-trees,

body.text: vaiḍūryasiṃhāsani saṃniṣaṇṇān śṛṇvantu dharmāṃśca prakāśyamānān // Suv_4.92 //
body.translated_text: Seated upon lapis lazuli lion-thrones, and may they hear the <s>Dharma</s> being proclaimed. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.92 //

children.text: pāpāni karmāṇi mayā jitāni pūrvārjitā yadbhavasaṃkaṭeṣu /
children.translated_text: May the sinful deeds that I have conquered—those accumulated in former lives in the straits of existence—

children.text: ye pāpakarmābhiratā vahante te sarvi kṣīyantu ca nirviśeṣāḥ // Suv_4.93 //
children.translated_text: And all those who carry [the burden of] evil deeds—may they all be utterly exhausted without remainder. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.93 //
May all those beings standing in the bondage of existence, tightly bound by the fetters of <s>saṃsāra</s>—

children.text: prajñākarairbhāsita bhontu bandhanānmucyantu duḥkhairupajā bhavantu // Suv_4.94 //
children.translated_text: May they be illuminated by the rays of wisdom; may they be freed from their bonds and may suffering cease for them. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.94 //

children.text: ye cāpi sattvā iha jāmbudvīpe ye cāpi anyaṣu ca lokadhātuṣu /
children.translated_text: Whatever beings exist here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> or in other world-systems—
May they perform profound and marvelous merit; I rejoice in all that merit. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.95 //
By that very rejoicing in merit, accumulated through body, speech, and mind—

children.text: praṇidhānasiddhiḥ saphalā mayāstu spṛśeya bodhiṃ virajāmanuttarām // Suv_4.96 //
children.translated_text: May the fulfillment of [my] aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) be fruitful for me; may I touch the unsurpassed, stainless <s>Bodhi</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.96 //

children.text: yo vandate toṣyati daśabalān sadā ca prasannaśuddhāmalamānasena /
children.translated_text: Whoever venerates and pleases the Ten-powered Ones (<s>Daśabala</s>), always with a serene, pure, and stainless mind—

children.text: imāya pariṇāmanadeśanāya ṣaṣṭiṃ ca kalpān jahate apāyān // Suv_4.97 //
children.translated_text: Through this teaching of dedication (<s>pariṇāmana</s>), for sixty aeons they abandon the lower realms. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.97 //

body.text: etebhi ślokebhi ca varṇitebhiḥ puruṣāḥ striyo brahmaṇakṣatriyā ca /
body.translated_text: By these verses that have been recited—men, women, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and <s>Kṣatriyas</s>—

body.text: yastoṣyate muniṃ sa kṛtāñjalibhiḥ sthihitva sarvatra jātismaru śatajātiṣu // Suv_4.98 //
body.translated_text: Whoever pleases the Sage with joined palms, standing [in reverence], shall have memory of [past] births in a hundred births everywhere. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.98 //

children.translated_text: With all limbs and all senses beautiful, endowed with manifold and complete virtues,

children.text: narendrarājaiśca supūjitaḥ sadā etādṛśo bheṣyati tatra tatra // Suv_4.99 //
children.translated_text: Always well-worshipped by kings of men—such will one become, here and there. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.99 //

children.text: na tairekasya buddhasya cāntike kuśalaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: It is not in the presence of just one <s>Buddha</s> that [such] wholesome [deeds] have been performed,

children.text: na dvayorapi trayeṣu na pañcasu na daśasu // Suv_4.100 //
children.translated_text: Nor of two, nor of three, nor of five, nor of ten— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.100 //
But in the presence of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> have wholesome [deeds] been performed
By those into whose ears this teaching will enter. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 4.101 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje deśanāparivarto nāma caturthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, the Chapter on Teaching (<s>Deśanā-parivarta</s>), in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // kamalākarasarvatathāgatastavaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The Chapter of <s>Kamalākara</s>'s Praise of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstāṃ bodhisattvasamuccayāṃ kuladevatāmetadavocat / tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate kālena tena samayena rājā suvarṇabhujendro nāmāsīt / etena kamalākareṇa sarvatathāgatastavenātītānāgatapratyutpannān buddhān bhagavato 'bhyastāvīt //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed that assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the deity <s>Kuladevatā</s>: 'At that time, in that era, there was a king named <s>Suvarṇabhujendra</s>. With this <s>Kamalākara</s> praise of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, he praised the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present.'

children.text: ye jina pūrvaka ye ca bhavanti ye ca dhriyanti daśodiśi loke /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) of the past, those who will be, and those who abide in the ten directions of the world—

children.text: teṣa jināna karomi praṇāmaṃ taṃ jinasaṃghamahaṃ praśayiṣye // Suv_5.1 //
children.translated_text: To those <s>Jinas</s> I make my salutation; I bow to that assembly of the Conquerors. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.1 //
The tranquil, perfectly peaceful, pure Lord of Sages, whose body blazes with the radiance of golden hue,
The <s>Buddha</s> of beautiful voice [praised by] all gods and demons, whose thunderous sound is like the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.2 //
Whose hair is like great trees crowned with bees, dark-blue, beautifully curled, and lightning-like in radiance;
Whose teeth are white as conch-shell and frost, whose navel blazes with golden splendor. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.3 //
Whose eyes are blue, wide, and perfectly pure, shining like the radiance of fallen blue lotuses;
Whose tongue is broad and golden like a lotus, whose lotus-face shines with lotus-radiance. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.4 //
Whose facial arch is like a conch-shell or lotus-stem, of lapis lazuli hue turning to the right;
Whose body, fine as a waning crescent moon, is radiant like the shimmering glow of bees. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.5 //
With a nose delicate as a tip of gold, with nostrils full and upturned—
With the most excellent and distinguished beautiful nose, soft [is the body] of the <s>Jina</s> at all times. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.6 //
With body-hairs, each set evenly, with tips of fine hair turning to the right,
Blue-hued, with blazing coiled earrings, with a beautiful neck adorned by a blue-radiant diadem. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.7 //
With a body radiant like [newborn] gold, worshipped by all in the ten directions of the world,
Having pacified boundless suffering in the three worlds, having satisfied all beings with every happiness. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.8 //
In the hells, in the animal realms, in the realms of hungry ghosts, gods, demons, and humans—

children.text: teṣu ca sarvasukhārpitasattvaṃ sarvapraśānta apāyagatīṣu // Suv_5.9 //
children.translated_text: In all those [realms], one who has bestowed happiness upon beings, one who has fully pacified the lower destinies. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.9 //
Of complexion like gold, like refined gold in radiance, with a body blazing with the splendor of heated gold,
With a face serene as the spotless moon, with a blossoming, radiant, and stainless countenance. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.10 //
With a tender body, soft as young shoots, striding with the gait and power of a lion;
With hanging hands and arms extending [below the knees], like a <s>śāla</s> creeper swayed by the wind. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.11 //
Sending forth rays blazing with the splendor of the sky, like a thousand suns blazing together,
The Lord of Sages, with stainless and excellent limbs, illuminating all fields without limit. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.12 //
The net of moon, night-maker, and sun, in boundless hundreds of thousands of fields—

children.text: te 'pi ca niṣṭhita sarvamabhūṣi buddhaprabhāsavirocanatāyai // Suv_5.13 //
children.translated_text: All of those too are surpassed and rendered complete for the illumination of the <s>Buddha</s>'s radiance. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.13 //
The <s>Buddha</s>-sun, the lamp of the world, [surpassing] a hundred thousand <s>Buddha</s>-suns—
In boundless hundreds of thousands of fields, may beings behold the <s>Tathāgata</s>-sun! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.14 //
With a body accumulated from hundreds of thousands [of deeds of] merit, with limbs adorned with all virtues,
With arms like those of a noble bull-elephant, with stainless hands adorned with excellent marks. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.15 //

body.text: bhūmitalopamarajasamatulyaṃ sūkṣmarajopama ye gatabuddhāḥ //
body.translated_text: As numerous as dust-motes on the surface of the earth—[such are] the <s>Buddhas</s> who have gone, like subtle dust-motes;

body.text: sūkṣmarajopama ye ca bhavanti sūkṣmarajopama ye ca sthihanti // Suv_5.16 //
body.translated_text: Like subtle dust-motes are those who will be; like subtle dust-motes are those who [now] abide. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.16 //

children.text: teṣa jināna karomi praṇāmaṃ kāyatu vācamanena prasannaḥ /
children.translated_text: To those <s>Jinas</s> I make my salutation—with body, speech, and mind, serene,
With offerings of flowers and fragrant offerings, and with a beautiful mind [adorned by] a hundred praises. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.17 //

body.text: jihvaśatairapi buddhaguṇāni kalpasahasraśate na hi vaktum /
body.translated_text: Even with a hundred tongues, the virtues of the <s>Buddhas</s> cannot be spoken in a hundred thousand aeons;

body.text: ye guṇasādhunivṛtti jinānāṃ sā ca varāgravicitra anekaiḥ // Suv_5.18 //
body.translated_text: The virtues and noble conduct of the <s>Jinas</s>—they are the most excellent, marvelous, and manifold. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.18 //

children.text: ekajinasya guṇā na hi śakyā jihvaśatairapi bhāṣitu kaścit /
children.translated_text: The virtues of even a single <s>Jina</s> cannot be expressed by anyone, even with a hundred tongues;

children.text: kāmamaśakti hi sarvajinānāṃ ekaguṇasya hi vistara vaktum // Suv_5.19 //
children.translated_text: Even though one may desire [to do so], one is unable to describe in full even one virtue of all the <s>Jinas</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.19 //
The entire host of all divine families speaking together, all the waters in the highest existence—

children.text: keśagrahaṇena tu śakya pramātuṃ naiva ca ekaguṇā sugatānām // Suv_5.20 //
children.translated_text: Can be measured by grasping a tip of hair, but not even one virtue of the <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones). // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.20 //

children.text: varṇita saṃstuta me jinasarvaṃ kāyatu vāca prasannamanena /
children.translated_text: I have praised and extolled all the <s>Jinas</s>, with body, speech, and a serene mind;

children.text: yanmama sañcitapuṇyaphalāgraṃ tena ca sattva prabhotu jinatvam // Suv_5.21 //
children.translated_text: By the foremost fruit of whatever merit I have accumulated, may all beings attain the state of a <s>Jina</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.21 //

children.text: evaṃ stavitva narapati buddhaṃ evaṃ karoti nṛpaḥ praṇidhānam /
children.translated_text: Having thus praised the <s>Buddha</s>, that king made this aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>):

children.text: yatra ca kutraci mahya bhaveta jāti anāgatakalpamanantā // Suv_5.22 //
children.translated_text: 'Wherever and in whatever [realm] birth may arise for me in the boundless future aeons— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.22 //

children.text: īdṛśi bheri mi paśyami svapne īdṛśa deśana tatra śṛṇomi /
children.translated_text: May I behold such a drum in my dream, may I hear such a teaching there,

children.text: īdṛśa jīnastutikamalākara jātiṣu tatra labhe smaraṇatvam // Suv_5.23 //
children.translated_text: May I obtain such a praise of the <s>Jinas</s>—the <s>Kamalākara</s>—and remembrance in those births. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.23 //

body.text: buddhaguṇāni anantamatulyā ye 'pi ca durlabha kalpasahasraiḥ /
body.translated_text: The virtues of the <s>Buddhas</s> are boundless and incomparable, and difficult to obtain even in thousands of aeons;

body.text: amu śruṇeya ca svapnagato 'pi teṣu ca deśayi divasagato 'pi // Suv_5.24 //
body.translated_text: May I hear these even in a dream, and may I teach them even while awake. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.24 //

children.text: duḥkhasamudra vimocayi sattvā pūrayi ṣaḍabhi pi pāramitābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: May I deliver beings from the ocean of suffering; may I fulfill the six <s>Pāramitās</s>;

children.text: bodhimanuttara paśca labheyaṃ kṣetra bhaveta mamā asamarthyam // Suv_5.25 //
children.translated_text: May I afterward attain the unsurpassed <s>Bodhi</s>; may my field be one of incomparable [splendor]. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.25 //
By the fruit of the ripening of the offering of the drum, and by the cause of praising all the <s>Jinas</s>—

children.text: saṃmukha paśyami śākyamunīndraṃ vyākaraṇaṃ hyahu tatra labheyam // Suv_5.26 //
children.translated_text: May I behold <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Lord of Sages, face to face, and may I there obtain a prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) [of future Buddhahood]. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.26 //

children.text: ye ima dāraka dvau mama putrau kanakendra kanakaprabhāsvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: These two boys, my sons—<s>Kanakendra</s> and <s>Kanakaprabhāsvara</s>—

children.text: te ubhi dāraka tatra labheyaṃ bodhimanuttara vyākaraṇaṃ ca // Suv_5.27 //
children.translated_text: May I obtain those two boys [again] there, and [may they receive] the unsurpassed <s>Bodhi</s> and a prophecy [of Buddhahood]. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.27 //

children.text: ye 'pi ca sattva arakṣa atrāṇā śaraṇavihīna viyāsagatāśca /
children.translated_text: Whatever beings are unprotected, without refuge, deprived of shelter, and in distress—

children.text: teṣu bhaveya anāgata sarva trāṇaparāyaṇaśaraṇebhiśca // Suv_5.28 //
children.translated_text: May I become for all of them in the future a protector, a supreme refuge, and a shelter. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.28 //
The destroyer of the arising of suffering, and the source of all happiness—

children.text: kalpa anāgata bodhi careyaṃ yattaka pūrvakakoṭigatāśca // Suv_5.29 //
children.translated_text: May I practice [the path to] <s>Bodhi</s> through future aeons, for as many aeons as have passed before. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.29 //

body.text: svarṇaprabhottamadeśanatāya pāpasamudra śoṣatu mahyam /
body.translated_text: By the power of the teaching of the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, may the ocean of sin be dried up for me;

body.text: karmasamudra vikīryatu mahyaṃ kleśasamudra vicchidyatu mahyam // Suv_5.30 //
body.translated_text: May the ocean of <s>karma</s> be scattered for me; may the ocean of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) be severed for me. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.30 //

children.text: puṇyasamudra prapūryatu mahyaṃ jñānasamudra viśodhyatu mahyam /
children.translated_text: May the ocean of merit be filled for me; may the ocean of knowledge be purified for me;
By the power of stainless knowledge-radiance, may I become an ocean of all virtues. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.31 //
Filled with jewel-virtues of <s>Bodhi</s>, by the power of this teaching, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s>—

children.text: puṇyaprabhāsa bhaviṣyati mahyaṃ bodhiprabhāsa viśodhyatu mahyam // Suv_5.32 //
children.translated_text: May the radiance of merit arise for me; may the radiance of <s>Bodhi</s> be purified for me. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.32 //

children.text: kāyaprabhāsa bhaviṣyati mahyaṃ puṇyaprabhāsa virocanatā ca /
children.translated_text: May radiance of body arise for me, and the illumination of merit-radiance;

children.text: sarvatriloki viśiṣṭa bhaveyaṃ pūṇyabalena samanvita nityam // Suv_5.33 //
children.translated_text: May I become preeminent in all the three worlds, always endowed with the power of merit. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.33 //
May I lift [all] beings out of the ocean of suffering; may I become like an ocean of all happiness;
May I practice [the path to] <s>Bodhi</s> through future aeons, for as many aeons as have passed before. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.34 //
Whatever are the most excellent fields in the three worlds, with the infinite virtues of all the <s>Jinas</s>—
Such a field of infinite virtues shall all be mine in the future. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 5.35 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje kamalākarasarvatathāgatastavaparivarto nāma pañcamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, the <s>Kamalākara</s> Chapter of Praise of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // Śūnyatāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The Chapter on Emptiness (<s>Śūnyatā-parivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: In other inconceivable <s>sūtras</s>, the teachings on emptiness (<s>śūnya-dharma</s>) have been set forth at great length;
