children.text: tasmādime sūtravarottame vaḥ saṃkṣepato deśita śūnyadharmāḥ // Suv_6.1 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in this most excellent <s>sūtra</s>, the teachings on emptiness are set forth for you in brief. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 6.1 //

children.text: sattvo 'lpabuddhiravijānamāno na śakya jñātuṃ khalu sarvadharmā /
children.translated_text: A being of little understanding, not comprehending, is unable to know all <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: paśyeha sūtrendravarottamena saṃkṣepato deśita śūnyadharmāḥ // Suv_6.2 //
children.translated_text: Behold! By this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>dharmas</s> of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) have been taught in brief. // Suv_6.2 //
And through other skillful means and logical methods, for the purpose of arousing compassion toward beings,

children.text: prakāśitaṃ sūtravarendrametaṃ yathābhijānanti hi sarvasattvāḥ // Suv_6.3 //
children.translated_text: this supreme king of sūtras has been illuminated, so that all beings may understand. // Suv_6.3 //

children.text: ayaṃ ca kāyo yatha śūnyagrāmaḥ ṣaḍgrāma coropama indriyāṇi /
children.translated_text: This body is like an empty village; the six sense faculties (<s>indriyas</s>) are like thieves in the village;

children.text: tānyekagrāme nivasanti sarve na te vijānanti paraspareṇa // Suv_6.4 //
children.translated_text: they all dwell in one village, yet they do not know each other. // Suv_6.4 //
The eye-faculty (<s>cakṣur-indriya</s>) runs after visible forms; the ear-faculty (<s>śrotra-indriya</s>) [runs] in the investigation of sounds;

children.text: ghrāṇendriyaṃ gandhavicitrahāri jihvandriyaṃ nitya raseṣu dhāvati // Suv_6.5 //
children.translated_text: the nose-faculty (<s>ghrāṇa-indriya</s>) is seized by varied scents; the tongue-faculty (<s>jihva-indriya</s>) constantly runs after tastes. // Suv_6.5 //
The body-faculty (<s>kāya-indriya</s>) rushes toward contact; the mind-faculty (<s>mana-indriya</s>) [runs] in the investigation of <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: ṣaḍindriyāṇīti paraspareṇa svakaṃ svakaṃ viṣayamabhidhāvati // Suv_6.6 //
children.translated_text: thus the six faculties, each one separately, rush after its own object. // Suv_6.6 //

children.text: cittaṃ hi māyopama cañcalaṃ ca ṣaḍindriyaṃ viṣayavicāraṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The mind (<s>citta</s>) is like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>), fickle; the six faculties investigate their objects;

children.text: yathā naro dhāvati śūnyagrāme saṃgrāma caurebhi samāśritaśca // Suv_6.7 //
children.translated_text: just as a man runs in an empty village, taking refuge among thieves in a battle. // Suv_6.7 //

children.text: cittaṃ yathā ṣaḍviṣayāśritaṃ ca prajānate indriya gocaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The mind, relying on the six objects, knows the domain of the faculties —

children.text: rūpaṃ ca śabdaṃ ca tathaiva gandhaṃ rasaṃ ca sparśa tatha dharmagocaram // Suv_6.8 //
children.translated_text: form, sound, and likewise scent, taste, touch, and the domain of <s>dharmas</s>. // Suv_6.8 //

children.text: cittaṃ ca sarvatra ṣaḍindriyeṣu śakuniriva cañcalaṃ indriyasaṃpraviṣṭam /
children.translated_text: The mind, [roaming] everywhere among the six faculties, fickle like a bird, enters the faculties;

children.text: yatra yatrendriyasaṃśritaṃ ca na cendriyaṃ kurvatu jānamātmakam // Suv_6.9 //
children.translated_text: wherever it relies on a [particular] faculty — yet the faculty does not know itself. // Suv_6.9 //

children.text: kāyaśca niśceṣṭa nirvyāpāraṃ ca asārakaḥ pratyayasaṃbhavaśca /
children.translated_text: The body is inert, without activity, without essence, and arisen from conditions;
arisen from unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūta-vikalpa</s>), it is like an automaton (<s>yantra</s>) standing through [past] <s>karma</s> — an empty village. // Suv_6.10 //
Earth, water, fire, and wind — like thieves stationed in different parts within the village,

children.text: paraspareṇaiva sadā viruddhā yathaiva āśīviṣa ekaveśmani // Suv_6.11 //
children.translated_text: they are always mutually hostile, like poisonous serpents in one dwelling. // Suv_6.11 //

children.text: dhātūragāste ca caturvidhāni dve ūrdhvagāmī dvaya heṣṭagāmī /
children.translated_text: Those four element-serpents (<s>dhātu-uraga</s>): two go upward and two go downward;

children.text: dvayādvayaṃ diśi vidiśāsu sarvaṃ naśyanti tā dhātubhujaṅgamāni // Suv_6.12 //
children.translated_text: in pairs, in every direction and intermediate direction, those element-serpents perish. // Suv_6.12 //

children.text: kṣityuragaśca saliloragaśca imau ca heṣṭā kṣayatāṃ vrajete /
children.translated_text: The earth-serpent and the water-serpent — these two go downward and proceed to dissolution;

children.text: tejoragaścānilamārutoraga imau hi dve ūrdhvagatau nabho 'nte // Suv_6.13 //
children.translated_text: the fire-serpent and the wind-serpent — these two go upward, to the edge of space. // Suv_6.13 //

children.text: cittaṃ ca vijñānamadhyasthitaṃ ca gatvā yathā pūrvakṛtena karmāṇā /
children.translated_text: The mind (<s>citta</s>) and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), situated in the midst, go according to formerly performed <s>karma</s>;

children.text: deve manuṣyaeṣu ca triṣvapāyā yathākṛtaṃ pūrvabhave pravarttyā // Suv_6.14 //
children.translated_text: among gods, humans, and the three lower realms (<s>apāya</s>) — [rebirth occurs] as was done in former existences. // Suv_6.14 //
The body, reaching its end through phlegm (<s>śleṣman</s>), wind (<s>anila</s>), and bile (<s>pitta</s>), is filled with feces, urine, and filth;

children.text: nirābhirāmaḥ kṛmikṣudrapūrṇaḥ kṣiptaḥ śmaśāne yatha kāṣṭhabhūtaḥ // Suv_6.15 //
children.translated_text: unlovely, filled with worms and vermin — [when] cast upon the charnel ground, it becomes like a log of wood. // Suv_6.15 //

body.text: paśyāhi tvaṃ devata ebhi evaṃ katyatra sattvastatha pudgalo vā /
body.translated_text: See, O goddess, thus consider these: where is a being or a person in this?

body.text: śūnyā hi ete khalu sarvadharmā avidyataḥ pratyayasaṃbhavāśca // Suv_6.16 //
body.translated_text: For all these <s>dharmas</s> are indeed empty — arising from conditions out of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). // Suv_6.16 //

children.translated_text: These great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>) are all unreal, since the nature of the great elements is without [inherent] existence;

children.text: tasmācca bhūtā hi asaṃbhavāśca avidyamānā na kadāci vidyate // Suv_6.17 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the elements are non-arising — that which does not exist never comes into existence. // Suv_6.17 //
From ignorance, arisen through conditions, non-existent indeed — [these are] the words of ignorance;

children.text: tasmānmayā ukta avidya eṣā saṃskāravijñāna sanāmarūpam // Suv_6.18 //
children.translated_text: therefore it has been said by me: this is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), [followed by] formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), and name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>); // Suv_6.18 //

children.text: ṣaḍāyatanasparśa tathaiva vedanā tṛṣṇā upādāna tathā bhavaśca /
children.translated_text: the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>), contact (<s>sparśa</s>), and likewise feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), grasping (<s>upādāna</s>), and existence (<s>bhava</s>);

children.text: jātijarāmaraṇaśoka upadravāṇāṃ duḥkhāni saṃskāra acintiyāni // Suv_6.19 //
children.translated_text: birth (<s>jāti</s>), old age and death (<s>jarā-maraṇa</s>), grief, and calamities — inconceivable sufferings [arising from] formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>). // Suv_6.19 //

children.text: saṃsāracakre ca yathā sthitāni abhūta saṃbhūta asaṃbhavāśca /
children.translated_text: As they are established in the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> — unreal, arisen yet non-arising —

children.text: ayoniśaścittavicāraṇaṃ tathā dṛṣṭīgataṃ chetsyatha ātmanaiva // Suv_6.20 //
children.translated_text: through improper mental investigation (<s>ayoniśaś-citta-vicāraṇa</s>) and through wrong views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) — you shall cut [these] by yourselves. // Suv_6.20 //

children.text: jñānāsinā chindatha kleśajālaṃ skandhālayaṃ paśyatha śūnyabhūtam /
children.translated_text: Cut the net of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) with the sword of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>); see the abode of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) as empty in nature;

children.text: sparśetha taṃ bodhiguṇaṃ hyudāraṃ vivarta ca me amṛtapurasya dvāram // Suv_6.21 //
children.translated_text: touch that noble quality of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), and the door of the city of the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>) will open for me! // Suv_6.21 //

body.text: saṃdarśi taṃ amṛtapurasya bhājanaṃ pravekṣya taṃ amṛtapurālayaṃ śubham /
body.translated_text: I have shown the vessel of the city of the deathless; having entered that auspicious abode of the deathless city,

body.text: tarpiṣya ha amṛtatarasena ātmanāṃ parāhatā me varadharmabherīḥ // Suv_6.22 //
body.translated_text: I shall satisfy myself with the nectar-stream of the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>); the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-drum has been struck by me! // Suv_6.22 //

children.text: āpūrito me varadharmaśaṅkhaḥ prajvālitā me varadharma ulkā /
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>Dharma</s>-conch has been filled by me; the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-torch has been kindled by me;

children.text: suvarṣitaṃ me varadharmavarṣaṃ parājitā me parakleśaśatravaḥ // Suv_6.23 //
children.translated_text: the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-rain has been well-rained by me; the enemies [that are] the afflictions of others have been conquered by me! // Suv_6.23 //

children.text: ucchrepitaṃ me varadharmadhvajaṃ pratāritā me bhavasattvasamudrāḥ /
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>Dharma</s>-banner has been raised by me; the beings in the ocean of existence have been ferried across by me;

children.text: pidhitāni me 'pāyapathāni trīṇi kleśāgnidāhaṃ śamayitva prāṇinām // Suv_6.24 //
children.translated_text: the three paths of the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>) have been closed by me, having pacified the burning of the fire of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) for all beings. // Suv_6.24 //

children.text: yasmāddhi pūrvamahamanekakalpān acintiyā pūjitva nāyakā hi /
children.translated_text: Since in the past, for innumerable <s>kalpas</s>, I worshipped inconceivable guides (<s>nāyakas</s>),

children.text: caritva bodhāya dṛḍhavratena saddharmakāyaṃ pariveṣamāṇaḥ // Suv_6.25 //
children.translated_text: and practiced with firm vows for awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), distributing the body of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma-kāya</s>); // Suv_6.25 //

children.text: hastau ca pādau ca parityajitvā dhanaṃ hiraṇyaṃ maṇimuktabhūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: having relinquished hands and feet, wealth, gold, gems, pearls, and ornaments,
eyes, head, dear wife and children, gold, beryl, and various jewels; // Suv_6.26 //
having cut all the trees and forest-lords in the trichiliocosm,

children.text: sarvaṃ ca cūrṇayitvā tat kuryāt sūkṣmarajopamam // Suv_6.27 //
children.translated_text: and having ground all of that, making it like fine dust — // Suv_6.27 //
having made a heap of dust as vast as the extent of space,
or [atoms] equal to the dust-particles of the earth divided into innumerable parts — // Suv_6.28 //

children.text: sarvasattvā aneke hi jñānavata tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: all the many beings, even those endowed with knowledge,

children.text: sarvaṃ gaṇayituṃ śakyaṃ na tu jñātaṃ jinasya ca // Suv_6.29 //
children.translated_text: could count all [those atoms], but not the knowledge of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror). // Suv_6.29 //
Even the knowledge that arises in a single moment for the Great Sage

children.text: anekakalpakoṭīṣu na śakyaṃ gaṇayituṃ kvacit // Suv_6.30 //
children.translated_text: cannot be counted even in many tens of millions of <s>kalpas</s>. // Suv_6.30 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje śūnyatāparivarto nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixth chapter, the <s>Śūnyatā</s> (Emptiness) Chapter, in the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Caturmahārājaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Caturmahārāja</s> (Four Great Kings) Chapter //

body.text: atha khalu vaiśravaṇo mahārājo dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājo virūḍhako mahārājo virūpākṣo mahārāja utthāyasanebhya ekāṃsena cīvarāṇi prāvṛtya dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalāni pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocan / ayaṃ bhagavan, suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājaḥ sarvatathāgatabhāṣitaḥ sarvatathāgatāvalokitaḥ sarvatathāgatasamanvāgataḥ sarvabodhisattvagaṇanamaskṛtaḥ sarvadevagaṇapūjitaḥ sarvedevendragaṇasaṃpraharṣakaḥ sarvalokapālastutaḥ stavito varṇitaḥ praśaṃsitaḥ sarvadevabhavanāvabhāsitaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ paramasukhapradāyakaḥ sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokaduḥkhasaṃśodhakaḥ sarvabhayapratiśamanaḥ sarvaparacakrapratinivartako durbhikṣakāntārapraśamano vyādhikāntārapraṇāśako jñānaprakāśakaḥ paramaśāntikaraḥ śokāyāsapraśamano vividhanānopadravyapraśamayitopadravaśatasahasrapraṇāśayitā / imamasya bhadanta bhagavan suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājasya vistareṇa parṣadi saṃprakāśyamānasyāsmākaṃ catūrṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sabalaparivārāṇām / etena ca dharmaśravaṇena dharmāmṛtarasena ca divyātmabhāvamahātejasā vivardhayiṣyanti // asmākaṃ kāyeṣu vīryaṃ ca balaṃ sthāma ca saṃjanitaṃ bhaviṣyanti / tejaśca śriyaṃ ca lakṣmīṃ cāsmākaṃ kāyeṣvāviśanti / vayaṃ bhagavaṃścatvāro mahārājā dhārmikāśca dharmavādinaśca dharmarājā dharmeṇa vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍanaramahoragāṇāṃ rājatvaṃ kārayiṣyāmaḥ / te vayaṃ bhagavan, catvāro mahārājāḥ sārdhamaṣṭāviṃśatiyakṣasenāpatibhiranekaiśca yakṣaśatasahasraiḥ satatasamitaṃ sarve jambudvīpaṃ divyena viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa vyavalokayiṣyāma ārakṣayiṣyāmaḥ paripācayiṣyāmaḥ / tena hetunā bhadanta bhagavannasmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ lokapāla iti saṃjñotpāditā //
body.translated_text: Then the great king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the great king <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the great king <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, and the great king <s>Virūpākṣa</s> rose from their seats, arranged their robes over one shoulder, placed their right knee upon the ground, and joining their palms in the direction of the Blessed One, said to him: 'This, O Blessed One — this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, is spoken by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, beheld by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, endowed with [the blessings of] all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, revered by all assemblies of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, worshipped by all hosts of gods, delighting all hosts of <s>Indras</s> among the gods, praised, lauded, extolled, and commended by all <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians); it illuminates all divine abodes; it bestows supreme happiness upon all beings; it purifies the sufferings of all hells, animal births, and the realm of <s>Yama</s>; it pacifies all fears; it repels all hostile armies; it calms the desolation of famine; it destroys the desolation of disease; it illuminates knowledge; it creates supreme peace; it pacifies grief and distress; it pacifies various and manifold calamities and destroys hundreds of thousands of afflictions. O Venerable Blessed One, when this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, is being expounded at length before the assembly, for us, the four great kings, together with our retinues and forces — by this hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> and the nectar-taste of the <s>Dharma</s>, the divine bodily splendor and great radiance will increase. Vigor, strength, and firmness will be generated in our bodies. Splendor, glory, and prosperity will enter our bodies. We, the four great kings, O Blessed One, are righteous and speakers of righteousness, and we are kings of <s>dharma</s>. O Venerable Blessed One, by <s>dharma</s> we shall exercise sovereignty over the gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, humans, and <s>mahoragas</s>. We, the four great kings, O Blessed One, together with the twenty-eight <s>yakṣa</s> generals and with many hundreds of thousands of <s>yakṣas</s>, shall constantly and uninterruptedly survey the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with divine, pure, superhuman vision; we shall protect it, guard it, and nurture it. For this reason, O Venerable Blessed One, we four great kings have been given the designation <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians).'

body.text: ye kecidbhadanta bhagavannasmin jambudvīpe viparyāsāḥ paracakreṇa copahatā bhaviṣyanti, durbhikṣakāntareṇa vā nānāvidhairupadravaśatairupadravasahasrairupadravaśatasahasrairupahatā bhaviṣyanti, te vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan catvāro mahārājā idamasya suvarṇaprabhāsoottamasūtrendrarājasya teṣāṃ ca sūtredradhāriṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ saṃcodanāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / yadā ceme bhadanta bhagavan dharmabhāṇakā bhikṣavo 'smākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ saṃcodanayā buddhādhiṣṭhānena ca yeṣu viṣayeṣūpasaṃkrameyusteṣu te viṣayeṣuḥ cemaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājaṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayeyuḥ / ya imānyevaṃrūpāṇi viṣayagatāti nānāvidhānyupadravaśatānyupadravasahasrānyupadravaśatasahasrāṇi ca praśamayiṣyanti //
body.translated_text: 'Whatever adversities, O Venerable Blessed One, may arise in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> from hostile armies, from the desolation of famine, or from hundreds, thousands, or hundreds of thousands of various afflictions — we, the four great kings, O Venerable Blessed One, shall encourage [the propagation of] this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, and those monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>) who uphold this king of sūtras. When, O Venerable Blessed One, these <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monks, encouraged by us four great kings and empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>, approach those regions — in those regions they shall expound at length this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>. And they shall pacify whatever various hundreds, thousands, and hundreds of thousands of afflictions may have arisen in those regions.'

body.text: yasya ca bhadanta bhagavan manuṣyarājasya viṣaye te sūtrendradhārakā bhikṣavā dharmabhāṇākā upasaṃkrāntā bhaviṣyanti / ayaṃ ca manuṣyarāja imaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsasūtrendrarājaṃ śṛṇyāt / śrutvā ca teṣāṃ sūtrendradhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ sarvapratyarthikebhya ārakṣāṃ kuryāt paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ kuryāt / te vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan catvāro mahārājāstasya manuṣyarājasya sarvaviṣayagatānāṃ ca sattvānāmārakṣāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / yadā ca bhadanta bhagavan sarvamanuṣyarājaḥ sūtrendradhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāṃ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ sukhatāṃ kuryāt / te vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan catvāro mahārājāstaṃ manuṣyarājaṃ sarvarājebhyaḥ satkṛtataraṃ kariṣyāmo gurukṛtaṃ ca kariṣyāmo mānitaṃ ca pūjitaṃ ca sarvaviṣayeṣu ca prasaṃśanīyaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'And, O Venerable Blessed One, in whatever human king's domain those monks who are <s>Dharma</s>-preachers and bearers of this king of sūtras shall arrive — if that human king should hear this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s>, and having heard it, should provide protection, shelter, support, and safeguarding for those monks who bear the king of sūtras against all adversaries — then we, O Venerable Blessed One, the four great kings, shall provide protection, shelter, support, safeguarding, peace, and well-being for that human king and for all beings in all the regions [of his domain]. And when, O Venerable Blessed One, any human king provides comfort to those monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers who bear the king of sūtras, with all means of comfort — then we, O Venerable Blessed One, the four great kings, shall make that human king honored above all kings, respected, esteemed, worshipped, and praised in all regions.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃścaturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu mahārājāḥ sādhu sādhu yuṣmākaṃ mahārājāḥ / yathāpi te yūyaṃ pūrvajinakṛtādhikārā avaropitakuśalamūlā bahubuddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraparyupāsitā dharmikāśca dharmavādinaśca dharmeṇa devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca rājatvaṃ kārayadhvam / yathāpi pūrvadīrgharātraṃ sarvasattvānāṃ hitacittāḥ sukhamaitrīcittāḥ sarvasattvahitasukhādhyāśayapratipannāḥ
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the four great kings: 'Excellent, excellent, O great kings! Excellent, excellent! Since you, O great kings, have performed meritorious acts under former <s>Jinas</s>, have planted roots of merit, and have attended upon many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Buddhas</s> — you are righteous and speakers of righteousness; exercise sovereignty over gods and humans by <s>dharma</s>! Since you have long been well-disposed, with minds of loving-kindness for the happiness [of all], and have resolved upon the welfare and happiness of all beings'

body.text: sarvāhitapratiṣedhikāḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sarvahitopasaṃhārābhiyuktāḥ / te yūyaṃ catvāro mahārājāsteṣāṃ manuṣyarājasya ca suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājasya pūjāsatkārābhiyuktānāmārakṣāṃ kariṣyata paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyata / tena yuṣmābhiścaturmahārājaiḥ sabalaparivārairanekaiśca yakṣaśatasahasrairatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dharmanetryārakṣitā bhaviṣyati paripālitā ca parigṛhītā ca bhaviṣyati / tena yuṣmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sabalaparivārāṇamanekeṣāṃ yakṣaśatasahasrāṇāṃ devānāṃ devāsurasaṃgrāme jayo bhaviṣyati, asurāṇāṃ ca parijayo bhaviṣyati / sarvaparacakrapramardakasya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājasyārthāya teṣāṃ sūtrendradhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāmārakṣāṃ kariṣyata paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyata //
body.translated_text: —who avert all harm and are devoted to bringing about the welfare of all beings. You, the Four Great Kings, shall provide protection, rescue, shelter, guardianship, and the blessing of peace and well-being to those human kings who are devoted to honoring and worshipping this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>. Through you, the Four Great Kings, with your retinues and with many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-vision of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present, shall be guarded, protected, and sheltered. Through this, for you Four Great Kings with your retinues and for the many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, there shall be victory among the gods in the battle between the gods and <s>Asuras</s>, and the <s>Asuras</s> shall be defeated. For the sake of this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, the crusher of all hostile forces, you shall provide protection, rescue, shelter, guardianship, and the blessing of peace and well-being to those who uphold this <s>Sūtra</s>—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.

body.text: atha vaiśravaṇo mahārājo dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājo viruḍhako mahārājo virūpākṣo mahārāja utthāyāsanebhya ekāṃsāni cīvaraiḥ prāvṛtya dakṣiṇāni jānumaṇḍalāni pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocan / ayaṃ bhadanta bhagavan, suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājo 'nāgate 'dhvani yatra grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu pracariṣyati yasya yasya manuṣyarājasya viṣayamanuprāpto bhaviṣyati / kaścidbhadanta bhagavanmanuṣyarājo bhagavan yenānena devendrasamayena rājaśāsreṇa rājatvaṃ kārayet / asya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya śrotā bhavaṃstāśca sūtrendradhārakā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayetpūjayetsatatasamitaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājaṃ śṛṇuyāt / anena dharmaśravaṇena saṃcodanadharmāmṛtapuṇyātmakānāmasmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sakalaparivārāṇāmanekeṣāṃ ca yakṣarākṣasaśatasahasrāṇāmimān divyātmabhāvān mahataujasā vivardhayet / mahāntaṃ vīryaṃ ca sthāma ca balaṃ cāsmākaṃ kāyeṣu tejaḥśriyaśca lakṣmī cāsmākaṃ vivardhayet / tena vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavaṃścatvāro mahārājāḥ sabalaparivārā anekaiḥ
body.translated_text: Then the Great King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the Great King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the Great King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, and the Great King <s>Virūpākṣa</s> rose from their seats, arranged their robes over one shoulder, placed their right knees upon the ground, and, joining their palms in the direction of the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Blessed One, this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, in the future time, wherever it circulates—in villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals—whatever human king's domain it shall reach: if any human king, Venerable Blessed One, should exercise kingship by means of this <s>Devendra</s>-covenant, this treatise on kingship; if he should become a listener of this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>; and if he should honor, revere, respect, and worship those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this <s>Sūtra</s>, and should constantly and continuously listen to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>—then through this hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>, the nectar-merit of the <s>Dharma</s>'s exhortation would increase, with great splendor, these divine bodies of ours—the Four Great Kings with our complete retinues and the many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>. It would increase great vigor, firmness, and strength in our bodies, and radiance, glory, and fortune for us. Therefore, Venerable Blessed One, we Four Great Kings with our retinues, together with many

body.text: yakṣaśatasahasrairadṛśyadbhiḥ kāyātmabhāvairetarhi cānāgate 'dhvani yatra grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣūpasaṃkramiṣyāmaḥ tatrāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājaḥ pracariṣyati / teṣāṃ ca manuṣyarājānāmasya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya śrotṝṇāṃ mātāpitṝṇāṃ cārakṣāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / paritrāṇaṃ paripālanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śasraparihāraṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ ca kariṣyāmaḥ / teṣāṃ ca rājakulānāṃ teṣāṃ ca rāṣṭrāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca viṣayāṇāmārakṣāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śasraparihāraṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / tāṃśca viṣayān sarvabhayopāyāsebhyaḥ parimocayiṣyāmaḥ paracakrāṇi ca pratinivartayiṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, with invisible bodies, both now and in the future time, shall proceed wherever—in villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals—this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> circulates. We shall provide protection to those human kings who listen to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, and to their parents. We shall provide rescue, guardianship, removal of punishment, removal of weapons, and the blessing of peace and well-being. We shall provide protection to those royal families, those kingdoms, and those domains. We shall provide rescue, shelter, guardianship, removal of punishment, removal of weapons, and the blessing of peace and well-being. We shall deliver those domains from all fears and afflictions, and we shall turn back hostile armies.'

body.text: yaḥ kaścit tasya manuṣyarājasya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya śroturmānayituḥ pūjayituranyaḥ sāmantakaḥ pratiśatrurājā bhavet / yadā ca bhadanta bhagavaṃstasya sāmantakasya pratiśatro rājña evaṃ cittamutpādet / so 'haṃ caturaṅgena balakāyena sārdhamasya viṣayamupasaṃkrameyaṃ vināśayitum / tena khalu punarbhadanta bhagavān kālena tena samayenāsya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya tejo 'nubhāvena tasya sāmantakasya pratiśatrurājasyānyai rājabhiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgrāme bhaviṣyati / svaviṣayagatāśca viṣayavilopāśca bhaviṣyanti / dāruṇāśca rājasaṃkṣobhā bhaviṣyanti / graharogāśca viṣaye prādubhūtā bhaviṣyanti / nānāvyākṣepaśatāni viṣaye prādurbhūtāni bhaviṣyanti / yadā ca bhadanta bhagavaṃstasya sāmantakasya pratiśatrurājasya svaviṣayagatānyevaṃrūpāṇi nānopadravaśatāni nānāvyakṣepaśatāni bhaveyuḥ / sa ca bhadanta bhagavan sāmantakapratiśatrurājaścaturaṅgīṇīṃ senāṃ yojayitvā paracakragamanāya svaviṣayānniṣkrānto bhavet / yatrāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sutrendrarājo bhavet sa pratiśatrurājaḥ sārdhaṃ caturaṅgabalakāyena taṃ viṣayamupasaṃkramitukāmo bhavet / taṃ vināśitukāmo bhavet / te vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavañcatvāro mahārājāḥ sabalaparivārā anekairyakṣarākṣasaśatasahasrairadṛśyairātmabhāvaistatropasaṃkramiṣyāmaḥ taṃ paracakramadhvānaṃ mārgapratipannaṃ
body.translated_text: 'If any neighboring hostile king should arise against that human king who listens to, respects, and worships this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>—and if, Venerable Blessed One, the thought should arise in that neighboring hostile king: "I shall march with my fourfold army against his domain to destroy it"—then, Venerable Blessed One, at that time, by the majestic power of this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, that neighboring hostile king shall have war with other kings in his own domain. There shall be plundering within his own domain. There shall be terrible royal disturbances. Planetary afflictions and diseases shall appear in his domain. Hundreds of various calamities shall appear in his domain. And when, Venerable Blessed One, such hundreds of various afflictions and calamities shall arise within the domain of that neighboring hostile king—and when that neighboring hostile king, having assembled his fourfold army, shall have marched out from his own domain to attack the hostile army, wishing to invade and destroy the domain where this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> exists—then, Venerable Blessed One, we Four Great Kings, with our retinues and with many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, with invisible bodies, shall proceed there, and that hostile army on the march

body.text: tathaiva pratinivartayiṣyāmo nānāvyākṣepaśatāni copasaṃhariṣyāmo vighnāṃśca kariṣyāmaḥ / yathā ca tatparacakraṃ na śakṣyati tatra viṣaya upasaṃkramitum / kutaḥ punarvināśaṃ kariṣyati //
body.translated_text: we shall turn back in the same way, and we shall bring about hundreds of various calamities [upon them] and create obstacles. So that hostile army shall not be able to invade that domain—how much less will it be able to destroy it!'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu mahārājāḥ sādhu khalu punaryuṣmākaṃ mahārājānām / yadyūyamatyā asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasamudānītāyā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherarthāya teṣāṃ manuṣyarājānāmasya ca suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya śrotṝṇāmārakṣāṃ kariṣyatha / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyatha / tāni ca rājakulāni tāni nagarāṇi tāni ca rāṣṭrāṇi tāni ca viṣayāṇyārakṣayiṣyatha / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śasraparihāraṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyatha / tāni ca viṣayāṇi sarvamayopadravopasargāpāyāsebhyaḥ parimocayiṣyatha / paracakrāṇi ca nivartayiṣyatha / sarvajambudvīpagatānāṃ cāsya manuṣyarājasyākalahayābhaṇḍanayāvigrahayā vivādayautsukyamapapadyatha / yathā ca te yuṣmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sabalaparivārāṇāmasmiñjambudvīpe teṣu caturṣu nagarasahasreṣu tāni caturaśītinagarasahasrāṇi teṣu teṣu viṣayeṣvabhirameyustena ca rājyaiśvaryeṇābhirameyustena ca dhanaskandhena parasparaṃ na viheṭhayeyuḥ / na parasparaṃ viheṭhaṃ janayeyuḥ / svena ca yathā pūrvakarmopacayena rājatvaṃ pratilabheyuḥ / svena ca rājyaiśvaryeṇa ca tuṣṭā bhaveyuḥ / na ca paraspareṇa vināśayeyuḥ / na viṣeya vināśāya parakrameyuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One gave his approval to those Four Great Kings: 'Excellent, excellent, Great Kings! It is truly excellent of you, Great Kings, that you, for the sake of the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) accumulated over inconceivable <s>koṭīniyutaśatasahasra</s> aeons, shall provide protection, rescue, shelter, guardianship, and the blessing of peace and well-being to those human kings who listen to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>; and that you shall protect those royal families, those cities, those kingdoms, and those domains. You shall provide rescue, shelter, guardianship, removal of punishment, removal of weapons, and the blessing of peace and well-being. You shall deliver those domains from all diseases, afflictions, misfortunes, and distresses. You shall turn back hostile armies. You shall bring about for all the beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and for that human king [a state] free from quarrel, free from dispute, free from conflict, and free from controversy, bringing contentment. And so those eighty-four thousand cities in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> shall rejoice in their respective domains under your [protection], you Four Great Kings with your retinues, and they shall rejoice in that royal sovereignty, and with that wealth they shall not harm one another. They shall not engender mutual harm. Each shall obtain kingship through the accumulation of their own former <s>karma</s>. They shall be contented with their own royal sovereignty. They shall not destroy one another, nor shall they advance to destroy [another's] domain.'

body.text: yathā cāsmiñjambudvīpe teṣu caturaśītiṣu viṣayanagarasahasreṣu tāni caturaśītirāja sahasrāṇi paraspareṇa hitacittāni maitrīcittāni sukhacittāni paraspareṇa kalahayābhaṇḍanayāvigrahayāvivādayā sveṣu sveṣu viṣayeṣvabhiramerantena puṇyena caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sabalaparivārāṇāmayaṃ ca jambudvīpaḥ sphīto bhaviṣyati / subhikṣaśca ramaṇīyaśca bahujanasamākīrṇaścarddhaścaujovataraśca bhaviṣyati / ṛtumāsārdhamāsasaṃvatsarāṇi ca sarvāṇi samācārayuktāni bhaviṣyanti / ahorātraṃ grahanakṣatracandrasūryāśca samāgrahiṣyanti / kālena ca varṣadhārāḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatiṣyanti / sarvajamdudvīpagatāni ca sattvāni sarvadhanadhānyasamṛddhāni bhaviṣyanti / mahābhogāni cāmatsarāṇi ca bhaviṣyanti / parityāgavanti daśakuśalakarmapathasamanvāgatāni ca bhaviṣyanti / yadbhūyasā sugatau svargaloka upapatsyante / devabhuvanāni cākīrṇāni bhaviṣyanti devairdevaputraiśca //
body.translated_text: 'And when in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in those eighty-four thousand domain-cities, those eighty-four thousand kings, with minds of mutual goodwill, friendliness, and happiness, free from quarrel, dispute, conflict, and controversy, shall rejoice in their respective domains—then by that merit, for the Four Great Kings with their retinues, this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> shall become prosperous, well-provisioned, delightful, teeming with people, flourishing, and vigorous. The seasons, months, fortnights, and years shall all follow their proper course. Day and night, the planets, constellations, moon, and sun shall move in harmony. Rains shall fall upon the earth in due season. All beings throughout <s>Jambudvīpa</s> shall be endowed with abundant wealth and grain. They shall have great enjoyments and be free from miserliness. They shall be generous and endowed with the ten wholesome courses of action. For the most part, they shall be reborn in the heavenly world, in the <s>Svarga</s> realm. The divine mansions shall be filled with gods and sons of gods.'

body.text: yatkaścinmahārājo bhaved ya itthamasya suvarṇaprabhāsattamasya sūtrendrarājasya śrotā bhavenmānayitā ca pūjayitā ca teṣāṃ ca sūtrendradhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāmautsukyaṃ satkuryād gurukuryānmānayetpūjayet / yuṣmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sabalaparivārāṇāmanekeṣāṃ ca yakṣaśatasahasrāṇāmanukampārthāya satatasamitaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājendraṃ śṛṇvan / anena dharmaśravaṇasalilodakena yuṣmākametānyātmabhāvāni saṃtarpayet / mahataujasā yuṣmākametāni śarīrāṇi vivardhayet / mahacca yuṣmākaṃ vīryaṃ ca sthāma balaṃ ca vapuṣaḥ saṃjanayet / tejaśca śriyaśca lakṣmīśca yuṣmākaṃ vivardhayet / tena ca manuṣyarājena mama śākyamunestathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyācintyā mahāvipulavistīrṇā pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati / tena tasya manuṣyarājenātītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāmanekeṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ koṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāmacintyā mahatī vistīrṇā sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati / tena tasya manuṣyarājasya mahatyārakṣā kṛtā bhaviṣyati / tena ca tasya rājño rakṣāṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śasraparihāraṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati / agramahiṣyāśca rājaputrāṇāṃ ca sarvāntaḥpurasya ca rājakulasya ca sarvasya mahatyārakṣā kṛtā bhaviṣyati / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati / rājakulanivāsanyaśca sarvadevatā ojovattarāśca cittena sukhasaumanasyena samanvāgatā bhavitāro ratimanubhaviṣyanti / tāni ca rāṣṭrāṇi tāni ca viṣayāṇi cārakṣitāni bhaviṣyanti / paripācitāni cānutpīḍitāni cākaṇṭakāni bhaviṣyanti / sarvaparacakrānyavamarditāni cānupasargāṇi cānupāyāsāni ceti //
body.translated_text: 'Whatever great king there may be who becomes a listener, one who respects and worships this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, and who with eagerness honors, reveres, respects, and worships those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this <s>Sūtra</s>—[if] out of compassion for you Four Great Kings with your retinues and for the many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, he constantly and continuously listens to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>—then by this water of <s>Dharma</s>-hearing, he would nourish these bodies of yours; he would increase these bodies of yours with great splendor; he would generate great vigor, firmness, and strength for your bodies; and he would increase radiance, glory, and fortune for you. By that human king, an inconceivable, great, vast, and extensive worship of me, <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, Worthy One, Perfectly Awakened One, shall have been performed. By that human king, an inconceivable, great, vast worship with all requisites shall have been performed for <s>koṭīniyutaśatasahasras</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, countless <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present. Great protection shall have been established for that human king. Protection, rescue, shelter, guardianship, removal of punishment, removal of weapons, and the blessing of peace and well-being shall have been established for that king—for the chief queen, the princes, the entire inner palace, and all the royal family. The deities dwelling in the royal palace shall be endowed with vigor, with minds of happiness and joy, and shall experience delight. Those kingdoms and those domains shall be protected, brought to maturity, unoppressed, free from thorns, with all hostile forces crushed, free from misfortune, and free from affliction.'

body.text: evamukte vaiśravaṇo mahārājo dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājo virūḍhako mahārājo virūpākṣo mahārājaste sarve bhagavantametadavocan / tena ca bhagavanmanuṣyarājena susnātagātreṇa bhavitavyaṃ sugandhavāsanadhāriṇā navaruciravastraprāvṛtena nānālaṃkāravibhūṣitena bhavitavyam / ātmanaśca nīcataramāsanaṃ prajñapayitavyam / tatrāsane niṣīditvā rājyamadamattena na bhavitavyam / na coccai rājñā svayaṃ prajñapayitavyam / śāṭhyamānamadadarpavivarjitena cittenāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājaḥ śrotavyaḥ / tasya ca dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣorantike śāstṛsaṃjñotpādayitavyā / tena manuṣyarājena tasminkāle tasmitsamaye 'gramahiṣī rājaputrāśca rājaduhitaraśca sarvāntaḥpuragaṇāśca
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> the Great King, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> the Great King, <s>Virūḍhaka</s> the Great King, and <s>Virūpākṣa</s> the Great King—all of them said this to the Blessed One: 'That human king, O Blessed One, should have his body well-bathed, should wear fragrances and perfumed garments, should be wrapped in fresh and beautiful robes, and should be adorned with various ornaments. He should have a seat prepared lower than his own [for himself]. Having sat upon that seat, he should not be intoxicated with the pride of kingship. The king should not have [a seat] set up high for himself. With a mind free from deceit, arrogance, pride, and haughtiness, he should listen to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>. And in the presence of that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk, he should generate the perception [of him as] the Teacher. That human king, at that time and on that occasion, should look upon the chief queen, the princes, the princesses, and the entire retinue of the inner palace

body.text: priyahitābhyāṃ prekṣitavyāḥ / priyavacanaiścāgramahiṣī rājaputrāśca rājaduhitaraśca sarvāntaḥpuragaṇāśca ālapayitavyāḥ / nānāvicitrāśca dharmaśravaṇapūjā ājñāpayitavyāḥ / acintyayātulyayā prītyātmānaṃ saṃtarpayitavyam / acintyena prītisukhena sukhāpayitavyam / sukhendriyeṇa ca bhavitavyam / ātmanaśca mahābalena bhavitavyam / mahatā praharṣeṇātmā praharṣayitavyaḥ / mahatā premajātena dharmabhāṇakaḥ pratyutthātavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: with love and goodwill. He should address the chief queen, the princes, the princesses, and the entire retinue of the inner palace with kind words. He should order various and wonderful honors for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>. He should gratify himself with inconceivable and incomparable joy. He should make himself happy with inconceivable joy and bliss. He should have faculties at ease. He should be possessed of great strength. He should delight himself with great exultation. He should rise to greet the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher with great affection.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavāṃstāṃścaturo mahārājānetadavocat / tasmiṃśca khalu pugarmahārajāḥ kāle tasminsamaye tena manuṣyarājena sarvaśvetāni pāṇḍurāṇi navarucivastrāṇi prāvaritavyāni / nānāvibhūṣaṇālaṃkārairātmā samalaṃkartavyaṃ / mahatā rājānubhāvena mahatā rājavyūhena nānāvicitraratnamaṅgalaparigṛhītaistato rājakulādabhiniṣkramitavyam / tasya ca dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣoḥ pratyudgamanāya gantavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ? yāvanti manuṣyarājastatra padāni bhāvayati tāvanti kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃsārātparāṅmukhāni kariṣyati tāvatāṃ cakravartirājakulakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyati / yāvanti sa tatra padānyatikramiṣyati tāvatāṃ caiva dṛṣṭadhārmikeṇācintyena mahatā rājyaiśvaryeṇa vivardhiṣyate / anekakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāmudārodārāṇāṃ cāvasthānānāṃ saptaratnamayānāṃ divyavimānānāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyati / anekeṣāṃ ca divyodārāṇāṃ mānuṣyakāṇāṃ rājakulaputraśatasahasrāṇāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyati / sarvatra ca jātiṣu mahaiśvaryaprāpto bhaviṣyati / dīrghāyuṣkaśca bhaviṣyati / ciraṃjīvī ca bhaviṣyati / pratibhāṇavāṃścādeyavacanaśca yaśasvī ca suviśālakīrtiśca bhaviṣyati / sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasya sukhitaśca bhaviṣyati / udārodārāṇāṃ ca divyamānuṣyakāṇāṃ sukhānāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyati / mahābalaśca mahānagnabalavegadhārī cābhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkaratayā samanvāgataśca bhaviṣyati / sarvatra jātiṣu tathāgatasamavadhānagato bhaviṣyati / sarvakalyāṇamitrāṇi ca pratilapsyate / aparimitapuṇyaskandhasya parigṛhīto bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said this to those four Great Kings: 'At that time and on that occasion, O Great Kings, that human king should cover himself with entirely white, clean, fresh, and beautiful garments. He should adorn himself with various ornamental decorations. With great royal majesty, with a great royal retinue, accompanied by various wonderful jewel-auspicious objects, he should proceed out from the royal palace. He should go to meet that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk. For what reason? As many steps as that human king takes there, for that many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of aeons will he turn away from <s>saṃsāra</s>, and he will obtain that many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of lineages of <s>Cakravartin</s> kings. As many steps as he takes there, by that many [times] will he prosper in this very life with inconceivable and great royal sovereignty. He will obtain hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of aeons' worth of noble and excellent abodes, divine mansions made of the seven treasures. He will obtain hundreds of thousands of noble divine and human sons of royal lineages. In all births he will attain great sovereignty. He will be long-lived. He will be long-enduring. He will be eloquent, of authoritative speech, famous, and of widely-spread renown. He will be happy in the world of <s>devas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. He will obtain noble and excellent divine and human pleasures. He will be of great strength, bearing the power and force of great vigor, handsome, pleasing, beautiful to behold, endowed with the most auspicious excellence of complexion. In all births he will be in the presence of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. He will obtain all spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇa-mitras</s>). He will be embraced by an immeasurable aggregate of merit.'

body.text: imanyevaṃrūpāṇi mahārājaguṇānuśaṃsāni saṃpaśyamānena tena rājñā dharmabhāṇako yojanātpratyutthātavyaḥ / tasya dharmabhāṇakasyāntike śāstṛsaṃjñotpādayitavyā / evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam / adya mama śākyamunistathāgato 'rhansamyaksaṃbuddha iha rājakule pravekṣyati / adya mama śākyamunistathāgato 'rhansamyaksaṃbuddha iha rājakule svajanamanuśasiṣyate / sarvalokavipratyayanīyaṃ dharmaśravaṇaṃ śroṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: 'Seeing such qualities and benefits, O Great Kings, that king should rise to meet the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher from a distance of one <s>yojana</s>. In the presence of that <s>Dharma</s>-preaching monk, he should generate the perception [of him as] the Teacher. He should generate this thought: "Today <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, will enter my royal palace. Today <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, will instruct my own people in this royal palace. I shall hear a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that inspires confidence in all the world.

body.text: adyāhamanena dharmaśravaṇenāvaivartiko bhaviṣyāmyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / adya mayā tathāgatakoṭīniyutaśataśasrāṇyārāgitāni bhaviṣyanti / adya mayātītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmacintyā mahatī vipulā vistīrṇā pūjā kṛtā bhaviṣyati / adya mama narakagatitiryagyoniyamalokaduḥkhānyantaśaḥ samucchinnāni bhaviṣyanti / adya mayānekānāṃ brahmendrarājatvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrātmabhāvapratilabdhānāṃ kuśalamūlabījānyavaropitāni bhaviṣyanti / adya mayānekānāṃ śakrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrātmabhāvapratilabdhānāṃ kuśalamūlānyavaropitāni bhaviṣyanti / adya mayānekāni cakravartirājakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrātmabhāvapratilabdhānāṃ kuśalamūlabījānyavaropitāni bhaviṣyanti / adya mayā sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃsārātparimocitāni bhaviṣyanti / adya mayācintyasuvipulavistīrṇāpāramitapuṇyaskandhaḥ parigṛhīto bhaviṣyanti / adya mama sarvāntaḥpurasya mahatyārakṣā kṛtā bhaviṣyanti / adya mama rājakule 'cintyā samabiśiṣṭānuttarā mahatī śāntiḥ kṛtā bhaviṣyati svastyayanaṃ ca / adya mamāyaṃ sarvaviṣaya ārakṣito bhaviṣyati / paripālitaścānutpīḍitaścānutkaṇṭhikaśca sarvaparacakrānavamarditaścānupasargaścānupāyāsaśca bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: Today, by this hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>, I shall become irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) in unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Today, by me, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s> will have been delighted. Today, by me, an inconceivable, great, vast, and extensive offering will have been made to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present. Today, the sufferings of the realms of hell, animal rebirth, and the world of <s>Yama</s> will have been completely cut off for me. Today, by me, seeds of roots of merit for the attainment of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of existences as <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and kings will have been planted. Today, by me, roots of merit for the attainment of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of existences as <s>Śakra</s> will have been planted. Today, by me, seeds of roots of merit for the attainment of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of existences as <s>Cakravartin</s> kings will have been planted. Today, by me, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of beings will have been liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s>. Today, by me, an inconceivable, well-extensive, vast, immeasurable aggregate of merit will have been embraced. Today, great protection will have been established for my entire inner palace. Today, in my royal house, an inconceivable, equally distinguished, unsurpassed, great peace and well-being (<s>svastyayana</s>) will have been established. Today, this entire realm of mine will be protected, guarded, unoppressed, undistressed, uncrushed by any foreign army, free from calamity, and free from affliction."'

body.text: yadā ca mahārājāḥ sa manuṣyarājo 'nenaivaṃrūpeṇa saddharmagauraveṇa suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājadhārakā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayedyuṣmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sabalaparivārāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca devagaṇānāmanekeṣāṃ ca yakṣaśatasahasrāṇāṃ mahā tathā dharmāṅgapratyakṣaṃ dadyāt yena caivāsau manuṣyarājaḥ puṇyabhisaṃskāreṇa kuśalābhisaṃskāreṇa ca tenaiva cātmabhāvena ca dṛṣṭadhārmikeṇācintyena mahatā rājyaiśvaryeṇa vivardhayiṣyati / dṛṣṭadhārmikeṇācintyena mahatā rājatejasā samanvāgato bhaviṣyati / śriyā ca tejasā ca lakṣmyā cālaṃkṛto bhaviṣyati / sarvapratyarthikāśca sarvaśatravaśca sahadharmeṇa sunigṛhītā bhaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: 'When, O Great Kings, that human king, with such reverence for the true <s>Dharma</s>, honors, respects, esteems, and venerates the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, and when he makes a direct offering of the great limb of the <s>Dharma</s> to you four Great Kings together with your retinues and forces, and to those hosts of <s>devas</s>, and to many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>—then, by that very merit-formation and wholesome-formation, that human king will prosper in this very life with inconceivable and great royal sovereignty. He will be endowed in this very life with inconceivable and great royal splendor. He will be adorned with glory, majesty, and fortune. All adversaries and all enemies will be well-subdued by the force of <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: evamukte catvāro mahārājā bhagavantametadavocan / yaḥ kaścidbhadanta bhagavanmanuṣyarājo bhavet so 'nenaivaṃrūpeṇa dharmagauraveṇemaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ śṛṇuyāt / tāśca sūtrendradhārakā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ satkuryādgurukuryānmānayetpūjayet / asmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāmarthāya tadrājakulaṃ suśodhitaṃ śodhayet / nānāgandhodakasaṃsiktaṃ kuryāt / taṃ ca dharmaśrāvaṇamasmābhiścaturbhiśca mahārājaiḥ sārdhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ śṛṇyādātmano 'rthāya sarvadevatā ca kiṃcinmātraṃ kuśalaṃ pratyakṣaṃ dadyāt / samantaraniṣaṇṇasya ca bhadanta bhagavaṃstasya bhikṣordhamāsanagatasya tena manuṣyarājenāsmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāmarthāya nānāgandhā dhūpayitavyāḥ / sahadhūpiteṣu bhadanta bhagavaṃstasya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya pūjārthāya nānāgandheṣu nānāgandhadhūpalatā niścaranti / tasminneva kṣaṇalavamuhūrte 'smākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ svakasvakabhavanagatānyuparyantarīkṣe nānāgandhadhūpalatāchatrāṇi saṃsthāsyanti / udārāṃśca gandhānāghrāsyanti / suvarṇavarṇamayāścāvabhāsāḥ prādurbhaviṣyanti / tena cāvabhāsenāsmākaṃ bhavanānyavabhāsitāni bhaviṣyanti / brahmaṇaḥ sahāṃpateḥ śakrasya ca devānāmindrasya sarasvatyāśca mahādevyā dṛḍhāyāśca mahādevyāḥ śriyaśca mahādevyāḥ saṃjayasya ca mahāyakṣasenāpateraṣṭāviṃśatīnāṃ ca mahāyakṣasenāpatīnaṃ maheśvarasya ca devaputrasya vajrapāṇeśca mahāyakṣasenāpatermāṇibhadrasya ca mahāyakṣasenāpaterhārītyāśca pañcaputraśataparivārāṇāmanavataptasya ca nāgarājasya caiteṣāṃ bhadanta bhagavansvakasvakabhavanagatānām / tena kṣaṇalavamuhūrtenoparyantarīkṣe nānāgandhadhūpalatāchatrāṇi saṃsthāsyanti / udārāṃśca nānāgandhānāghrāsyanti / suvarṇavarṇamayāścāvabhāsāḥ prādurbhaviṣyanti / tayā cāvabhāsayā sarvabhavanānyavabhāsitāni bhaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the four Great Kings said this to the Blessed One: 'Whatever human king there may be, Venerable Blessed One, who with such reverence for the <s>Dharma</s> listens to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, and who honors, respects, esteems, and venerates the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this king of <s>sūtras</s>, and who cleans that royal palace thoroughly for the sake of us four Great Kings, and has it sprinkled with various fragrant waters, and who listens to this <s>Dharma</s>-hearing in common together with us four Great Kings for his own benefit and makes even the slightest merit directly available to all the deities—then, Venerable Blessed One, when that monk seated nearby on the <s>Dharma</s>-seat [begins to preach], that human king should burn various incenses for the sake of us four Great Kings. As soon as the incenses are burned, Venerable Blessed One, for the worship of this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, from those various incenses, various fragrant incense-tendrils will issue forth. In that very instant, moment, and hour, fragrant incense-tendril canopies will stand in the sky above the respective palaces of us four Great Kings. They will smell noble fragrances. Golden-colored radiances will appear. And by that radiance, our palaces will be illuminated. [The same will occur] for <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, for <s>Śakra</s> the lord of <s>devas</s>, for the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, for the great goddess <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, for the great goddess <s>Śrī</s>, for <s>Saṃjaya</s> the great <s>Yakṣa</s>-general, for the twenty-eight great <s>Yakṣa</s>-generals, for the <s>deva</s>-prince <s>Maheśvara</s>, for <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> the great <s>Yakṣa</s>-general, for <s>Māṇibhadra</s> the great <s>Yakṣa</s>-general, for <s>Hārītī</s> together with her retinue of five hundred sons, and for <s>Anavatapta</s> the <s>Nāga</s>-king—for all these, Venerable Blessed One, in their respective palaces: in that instant, moment, and hour, various fragrant incense-tendril canopies will stand in the sky above. They will smell noble and various fragrances. Golden-colored radiances will appear. And by that radiance, all their palaces will be illuminated.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavāṃścaturo mahārājānetadavocat / na kevalaṃ yuṣmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ svakasvakabhavanagatānāmuparyantarīkṣagatāti nānāgandhadhūpalatāchatrāṇi saṃsthāsyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? sahapradhūpitāśca mahārājāstena manuṣyarājena nānāgandhā asya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya pūjopasthānāya / tataścaiva dhūpakuṇḍahastaparigṛhītā nānāgandhadhūpalatā niścariṣyanti / tena kṣaṇalavamuhūrtena sarvasyāmasyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau yatra koṭīśataṃ candrāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the four Great Kings: 'Not only above the respective palaces of you four Great Kings will various fragrant incense-tendril canopies stand in the sky. For what reason? As soon as those various incenses are burned by that human king for the worship and service of this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, from the very incense-burner held in hand, various fragrant incense-tendrils will issue forth. In that instant, moment, and hour, throughout this entire <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> (triple-thousand great-thousand) world-system, wherever there are hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of moons,

body.text: koṭīśataṃ sumerūṇāṃ parvatarājānāṃ koṭīśataṃ cakravāḍamahācakravāḍānāṃ parvatarājānāṃ koṭīśataṃ caturmahādvīpānāṃ koṭīśataṃ caturmahārājakāyikānāṃ devānāṃ koṭīśataṃ trayastriṃśānāṃ devānāṃ koṭīśataṃ yāvannaivasaṃjñāyatanopagānāṃ devānām / sarvatra ca teṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātukoṭīśateṣu trayastriṃśeṣu devanikāyeṣu sarveṣāṃ ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakiṃnaramahoragāṇāṃ ca bhavanagatānāṃ coparyantarīkṣagatāni nānāgandhadhūpalatāchatrāṇi saṃsthāsyanti / udārāṃśca nānāgandhānāghrāsyanti / suvarṇavarṇamayāścāvabhāsāḥ prādurbhaviṣyanti / tābhiścāvabhāsābhiḥ sarvabhavanānyavabhāsitāni bhaviṣyanti / ratnacchatrāṇi saṃsthāsyanti / udārodārāñca gandhānāghrāsyanti sarvadevabhavaneṣu suvarṇavarṇāvabhāsāḥ prādurbhaviṣyanti / tena cāvabhāsena sarvadevabhavanānyavabhāsitāni bhaviṣyanti / yathā trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sarvadevabhavanānyuparyantarīkṣe tāni nānāgandhadhūpalatāchatrāṇi saṃsthāsyanti / tathā cāsya mahārājāḥ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya tejasā kuṇḍahastena dhūpitāstena manuṣyarājena nānāgandhā asya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya pūjārthāya nānāgandhadhūpalatāchatrāṇi saṃsthāsyanti / tena kṣaṇalavamuhūrtena samantāddaśasu dikṣvanekeṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣvanekeṣāṃ gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānāṃ tathāgatakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāmuparyantarīkṣe tāni nānāgandhadhūpalatāchatrāṇi saṃsthāsyanti / teṣu vālukopameṣu buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣvudārodārānnānāgandhadhūpānāghrāsyanti / suvarṇavarṇamayāvabhāsāḥ prādurbhaviṣyanti / tena cāvabhāsena tānyanekāni gaṅgānadīvālukopamāni buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyabhāsitāni bhaviṣyanti / samanantaraprādurbhūtāni ca mahārājā imānyevaṃrūpāṇi mahāprātihāryāṇi tānyanekāni gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi pratiṣṭhitāstathāgatāstaṃ ca dharmabhāṇakaṃ samanvāhariṣyanti / sādhukārāṇi ca pradāsyanti sādhu sādhu satpuruṣa sādhu punastvaṃ satpuruṣa / yastvamimamevaṃrūpaṃ gambhīramevaṃ gambhīrārthamevaṃ gambhīrāvabhāsamevamacintyaguṇadharmasamanvāgataṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayitukāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: hundreds of millions of <s>Sumeru</s>s, kings of mountains; hundreds of millions of <s>Cakravāḍa</s> and <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s> mountain-kings; hundreds of millions of four great continents; hundreds of millions of gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven; hundreds of millions of <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods; up to hundreds of millions of gods of the <s>Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s> (realm of neither perception nor non-perception). And everywhere in those hundreds of millions of great trichiliocosms, in the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> divine assemblies and in the abodes of all gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> — above, in the sky, various fragrant incense-creeper-parasols shall be established. They shall smell noble, various fragrances. Radiances of golden color shall appear. And by those radiances, all abodes shall be illuminated. Jeweled parasols shall be established. They shall smell supremely noble fragrances in all divine abodes, and radiances of golden color shall appear. And by that radiance, all divine abodes shall be illuminated. Just as in the great trichiliocosm, above all divine abodes in the sky, those various fragrant incense-creeper-parasols shall be established — even so, O great kings, by the power of this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, when that human king offers incense with a vessel as worship of this supreme king of sūtras, various fragrant incense-creeper-parasols shall be established. And in that instant, moment, and hour, in every direction, in the ten directions, in many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, above the many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Tathāgatas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the sky, those various fragrant incense-creeper-parasols shall be established. In those <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands [of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>], among hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Buddhas</s>, they shall smell supremely noble, various fragrant incenses. Radiances of golden color shall appear. And by that radiance, those many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> shall be illuminated. And immediately upon the appearance of these great miracles, O great kings, those many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Tathāgatas</s> established in <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> shall attend to that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher and shall give their approval: 'Excellent, excellent, O good man! Excellent again, O good man! That you wish to expound at length this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, so profound, of such profound meaning, of such profound radiance, endowed with such inconceivable qualities and <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: na caite sattvā itareṇa kuśalamūlena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti / ya imaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājamantaśaḥ śroṣyanti, prāgevodgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti likhiṣyanti likhāpayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti / vistareṇa parṣadi saṃprakāśayiṣyanti deśayiṣyantyuddekṣyanti svādhyāyiṣyanti yoniśo manasi bhāvayiṣyanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? sahaśravaṇenāsya puruṣasya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasyānekāni bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyavaivartikāni bhaviṣyantyanuttarāyāḥ samyaksabodheḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Nor shall those beings be endowed with merely ordinary roots of merit who shall even hear this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s> — how much more so those who shall take it up, retain it, write it, cause it to be written, recite it, master it, expound it at length before an assembly, teach it, preach it, study it, and properly contemplate it in their minds! Why is that? Because immediately upon hearing this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> shall become irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) from supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).'

body.text: atha khalu tāni samantāddaśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu buddhakṣetrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣvanekāni tathāgatakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi svakasvakeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pratiṣṭhitāni tena kālena tena samayenaikapādenaikavācaikasvaranirghoṣeṇa tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣordharmāsanagatasyaitadūcuḥ / upasaṃkramiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣānāgate 'dhvani bodhimaṇḍam / pradarśayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣa bodhimaṇḍavarāgragato drumarājamūlopaviṣṭaḥ sarvatrailokyaprativiśiṣṭāni sarvasattvāṃstrikālāntarāṇi vratatapaścaraṇabalādhānānyadhiṣṭhānānyadhiṣṭhitānyanekāni duṣkarakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi samalaṃkariṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣa bodhimaṇḍam / paritrāyiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣa sarvāṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātūn / parājayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣa drumarājamūlopaviṣṭaḥ kṛtimarūpaparamabībhatsadarśanaṃ nānāvikṛtarūpamacintyamārasainyam / abhisaṃbhotsyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣa bodhimaṇḍavarāgragato 'nupamapraśāntavirajaskagambhīrāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim / pravartayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣāryasāradṛḍhavajrāsanopaviṣṭaḥ sarvajanābhisaṃstutaṃ paramagambhīraṃ dvādaśākāramanuttaradharmacakram / parāhaniṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣānuttaraṃ dharmagañjavādyam / āpūrayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣānuttaraṃ mahādharmaśaṅkham / ucchrayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣa mahādharmadhvajam / prajvalayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣānuttarāṃ dharmolkām / pravarṣayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣānuttaraṃ mahādharmavarṣam / parājayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣanekāni kleśaśatasahasrāṇi / pratārayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣānekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi subhīmānmahābhayasamudrāt / parimocayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣānekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃsāracakrāt / ārāgayiṣyasi tvaṃ satpuruṣānekāni tathāgatakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi //
body.translated_text: Then those many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Tathāgatas</s> established in their respective <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the <s>Buddha</s>-field systems equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in every direction, in the ten directions — at that time and on that occasion, with one voice, one word, one utterance, said to that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk seated upon the <s>Dharma</s>-seat: 'You, O good man, shall in the future approach the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). You, O good man, seated at the supreme foremost seat of awakening at the foot of the king of trees, shall demonstrate [the path]. You, O good man, shall adorn the seat of awakening with the empowerments (<s>adhiṣṭhānas</s>) of vows, austerities, practices, and the accumulation of spiritual power, surpassing all three worlds, transcending the three times for all beings, through many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>kalpas</s> of difficult deeds. You, O good man, shall protect all the great trichiliocosms. You, O good man, seated at the foot of the king of trees, shall vanquish the inconceivable army of <s>Māra</s> with its fabricated, supremely hideous, and variously distorted forms. You, O good man, seated at the supreme foremost seat of awakening, shall fully awaken to the incomparable, tranquil, stainless, profound, unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). You, O good man, seated upon the noble, essential, firm, diamond seat (<s>vajrāsana</s>), shall turn the supremely profound Wheel of the <s>Dharma</s> in twelve aspects (<s>dvādaśākāra</s>), unsurpassed, acclaimed by all people. You, O good man, shall strike the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-kettle-drum. You, O good man, shall fill the unsurpassed great <s>Dharma</s>-conch. You, O good man, shall raise the great <s>Dharma</s>-banner. You, O good man, shall kindle the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-torch. You, O good man, shall rain the unsurpassed great <s>Dharma</s>-rain. You, O good man, shall vanquish many hundreds of thousands of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>). You, O good man, shall ferry across many hundreds of thousands of millions of beings from the terrifying, great, fearful ocean. You, O good man, shall liberate many hundreds of thousands of millions of beings from the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>. You, O good man, shall delight many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: evamukte catvāro mahārājā bhagavantametadavocan / asya bhadanta bhagavansuvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasyemānyevaṃrūpāṇi dṛpdhārmikāṇi māraparājayikāni ca guṇāni saṃpaśyamānasya buddhasahasrāvaruptakuśalamūlasya manuṣyarājasyānukampāccāparimitapuṇyaskandhaparigrahaṃ saṃpaśyamānāste vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavaṃścatvāro mahārājāḥ sabalaparivārā anekairyakṣaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ svabhavanagatā nānāgandhadhūpalatāchatrāḥ saṃcoditāḥ samānā adṛśyairātmabhāvairyena tasya manuṣyarājasyopagatasaṃskārakūṭasuśodhitaṃ nānāgandhodakasusaṃsiktaṃ nānālaṃkārasamalaṃkṛtaṃ rājakulaṃ tenopasaṃkramiṣyāmo dharmaśravaṇāya / brahmā ca sahāṃpatiḥ śakraśca devānāmindraḥ sarasvatī ca mahādevī śrīśca mahādevī dṛḍhā ca pṛthivīdevatā saṃjayaśca mahāyakṣasenāpatiraṣṭāviṃśatimahāyakṣasenāpatayaśca maheśvaraśca devaputro vajrapāṇiśca guhyakādhipatirmāṇibhadraśca mahāyakṣasenāpatirhārītī ca pañcaputraśataparivārā anavataptaśca nāgarājaḥ sāgaraśca nāgarājaḥ / anekāni ca devakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyadṛśyairātmabhāvairyena tasya manuṣyarājasya tatra ta nānālaṃkārasamalaṃkṛtaṃ rājakulaṃ yatra tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣoḥ puṣpābhikīrṇāyāṃ dharaṇyāṃ śaucapragṛhītaṃ nānālaṃkārasamalaṃkṛtaṃ yatra yatra dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣoḥ puṣpābhikīrṇāyaṃ dharaṇyāṃ śaucapragṛhītaṃ nānālaṃkārasamalaṃkṛtaṃ yatra yatra dharmāsanaṃ prajñaptaṃ tatra bhaviṣyanti dharmaśravaṇāya //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the four great kings said to the Blessed One: 'Seeing these such righteous and <s>Māra</s>-defeating qualities of this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, O Venerable Blessed One — and seeing the vast accumulation of merit for a human king who has roots of merit planted under a thousand <s>Buddhas</s>, out of compassion — we, the four great kings, O Venerable Blessed One, together with our retinues and forces, with many hundreds of thousands of <s>yakṣas</s>, having gone from our own abodes, bearing various fragrant incense-creeper-parasols, encouraged [by the sūtra], with invisible bodies, shall approach the well-purified, well-sprinkled with various fragrant waters, and variously adorned royal palace of that human king, for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. And <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> the lord of the gods, the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the great goddess <s>Śrī</s>, the earth-deity <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, the great <s>yakṣa</s>-general <s>Saṃjaya</s>, the twenty-eight great <s>yakṣa</s>-generals, <s>Maheśvara</s> the divine prince, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> the lord of the <s>guhyakas</s>, <s>Māṇibhadra</s> the great <s>yakṣa</s>-general, <s>Hārītī</s> with her retinue of five hundred sons, <s>Anavatapta</s> the <s>nāga</s>-king, <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>nāga</s>-king, and many hundreds of thousands of millions of gods — all with invisible bodies — shall come to that human king's variously adorned royal palace, to whatever place the <s>Dharma</s>-seat for the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk has been prepared upon the flower-strewn, purified, and variously adorned ground — there they shall be, for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: te vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavaṃścatvāro mahārājā anekairyakṣaśatasahasrairebhiśca sarvaiḥ sārdhaṃ samagrā bhaviṣyāmastasya manuṣyarājasya kalyāṇamitrasahāyakasya kalyāṇasaṃprāpakasyānuttaramahārasodāradāturanena dharmāmṛtarasena saṃtarpitāḥ saṃtarpya tasya manuṣyarājasyārakṣāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / tasya rājakulasya ca nagarasya ca viṣayasya ca rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyāmaṃ / tacca viṣayaṃ sarvopadravopasargopāyāsebhyaḥ parimocayiṣyāma iti //
body.translated_text: 'We, O Venerable Blessed One, the four great kings, together with many hundreds of thousands of <s>yakṣas</s> and all these [beings], shall be assembled, and having been satisfied by this nectar-taste of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmāmṛta-rasa</s>) — this noble, great, wondrous <s>rasa</s> given [by the preacher] who is a spiritual friend and guide to the good for that human king — having been satisfied, we shall provide protection for that human king: shelter, support, safeguarding, peace, and well-being. And we shall provide protection, shelter, support, safeguarding, peace, and well-being for his royal household, his city, and his domain. And we shall liberate that domain from all calamities, misfortunes, and tribulations.'

body.text: yaḥ kaścidbhadanta bhagavanmanuṣyarājo bhavet / yasya ca manuṣyarājasya viṣaye 'yaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ saṃpracaret / yadā cāsau bhadanta bhagavanmanuṣyarājaḥ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya
body.translated_text: 'Whatever human king there may be, O Venerable Blessed One, in whose domain this king of sūtras circulates — when, O Venerable Blessed One, that human king does not honor, does not respect, does not esteem, does not worship the monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers who bear this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>;'

body.text: dhārakān bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā na satkuryānna gurukuryānna mānayenna pūjayet / asmākaṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāmanekāni yakṣakoṭīniyutaśatasahassrāṇyanena dharmaśravaṇenainena dharmāmṛtarasena na saṃtarpayeranna pratimānayeran / imāni divyātmabhāvāni mahatā tejasā na vivardhayenna cāsmākaṃ vīryaṃ ca balaṃ ca saṃjanayet / tejaśca śriyaśca lakṣmīṃ cāsmākaṃ kāyeṣu na vivardhayet / na te 'pi vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavaṃścatvāro mahārājāḥ sabalaparivārā anekairyakṣakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraistasya ca viṣaye rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / bhadanta bhagavanviṣayamasmākamupekṣantaḥ sarvaviṣayavāsino devagaṇāstaṃ viṣayamupekṣyanti / devatāśca bhadanta bhagavantaṃ viṣayamupekṣyante //
body.translated_text: '[when he] would not satisfy or honor our many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>yakṣas</s>, [belonging to] us four great kings, with this hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> and this nectar-taste of the <s>Dharma</s>; would not increase these divine embodiments with great splendor; would not generate vigor, strength in us; would not cause splendor, glory, and prosperity to increase in our bodies — then we too, O Venerable Blessed One, the four great kings, together with our retinues and forces and many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>yakṣas</s>, shall not provide protection for that domain. O Venerable Blessed One, when we withdraw from that domain, all the divine hosts dwelling in every region shall also withdraw from that domain. And the deities too, O Venerable Blessed One, shall withdraw from that domain.'

body.text: tatra tatra viṣaye nānāvidhā viṣayalopā bhaviṣyanti / dāruṇāni ca rājasaṃkṣobhāni bhaviṣyanti / sarvaviṣayagatāni ca sattvāni kalahajātāni bhaviṣyanti / bhaṇḍanajātāni vigṛhītāni vivādamāpannāni nānāvidhāśca graharogā viṣaye prādurbhāviṣyanti / nānādigabhya āgatāścolkāpātāḥ prādurbhaviṣyanti / grahanakṣatrāṇi ca paraspareṇa viruddhāni bhaviṣyanti / sūryapratirūpakāṇi śaśina utpādayiṣyanti / candragrahāśca bhaviṣyanti / sūryagrahāśca satatasamitaṃ gaganāntaragatau sūryacandramasau no dṛkyathagatau bhaviṣyataḥ / ulkāpātasadṛśavarṇāni pariveśakāni gaganāntare kālena kālaṃ prādurbhaviṣyanti / pṛthivīkampāśca bhaviṣyanti / kūpāśca pṛthivīgatāḥ saṃkṣepantaḥ śokṣyanti / viṣamavātāśca vāsyanti / viṣamavarṣāśca bhaviṣyanti / durbhikṣakāntāraśca sarvaviṣaye bhaviṣyati / paracakrāṇi ca tadviṣayaṃ vekṣyanti / āyāsabahulaṃ bhaviṣyati / teṣāmasmākaṃ bhadanta bhagavaṃścaturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ sabalaparivārāṇāmanekeṣāṃ ca yakṣaśatasahasrāṇāṃ viṣayavāsināṃ ca devanāgānāṃ taṃ viṣayamupekṣatastatra viṣaya imānyevaṃ rūpāṇi nānāvidhānyupadravaśatāni bhaviṣyantyupadrasahasrāṇi vā //
body.translated_text: In those various regions, manifold devastations of the land will occur. There will be terrible royal disturbances. All beings throughout those regions will become engaged in quarrels, disputes, conflicts, and controversies. Various planetary diseases will appear in the land. Meteors falling from various directions will appear. The planets and constellations will be in mutual opposition. Mock suns will be produced by the moon. There will be lunar eclipses. There will be solar eclipses. Constantly and continuously, the sun and moon traversing the sky will not be visible. Halos resembling the color of falling meteors will appear in the sky from time to time. There will be earthquakes. Wells and underground water-sources will shrink and dry up. Irregular winds will blow. Irregular rains will fall. The desolation of famine will prevail throughout all the land. Foreign armies will eye that region. Affliction will be abundant. When we, O Venerable Blessed One—the four Great Kings with our retinues and forces, the many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, and the <s>devas</s> and <s>Nāgas</s> dwelling in that region—neglect that land, then in those regions such various hundreds and thousands of calamities will arise.

body.text: yaḥ kaścidbhadanta bhagavanmanuṣyarājo bhavet / ya ātmano mahatīmārakṣāṃ kartukāmo bhavet / ciraṃ ca nānāvidhāni rājasaukhyānyanubhavitukāmo bhavet / sarvasukhasamarpito na cireṇa rājatvaṃ kartukāmo bhavet / sarvaviṣayavāsināṃ ca sattvānāṃ sukhāpayitukāmo bhavet / sarvaparacakrāṇi ca parājayitukāmo bhavet / sarvasukhena viṣayaṃ paripālayitukāmo bhavet / dharmeṇa rājatvaṃ kārayitukāmo bhavet / svaviṣayaṃ ca sarvabhayopadravopasargopāyāsebhyaḥ parimocayitukāmo bhavet //
body.translated_text: 'Whatever human king there may be, O Venerable Blessed One, who desires to establish great protection for himself, who desires to experience various royal pleasures for a long time, who, endowed with all happiness, desires to exercise kingship for a long duration, who desires to bring happiness to all beings dwelling in all his domains, who desires to defeat all foreign armies, who desires to protect his realm with complete happiness, who desires to exercise kingship by <s>dharma</s>, and who desires to deliver his own domain from all fears, calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions—

body.text: tena ca bhadanta bhagavanmanuṣyarājenāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājaḥ śrotavyaḥ / śrutvā caitāstaddhārakā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ satkartavyā gurukartavyā mānayitavyāḥ pūjayitavyāḥ / vayaṃ catvāro mahārājāḥ sabalaparivārā anenaiva dharmaśravaṇakuśalamūlopacayenānena dharmākṛtarasena saṃtarpayitavyāḥ / asmākaṃ cemāni divyātmabhāvāni mahātejasā vivardhayitavyāni / tatkasya hatoḥ? yadbhadanta bhagavaṃstena manuṣyarājenāvaśyamayaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājaḥ śrotavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: that human king, O Venerable Blessed One, should listen to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>. Having listened, he should honor, respect, esteem, and worship those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold it. We, the four Great Kings with our retinues and forces, should be nourished by the accumulation of roots of merit from this <s>Dharma</s>-hearing—by the nectar-taste of the <s>Dharma</s>. These divine bodies of ours should be increased with great splendor. For what reason? Because, O Venerable Blessed One, that human king must necessarily listen to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.'

body.text: yāvanti bhadanta bhagavanbrahmendreṇa laukikalokottarāṇi ca nānāvidhāni śāstrāṇyupadarśitāni / yāvanti ca śakreṇa devendreṇa nānāvidhāni śāstrāṇyupadarśitāni / yāvanti ca nānāvidhaiḥ pañcabhijñai ṛṣirbhirlaukikalokottarāṇi ca sattvānāmarthāya śāstrāṇyupadarśitāni / bhadanta bhagavaṃstebhyo brahmendraśatasahasrebhyo 'nekebhyaśca śakrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrebhyaḥ sarvebhyaśca pañcābhijñebhya ṛṣikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrebhyastathāgato 'grataraśca viśiṣṭataraścemaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājaṃ vistareṇa sattvānāmarthāya saṃprakāśayitaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'As many worldly and supramundane treatises as <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Indra</s> has demonstrated, as many various treatises as <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of <s>devas</s>, has demonstrated, as many worldly and supramundane treatises as the various <s>ṛṣis</s> possessing the five supernatural knowledges (<s>pañcābhijña</s>) have demonstrated for the welfare of beings—O Venerable Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is more preeminent and more distinguished than those hundreds of thousands of <s>Brahmā-Indras</s>, than those many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of <s>Śakras</s>, and than all those hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of <s>ṛṣis</s> possessing the five supernatural knowledges. He has illuminated this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> at length for the welfare of beings.'

body.text: yathāyaṃ sarvajambudvīpagatānāṃ manuṣyarājānāṃ rājatvaṃ kārayitavyam / yathā ca sarvasattvāni sukhārpitāni bhaviṣyanti / yathā ca sarvaviṣayānutpīḍitāśca bhaviṣyantyakaṇṭakāḥ / yathā paracakrāṇi parājitāni bhaviṣyanti / parāṅmukhībhūtāni / yathā ca te viṣayā anupāyāsāśca / yathā ca sarvaviṣayadharmā anupāyāsāśca bhaviṣyantyanupadrutāśca / yathā ca tairmanuṣyarājaiḥ sveṣu viṣayeṣu mahatī dharmolkāḥ prajvalitā bhaviṣyantyādīpitāśca / yathā ca sarvadevatābhavanāni
body.translated_text: '[He has shown] how kingship is to be exercised by those human kings throughout <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; how all beings will be established in happiness; how all domains will be unoppressed and free from thorns; how foreign armies will be defeated and turned away; how those domains will be free from affliction; how all the laws of those domains will be free from affliction and unharassed; how those human kings will have great <s>Dharma</s>-torches blazing and kindled in their own domains; and how all the abodes of the deities

body.text: ādīpitāni bhaviṣyanti devairdevaputraiśca / yatha ca vayaṃ catvāro mahārājāḥ sabalaparivārā anekāni yakṣaśatasahasrāṇi sarvajambudvīpagatāśca devagaṇāḥ saṃtarpitā bhaviṣyanti saṃprasāditāśca / yathā cāsmākaṃ kāye mahāntaṃ vīryaṃ ca balaṃ ca sthāma ca saṃjanitaṃ bhaviṣyanti / yathā cāsmākaṃ kāye tejaśca śrīśca lakṣmīśca bhūyasyā mātrayābhiniciśanti / yathā ca sarvajambudvīpaḥ subhikṣo bhaviṣyati ramaṇīyaśca bahujanākīrṇamanuṣyaśca / yathā ca sarvajambudvīpagatāni sattvāni sarvasukhāni bhaviṣyanti / nānāratimanubhaviṣyanti / yathā ca sattvānyanekakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyayintyānyudārodārāṇi sukhānyanubhaviṣyanti / buddhaiśca bhagavadbhiḥ sārdhaṃ samavadhānagatāni bhaviṣyanti / anāgate 'dhvanyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / tatsarvametarhi bhagavatā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena mahatā kāruṇyabalādhiṣṭhānena śakrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi divyātirekatare 'nuttare tathāgatajñāne nānāvidhānekasarvapañcābhijñarṣigaṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi cātirekasamyaksaṃbuddhena brahmendrakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi cātirekavratatapo 'dhiṣṭhānena sa bhagavatā tathāgatonārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhenāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājo vistareṇa sarvasattvānāmarthāyeha jambudvīpe saṃprakāśitaḥ //
