body.translated_text: will be illuminated by <s>devas</s> and sons of <s>devas</s>; and how we, the four Great Kings with our retinues and forces, and the many hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, and the hosts of <s>devas</s> throughout <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, will be nourished and gladdened; and how great vigor, strength, and firmness will be generated in our bodies; and how splendor, glory, and fortune will increasingly enter our bodies; and how all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> will be prosperous, delightful, and teeming with many people; and how all beings throughout <s>Jambudvīpa</s> will be happy and will experience various delights; and how beings for innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> will experience noble and excellent pleasures; and will be in the presence of <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones; and in the future will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. All of this has now been illuminated at length by the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, through the empowerment of great compassion—[he who is] more preeminent than hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of <s>Śakras</s> in the unsurpassed, most excellent <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, more preeminent than hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of hosts of <s>ṛṣis</s> with various manifold five supernatural knowledges, and more preeminent than hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of <s>Brahmā-Indras</s> in [the power of] vows and austerities—by him, the Blessed One, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> has been illuminated at length for the welfare of all beings here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.'

body.text: tena manuṣyarājena sarvajambudvīpagatāni laukikalokottarāṇi rājakāryāṇi rājaśāsrāṇi rājakaraṇāni niryātāni / yairime sattvāḥ sukhino bhaviṣyanti / tāni sarvāṇi bhagavatā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhenāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāja upadarśitaḥ paridīpitaḥ saṃprakāśitaḥ / tena bhadanta bhagavanhetunā tena pratyayena ca tena manuṣyarājenāvaśyamāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājaḥ satkṛtya śrotavyaḥ satkṛtya mānayitavyaḥ satkṛtya pūjayitavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'By that human king, all the worldly and supramundane royal duties, royal ordinances, and royal acts throughout <s>Jambudvīpa</s> have been carried out—by which these beings will be happy. All of those have been demonstrated, elucidated, and illuminated by the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, through this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>. For that reason and for that cause, O Venerable Blessed One, that human king must necessarily listen to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> with reverence, honor it with reverence, and worship it with reverence.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavāṃścaturo mahārājānetadavocat / tena hi catvāro mahārājāḥ sabalaparivārā avaśyaṃ teṣāṃ manuṣyarājānāmasya suvarṇaprabhāsottamaya sūtrendrarājasya śrotṝṇāṃ pūjayitṝṇāṃ mahāntamautsukyaṃ kariṣyanti rakṣārtham etāśca mahārājāḥ sūtrendradhārakā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā buddhakṣetramārātpradarśante devamānuṣāsurasya lokasya buddhakṛtyāni
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the four Great Kings: 'Therefore, you four Great Kings with your retinues and forces must necessarily show great eagerness for the protection of those human kings who listen to and worship this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>. And, O Great Kings, those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this king of <s>sūtras</s> demonstrate the <s>Buddha</s>-field from afar to the world of <s>devas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>; they will perform the work of the <s>Buddha</s>

body.text: kariṣyanti / imaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti / avaśyaṃ yuṣmābhiścaturbhirmahārājaisteṣāṃ sūtrendredhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāmārakṣā kartavyā / paripālanaṃ paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kartavyam / yathā ca sūtrendradhārakā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā ārakṣitā bhaveyuranutpīḍitā anusargopāyāsāṃ sukhacittāḥ / imaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājaṃ vistareṇa sattvānāṃ saṃprakāśayitum //
body.translated_text: and will illuminate this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> at length. You four Great Kings must necessarily provide protection for those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this king of <s>sūtras</s>—protection, guardianship, rescue, shelter, removal of punishment, removal of weapons, and the blessing of peace and well-being—so that those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold the king of <s>sūtras</s> may be protected, unoppressed, free from misfortune and affliction, with minds at ease, in order to illuminate this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> at length for beings.'

body.text: atha khalu vaiśravaṇo mahārājo dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājo virūḍhako mahārājo virūpākṣo mahārājotthāyāsanebhya ekāṃsāni cīvarāṇi prāvṛtyottarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya tasyāṃ velāyāmabhimukhaṃ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirbhagavantamabhituṣṭuvuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the great king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the great king <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, the great king <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, and the great king <s>Virūpākṣa</s> rose from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder, placed their right knees upon the ground, and joining their palms in the direction of the Blessed One, at that moment praised the Blessed One face to face with fitting verses:

children.translated_text: Him whose body is as pure as the <s>Jina</s>-moon, resplendent as a thousand <s>Jina</s>-suns,
whose eyes are as spotless as the <s>Jina</s>-lotus, whose rows of teeth are as radiant as the <s>Jina</s>-night-lily washed in frost— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.1 //
the <s>Jina</s>-ocean, comparable to an ocean of <s>Jina</s>-virtues, a mine of manifold jewels,
filled with the waters of the stream of knowledge, pervaded by hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhis</s>— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.2 //
him whose feet are beautiful with the <s>Jina</s>-wheel pattern, resplendent on all sides like a thousand [suns],
whose hands and feet are beautifully webbed, like the webbed feet of the lord of swans— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.3 //
him who shines like a golden mountain, the <s>Jina</s>-mountain-lord, stainless as fine gold,
comparable to <s>Meru</s> in all virtues—we bow to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Jina</s>, lord of mountains! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.4 //
The <s>Tathāgata</s>-moon, like the moon in the sky, like the moon's reflection in water,
comparable to illusion and mirage—we bow to the stainless <s>Jina</s>! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.5 //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃścaturo mahārājāngāthābhirbabhāṣe //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the four Great Kings in verses:

children.translated_text: This—
this most excellent king of <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s> of the Ten-Powered Ones,
by you, the <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Guardians), it must be guarded ---------- // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.6 //
so that this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>, profound, bestowing happiness upon all beings,

children.text: sattvāna hitasukhārthaṃ ciraṃ ca pracarejjambūdvīpe 'smin // Suv_7.7 //
children.translated_text: for the welfare and happiness of beings, may circulate for a long time in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.7 //
And those beings in the <s>trisāhasra-mahāsāhasra</s> (triple-thousand great-thousand) world-system,
having pacified their sufferings of the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>) and the sufferings of hells— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.8 //

children.text: ye ceha jambudvipe gatā hi sarve rājānastu mahataḥ praharṣajātā /
children.translated_text: and all those kings here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, being filled with great joy,

children.text: dharmeṇa ca pālayantu viṣayā yenāyaṃ jambūdvīpaḥ kṣemaśca bhavet // Suv_7.9 //
children.translated_text: may they govern their domains by <s>dharma</s>, so that this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> may be at peace! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.9 //

children.text: sūbhikṣo ramaṇīyaḥ sarve jambūdvīpe sukhitāni bhavanti sarvasattvāni /
children.translated_text: Prosperous and delightful—may all beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> be happy!

children.text: yasyā nāsti narapaterviṣaye priyātmasaukhya prayatā ca rājatvam // Suv_7.10 //
children.translated_text: For a king in whose domain there is no self-cherishing happiness, devoted is his kingship. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.10 //

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ priyatā ca śrotavyastena sūtrarājaḥ paramaśatrukṣayakaram /
children.translated_text: Sovereignty and popularity [come from] listening to this king of <s>sūtras</s>, the supreme destroyer of enemies,
the repeller of foreign armies, the supreme dispeller of fear—this king of <s>sūtras</s> is supremely auspicious! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.11 //

children.text: yathā ratnavṛkṣaḥ surucirastu sarvaguṇasaṃbhavaḥ sugṛhaḥ saṃsthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a jewel-tree, most beautiful, the source of all virtues, stands firm in a good abode,
even so should this king of <s>sūtras</s> be regarded with respect to royal virtues and the rest. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.12 //

children.text: yathā śītalahimasalilaṃ dharmataṃ pratilabhata uṣṇa apaharaṇam /
children.translated_text: Just as cool snow-water, by its very nature, takes away heat,

children.text: tathaivāyaṃ sūtravarendro guṇasukhadātā bhavati narapatīnām // Suv_7.13 //
children.translated_text: even so this most excellent of <s>sūtras</s> bestows virtues and happiness upon kings. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.13 //
Just as a jewel-casket, a mine of all gems, rests in the palm of the hand,
even so is this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> for the hosts of kings. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.14 //
This king of <s>sūtras</s> is worshipped by the hosts of <s>devas</s> and bowed to by <s>Devendra</s>;
it is guarded by the four <s>Lokapālas</s> of great supernatural power. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.15 //
This king of <s>sūtras</s> is always blessed by the <s>Buddhas</s> dwelling in the ten directions;

children.text: sūtramidaṃ deśayataḥ sādhūkāra dadanti saṃbuddhāḥ // Suv_7.16 //
children.translated_text: to one who teaches this <s>sūtra</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones give their acclaim of 'Well done!' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 7.16 //

children.text: yakṣaśatasahasrāṇī rakṣanti ca viṣayaṃ daśasu diśāsu /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s> guard the domain in the ten directions,
they hear this king of <s>sūtras</s> with joyful and delighted minds. // Suv_7.17 //
The hosts of gods who have gone to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in secluded places —

children.text: te sarve devagaṇāḥ śṛṇvantu sūtramidaṃ pramuditāśca // Suv_7.18 //
children.translated_text: may all those hosts of gods hear this <s>sūtra</s> with delight! // Suv_7.18 //

children.text: tejobalaṃ vīryabalaṃ ca labhante tena dharmaśravaṇena /
children.translated_text: They obtain the power of radiance and the power of vigor through that hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>;
and with great splendor, the divine bodies shall increase. // Suv_7.19 //

body.text: atha khalu catvāro mahārājā bhagavato 'ntikādimā evaṃrūpā gāthāḥ śrutvāścaryaprāptā babhūvuradbhutaprāptā udvilyaprāptāstaddharmavegena muhūrtamātraṃ praruditā ivāśrūṇi ca pravartayāmāsuḥ / te ca saṃmānaiḥ śarīrai praphullibhiraṅgapratyaṅgairacintyena prītisukhasaumanasyena samanvāgatā bhūtvā punarapi bhagavantaṃ divyamāndāravaiḥ kusumairavakiranti sma / avakiritvā prakiritvotthāyāsanebhya ekāṃsāni cīvarāṇi prāvaritvā dakṣiṇāni jānumaṇḍalāni pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocan / vayamapi bhadanta bhagavaṃścatvāro mahārājā ekaiko mahārājo vayaṃ pañcayakṣaśataparivārā dharmamāṇakasya bhikṣoḥ sadānubaddhā bhaviṣyāmastaṃ dharmabhāṇakaṃ mānayanāya paripālanāya ceti //
body.translated_text: Then the Four Great Kings, having heard these verses from the presence of the Blessed One, were filled with wonder, amazement, and exultation. Carried by the force of that <s>Dharma</s>, for a brief moment they were as if weeping and shed tears. Then, with honored bodies, with limbs and secondary limbs blossoming forth, endowed with inconceivable joy, happiness, and gladness, they again showered the Blessed One with divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers. Having showered and scattered [flowers], they rose from their seats, arranged their robes over one shoulder, placed their right knees upon the ground, and joining their palms in the direction of the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'We too, Venerable Blessed One — we the Four Great Kings, each Great King with a retinue of five hundred <s>yakṣas</s> — shall always follow the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk, for the purpose of honoring and protecting that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher.'

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājo caturmahārāja parivarto nāma saptamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh chapter, the Chapter of the Four Great Kings (<s>Caturmahārājaparivarta</s>), in the supreme king of <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Sarasvatīdevīparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Chapter of the Goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> (<s>Sarasvatīdevīparivarta</s>) //

body.text: atha khalu sarasvatī mahādevyekāṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat / ahamapi bhadanta bhagavan sarasvatī mahādevī tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣorvākparibhūṣaṇārthāya pratibhāṇakamupasaṃhariṣyāmi / dhāraṇīṃ cānupradāsyāmi / suniruktatavarāṇāṃ bhāvaṃ saṃbhāvayiṣyāmi / mahāntaṃ ca dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣorjñānāvabhāsaṃ kariṣyāmi / yāni kāni citpadavyañjanānītaḥ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarājātparibhraṣṭāni bhaviṣyanti / vismaritāni ca tānyahaṃ sarvāṇi tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣoḥ suniruktatapadavyañjanānyupasaṃhariṣyāmi / dhāraṇīṃ cānupradāsyāmi smṛtyasaṃpramoṣaṇāya / yathā cāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājasteṣāṃ buddhasahasrāvaruptakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya ciraṃ jambudvīpe pracaret / na ca kṣipramantardhāpayet / anekāni ca sattvānīmaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ śrutvā cintya tīkṣṇaprajñā bhaveyuḥ / acintyaṃ ca jñānaskandhaṃ pratilabhante ca na duṣṭameva cāyuḥ / sampattiṃ pratilabheyuḥ / jātyanugrahaṃ cāparimitaṃ ca puṇyaskandhaṃ pratigṛhṇīyuḥ / sarvaśāstrakuśalāśca bhaveyurnānāśilpavidhijñāśca //
body.translated_text: Then the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, arranging her robe over one shoulder, placing her right knee upon the ground, and joining her palms in the direction of the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'I too, Venerable Blessed One — I, the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> — shall confer upon that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk the gift of eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>) for the adornment of his speech. I shall bestow a <s>dhāraṇī</s> upon him. I shall enhance in him the faculty of correct and excellent exposition. I shall create a great illumination of knowledge for that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk. Whatever syllables and phrases from this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> may have been lost or forgotten — all of those I shall restore to that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk as correctly and excellently articulated syllables and phrases. I shall bestow a <s>dhāraṇī</s> for the non-loss of memory. So that this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> may long circulate in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for the benefit of those beings whose roots of merit have been planted by thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, and may not quickly disappear. And many beings, having heard and contemplated this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>, shall become of sharp wisdom. They shall obtain an inconceivable aggregate of knowledge, and their lifespan shall not be corrupted. They shall obtain prosperity. They shall receive the blessing of [good] birth and an immeasurable aggregate of merit. They shall become skilled in all sciences and knowledgeable in various arts and crafts.'

body.text: tadidaṃ saṃyuktaṃ snānakarma bhāṣiṣyāmi tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣosteṣāṃ ca dharmaśravaṇikānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya / sarvagrahanakṣatrajanmamaraṇapīḍā kalikalahakaluṣaḍimbaḍamaraduḥkhapnaviṣodakapīḍāḥ / sarvakākhordavetālāḥ praśamaṃ yāsyanti /
body.translated_text: 'I shall now speak this connected bathing ritual (<s>snānakarma</s>) for the benefit of that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk and for the benefit of those beings who hear the <s>Dharma</s>. All afflictions caused by planets, constellations, birth, and death; the afflictions of strife, quarrel, impurity, tumult, uproar, suffering, bad dreams, poison, and water — all <s>kākhordas</s> and <s>vetālas</s> shall be pacified.'

children.text: auṣadhayo mantrā yena snāpayanti ca paṇḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The herbs and <s>mantras</s> with which the wise perform the bathing [ritual]:'

children.text: vacā gorocanā spṛkā śirīṣaṃ śyābhyakaṃ śamī /
children.translated_text: <s>Vacā</s> (sweet flag), <s>gorocanā</s> (cow-bezoar), <s>spṛkkā</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s> (silk tree), <s>śyābhyaka</s>, and <s>śamī</s> (acacia),
<s>indrahastā</s>, auspicious <s>vyāmaka</s>, <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood), and bark; // Suv_8.1 //
<s>nīveṣṭaka</s>, <s>sarja</s>-resin, frankincense (<s>sihlaka</s>), and <s>guggulu</s>-resin,

children.text: tagaraṃ patraśaileyaṃ candanaṃ ca manaḥśilā // Suv_8.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>tagara</s> (rosebay), <s>patra</s> (cinnamon leaf), <s>śaileya</s> (lichen), sandalwood (<s>candana</s>), and realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>); // Suv_8.2 //

children.text: samocakaṃ turuṣkaṃ ca kuṅkumaṃ musta sarṣapāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>samocaka</s>, <s>turuṣka</s> (olibanum), saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>), <s>musta</s> (cyperus), mustard seeds (<s>sarṣapa</s>),

children.text: naradaṃ cavya sūkṣmelā uśīraṃ nāgakeśaram // Suv_8.3 //
children.translated_text: spikenard (<s>narada</s>), <s>cavya</s> (long pepper root), cardamom (<s>sūkṣmelā</s>), vetiver (<s>uśīra</s>), and ironwood flower (<s>nāgakeśara</s>); // Suv_8.3 //
these, in equal portions, one should grind under the <s>Puṣya</s> constellation;
with these <s>mantra</s>-words, one should consecrate the powder a hundred times. // Suv_8.4 //

body.text: tadyathā / sukṛte karajātabhāge haṃsaraṇḍe indrajālamalilaka upasade avatāsike kutra kukalavimalamati śīlamati saṃdhibudhamati śiśiri satyasthita svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Tadyathā: sukṛte karajātabhāge haṃsaraṇḍe indrajālamalilaka upasade avatāsike kutra kukalavimalamati śīlamati saṃdhibudhamati śiśiri satyasthita svāhā</s>.

children.translated_text: Having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> of cow-dung, one should place loose flowers upon it;
in a golden vessel or silver vessel, one should set [the powder] with honey. // Suv_8.5 //
Four armored men should be stationed there;
four well-adorned maidens bearing water-pots should be placed [there]. // Suv_8.6 //
Constantly burning <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) as incense, one should arrange the five musical instruments;
and that goddess [image] should be adorned with parasols, banners, and flags. // Suv_8.7 //
Mirrors, arrows, and lances should be arranged around [the boundary];
then one should establish the boundary (<s>sīmābandha</s>), and afterward commence the ritual.
With the following sequence of <s>mantra</s>-words, one should establish the boundary: // Suv_8.8 //

body.text: syādyathedam / ane nayane hili hili gili khile svāhā // bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ snātvānena mantrajāpena snānaśāntiṃ yojayet / tadyathā / sugate vigate vigatāvati svāhā /
body.translated_text: It is as follows: <s>ane nayane hili hili gili khile svāhā</s>. Having bathed behind [the image of] the Blessed One, one should perform the bathing-pacification with this <s>mantra</s> recitation. <s>Tadyathā: sugate vigate vigatāvati svāhā</s>.

children.text: ye prasthitā nakṣatrā āyuḥ pālayantu caturdiśe /
children.translated_text: May the constellations that have arisen protect the lifespan in the four directions!
Whether it be afflictions from constellations and birth, or the fearful [effects] of zodiacal <s>karma</s>,
those arising from disturbance of the bodily humors — may the terrible fears be pacified! // Suv_8.9 //

body.text: same viṣame svāhā / sugate svāhā / sāgarasaṃbhūtāya svāhā // skandhamārutāya svāhā / nīlakaṇṭhāya svāhā / aparāhitavīryāya svāhā / himavatsaṃbhūtāya svāhā / animiṣacakrāya
body.translated_text: <s>Same viṣame svāhā. Sugate svāhā. Sāgarasaṃbhūtāya svāhā. Skandhamārutāya svāhā. Nīlakaṇṭhāya svāhā. Aparāhitavīryāya svāhā. Himavatsaṃbhūtāya svāhā. Animiṣacakrāya</s>

body.text: svāhā / namo bhagavatyai brāhmaṇyai namaḥ sarasvatyai devyai sidhyantu mantrapadāstaṃ brahma namasyantu svāhā /
body.translated_text: <s>svāhā. Namo bhagavatyai brāhmaṇyai. Namaḥ Sarasvatyai devyai. Sidhyantu mantrapadāḥ. Taṃ brahma namasyantu svāhā</s>.

body.text: etena snānakarmaṇā tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhakṣorarthāya teṣāṃ ca dharmaśravaṇikānāṃ lekhakānāmārthāya svayamevāhaṃ tatra gagaṇasiddhayakṣadevagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ tatra ca grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā vihāre vā sarvato rogapraśamanaṃ kariṣyāmi / sarvagrahakalikaluṣanakṣatrajanmapīḍānvā duḥkhasvapnavināyakapīḍānsarvakākhordavetālānpraśamayiṣyāmi / yathā teṣāṃ sūtrendradhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāṃ jīvitānugraho bhavet / saṃsāranirvāṇaṃ pratilabheyuḥ / avaivartikāśca bhaveyuranuttarāyāḥ samyak saṃbodheḥ //
body.translated_text: 'By this bathing ritual, for the benefit of that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk and for the benefit of those beings who hear the <s>Dharma</s> and the scribes, I myself, together with the hosts of sky-dwelling <s>siddhas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>devas</s>, in that village, city, market-town, or monastery, shall effect the pacification of all diseases everywhere. I shall pacify all afflictions from planets, strife, impurity, constellations, birth, bad dreams, and <s>Vināyaka</s>-spirits, and all <s>kākhordas</s> and <s>vetālas</s>. So that for those upholders of the king of <s>sūtras</s> — monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen — there may be the blessing of life. May they attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> from <s>saṃsāra</s>. And may they become irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) in unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>).'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānsarasvatyai mahādevyai sādhukāramadāt / sādhu sādhu sarasvati mahādevi bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya pratipanno yattvayā hīmāni mantroṣadhisaṃyuktāni bhāṣitāni / sā ca sarasvatī mahādevī bhagavataḥ pādāvabhivandanāṃ kṛtvaikānte niṣaṇṇā //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, great goddess! You have set forth, for the benefit and happiness of the many, these [teachings] connected with <s>mantras</s> and medicinal herbs.' And the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, having bowed at the feet of the Blessed One, sat down to one side.

body.text: atha khalvācāryavyākaraṇaprāptaḥ kauṇḍinyo mahābrāhmaṇastāṃ sarasvatīmāvāhayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, who had received the teacher's prediction, invoked that <s>Sarasvatī</s>:

children.translated_text: '<s>Sarasvatī</s>, the great goddess, worthy of worship, of great austerity,
renowned in all the worlds, a grantor of boons, of great virtues! // Suv_8.10 //
Dwelling on the peak, radiant, clad in a garment of <s>darbha</s>-grass,
she wears an auspicious garment and stands on one foot. // Suv_8.11 //
May all the gods, having assembled, [speak] this word of the <s>sūtra</s> —

children.text: jihvābhimukhaṃ ca sattvānāṃ bhāṣantu vacanaṃ śubham // Suv_8.12 //
children.translated_text: may they speak auspicious words face-to-face upon the tongues of beings! // Suv_8.12 //

body.text: syādyathedam / sure vire araje arajavati hi gule piṅgale piṅgale vatimukhe marīcisumati diśamati agrāmagrītalavitale ca vaḍivicarī mariṇipāṇaye lokajyeṣṭhake priyasiddhivrate bhīmamukhiśacivarī apratihate apratihatabuddhi namuci namuci mahādevi pratigṛhṇa namaskāra / sarvasattvānāṃ buddhirapratihatā bhavatu vidyā me siddhyatu śāsralokatantrapiṭakakāvyādiṣu /
body.translated_text: It is as follows: <s>sure vire araje arajavati hi gule piṅgale piṅgale vatimukhe marīcisumati diśamati agrāmagrītalavitale ca vaḍivicarī mariṇipāṇaye lokajyeṣṭhake priyasiddhivrate bhīmamukhiśacivarī apratihate apratihatabuddhi namuci namuci mahādevi pratigṛhṇa namaskāra</s>. May the intellect of all beings be unobstructed! May my knowledge be accomplished in the <s>śāstras</s>, worldly [sciences], <s>tantras</s>, <s>piṭakas</s>, <s>kāvya</s>, and the rest!

body.text: tadyathā / mahāprabhāve hili hili mili mili / vicaratu mama vicaratu me māyā sarvasattvānāṃ ca bhagavatyā devyāḥ sarasvatyā anubhāvena kadārake yuvati hili mili āvāhayāmi mahādevi buddhasatyena dharmasatyena saṃghasatyena indrasatyena varuṇasatyena ye loke satyavādinaḥ santi / tena teṣāṃ satyavacena āvāhayāmi mahādevi / hili hili mili vicarantu mama mantrino māyā sarvasattvānām / namo bhagavatyai sarasvatyai siddhyantu mantrapadāḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Tadyathā: mahāprabhāve hili hili mili mili</s>. May [eloquence] move through me, may my power move, and [the power] of all beings, by the majesty of the blessed goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>! <s>Kadārake yuvati hili mili</s> — I invoke you, O great goddess, by the truth of the <s>Buddha</s>, by the truth of the <s>Dharma</s>, by the truth of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, by the truth of <s>Indra</s>, by the truth of <s>Varuṇa</s>, and by those in the world who are speakers of truth — by the truth-word of those [truthful ones], I invoke you, O great goddess! <s>Hili hili mili</s> — may the power of my <s>mantras</s> move among all beings! Homage to the blessed goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>! May the <s>mantra</s>-words be accomplished! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

body.text: athācāryavyākaraṇaprāptaḥ kauḍinyo mahābrāhmaṇaḥ sarasvatīṃ mahādevīmimābhirgāthābhirabhyastāvīt //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, who had received the teacher's prediction, praised the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> with these verses:

body.text:
śṛṇvantu me bhūtagaṇā hi sarve stoṣyāmi devīṃ pravarottamacāruvaktrām /
yā mātṛgrāme pravarāgradevī / sadevagandharvasurendraloke // Suv_8.13 //
body.translated_text: 'May all the hosts of beings hear me! I shall praise the goddess of supremely excellent, beautiful face, who is the foremost and chief goddess among women, in the world of <s>devas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and the lord of the gods! // Suv_8.13 //

children.translated_text: Varied and marvelous, with beautifully adorned limbs — <s>Sarasvatī</s> by name, of wide eyes,
radiant with merit, endowed with the qualities of knowledge, supremely beautiful in varied and wonderful [forms]! // Suv_8.14 //
I shall praise her with distinguished qualities of speech — she who brings about accomplishment, the supremely excellent one,
the most praiseworthy of beings, a mine of virtues, supremely stainless, radiant like a lotus! // Suv_8.15 //

body.text:
sulocanāyai nayanottamāyai śubhāaśrayāyai śubhadeśanāyai /
guṇairacintyaiḥ samalaṃkṛtāyai / candropamāyai vimalaprabhāyai // Suv_8.16 //
body.translated_text: To her of beautiful eyes, of supreme vision, of auspicious abode, of auspicious teaching, adorned with inconceivable virtues, like the moon, of stainless radiance! // Suv_8.16 //

body.text: jñānākarāyai smṛtisamagratāyai siṃhottamāyai naravāhanāyai /
body.translated_text: To her who is a mine of knowledge, of complete mindfulness, supreme as a lioness, whose vehicle is a man (<s>naravāhana</s>),

body.text: ratnamaṇibāhusamalaṃkṛtāyai pūrṇaśaśāṅkopamadarśanāyai // Suv_8.17 //
body.translated_text: whose arms are adorned with jewels and gems, whose appearance is like the full moon! // Suv_8.17 //

children.translated_text: To her of pleasing speech, of gentle voice, endowed with profound wisdom,
of excellent goodness in accomplishing the foremost tasks, bowed to and worshipped by <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s>,
bowed to by the abodes of all hosts of <s>suras</s> and <s>asuras</s>, always worshipped by the hosts of beings! // Suv_8.18 //

body.text: namaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: Homage! <s>Svāhā</s>!

body.text: he 'haṃ devi namaste sā me prayacchatu guṇa augham //
body.translated_text: O goddess, I salute you! May she grant me a flood of virtues!

children.translated_text: May she bestow distinguished accomplishment upon all beings in all undertakings!

children.text: nityaṃ ca rakṣatū māṃ sarvānsattvāṃśca śatrumadhye // Suv_8.19 //
children.translated_text: May she always protect me and all beings in the midst of enemies!' // Suv_8.19 //
These complete sentences with their full syllables — rising at dawn, one of great energy should recite [them];

children.text: sarvābhiprāye dhanadhānyalābhī siddhiṃ ca prāpnoti śivāmudārāmiti // Suv_8.20 //
children.translated_text: for all [one's] desires, one obtains wealth and grain, and attains auspicious and noble accomplishment. // Suv_8.20 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje sarasvatīdevīparivarto nāmāṣṭamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eighth chapter, the Chapter of the Goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> (<s>Sarasvatīdevīparivarta</s>), in the supreme king of <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Śrīmahādevīparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Chapter of the Great Goddess <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Śrīmahādevīparivarta</s>) //

body.text: atha khalu śrīrmahādevī bhagavantaṃ praṇamyaitadavocat / ahamapi bhadanta bhagavanbhagavatī śrīrmahādevī tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣorautsukyatāṃ kariṣyāmi / yadidaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārairanyaiścopakaraṇairyathā sa dharmabhāṇakaḥ sarvopakaraṇasaṃpanno bhaviṣyati / avaikalpatāṃ ca pratilapsyate / svasthacitto bhaviṣyati / sukhacitto rātriṃ divā pratināmayiṣyati / itaśca suvarṇaprabhāsottamātsūtrendrarājānnānāvidhāni padavyañjanānyupanāmayiṣyati / vyupaparīkṣiṣyati / yenāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājasteṣāṃ buddhasahasrāvaruptakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya ciraṃ jambudvīpe pracatiṣyati / na ca kṣipramantardhāsyati / santi sattvāḥ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ / anekāni ca kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyacintyāni divyamānuṣyakāni sukhāni pratyanubhaveyuḥ / durbhikṣaścāntardhāpayet / subhikṣaśca prādurbhavet / sattvāśca manuṣyasukhopadhānena sukhitā bhaveyuḥ / tathāgatasamavadhānagatāśca bhaveyuḥ / anāgate 'dhvati cānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbodhayeyuḥ / sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokaduḥkhānyatyantasamucchinnāni bhaveyuriti //
body.translated_text: Then the glorious great goddess <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, having bowed to the Blessed One, said this: 'I too, Venerable Blessed One — I, the glorious great goddess <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, shall create eagerness in that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk — namely, with robes, almsfood, bedding, seats, medicine as requisites for illness, and other provisions, so that the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher shall be endowed with all provisions. He shall obtain freedom from want. He shall be of sound mind. He shall pass night and day with a happy mind. And furthermore, I shall bring forth from this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, various words and letters. I shall examine [them]. So that this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, for the benefit of those beings whose roots of merit have been planted under a thousand <s>Buddhas</s>, shall long circulate in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and shall not quickly disappear. There are beings who would hear this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, and would experience inconceivable divine and human pleasures for many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. Famine would disappear, and abundance would manifest. Beings would become happy through the endowment of human happiness. They would come into the presence of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And in the future time, they would fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). All the sufferings of the hells, animal births, and the world of <s>Yama</s> would be utterly and completely cut off.'

body.text: raktakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrīrnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / yatra śriyā mahādevyā mayā kuśalamūlamavaruptam / yenaitarhi yāṃ yāṃ diśaṃ sattvānāṃ viharati / yāṃ yāṃ diśaṃ sattvānyavalokayati / yāṃ yāṃ diśamupasaṃkramati / tasyāṃ tasyāṃ diśyanekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi sarvasukhopadhānena sukhitāni bhaviṣyanti / avaikalpatāṃ ca pratilapsyante / annena vā pānena vā dhanena vā dhānyena vā hiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktavaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatādibhiranyaiścopakaraṇaiḥ sarvopakaraṇasamṛddhāni sattvāni bhaviṣyanti śriyo mahādevyāḥ prabhāvena / tasya ca tathāgatasya pūjā kartavyā / gandhāśca puṣpāśca dhūpāśca dīpāśca dātavyāḥ / śriyo devyāstriṣkṛto nāmadheyamuccārayitavyam / tasyāśca gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ dātavyam / rasavihārā nikṣeptavyāni / tasya mahādravyarāśirvivardhate / tatredamucyate //
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Raktakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrī</s> — under him, I, <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, planted roots of merit. By that [merit], now, in whatever direction he dwells among beings, in whatever direction he looks upon beings, to whatever direction he approaches — in each of those directions, many hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭīs</s> of beings shall be made happy with all the endowments of happiness. They shall obtain freedom from want — with food, drink, wealth, grain, gold, silver, gems, pearls, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, refined gold, silver, and other provisions, beings shall be endowed with the prosperity of all provisions, through the majesty of <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>. And worship should be performed for that <s>Tathāgata</s>. Incenses, flowers, fragrances, and lamps should be offered. The name of the goddess <s>Śrī</s> should be pronounced three times. And to her, incense, flowers, fragrance, and lamps should be offered. Savory delicacies should be set down [as offerings]. That great heap of wealth increases. In this regard, it is said:' //

body.text: vivardhata dharaṇī raso dharaṇyā praharṣitā /
body.translated_text: The essence of the earth increases; the earth is delighted.

body.text: bhonti ca devatā sadā phalaśasyacitopamam /
body.translated_text: The deities are always [pleased]; [the harvest is] equal to fruit-and-grain-laden [trees].

body.text: vṛkṣadevatā rohanti śasyāni sucitrabhāvāḥ // Suv_9.1 //
body.translated_text: The tree-deities grow, the crops [appear] with marvelously beautiful forms. // Suv_9.1 //

body.text: suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya nāmadheyamuccārayitavyam / tānsattvāñchrīrmahādevīsamanvāhariṣyati / teṣāṃ ca mahatīṃ śriyaṃ kariṣyati //
body.translated_text: 'The name of this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, should be pronounced. And <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> shall attend to those beings and shall create great prosperity for them.' //

body.text: alakāvatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ puṇyakusumaprabhodyānavane suvarṇavarṇadhvajanāmni saptaratnaprabhavane śrīrmahādevī prativasati sma / yaḥ kaścitpuruṣo dhānyarāśiṃ vivardhayitukāmo bhavet / tena svagṛhaṃ suśodhayitavyam / śuciśvetavasraprāvṛtena sugandhavasanadhāriṇā bhavitavyam / namastasya bhagavato ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśriyastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya triṣkṛtvo nāmadheyamuccārayitavyam / śriyā mahādevyā hastena tasya pūjā kartavyā / puṣpadhūpagandhāśca dātavyāḥ / nānārasavihārāśca nikṣeptavyāḥ / tasya ca suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasyānubhāvena tena kālena śrīrmahādevī tasya gṛha samanvāhariṣyati / tasya ca mahādhānyarāśiṃ vivardhayiṣyati / tena śrīrmahādevīmāvāhayitukāmeneme vidyāmantrāḥ smarayitavyāḥ / tadyathā / namaḥ sarvabuddhānāmatītānāgatapratyutpannānām / namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām / namo maitreyaprabhṛtīnāṃ bodhisattvānām / teṣāṃ namaskṛtya vidyāṃ prayojayāmi iyaṃ me vidyā samṛdhyatu / syādyathedam / pratipūrṇavare samantagate / mahākāryapratiprāpaṇe sattvārthasamatānuprapure / āyānadharmitā mahābhāgine / mahātejopamaṃ hite / ṛṣisaṃgṛhīte / samayānupālane //
body.translated_text: 'In the royal capital <s>Alakāvatī</s>, in the garden-grove named <s>Puṇyakusumaprabha</s>, in the grove of the seven jewels named <s>Suvarṇavarṇadhvaja</s>, <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> dwelt. Whatever person wishes to increase his heap of grain — he should clean his own house well. He should be clothed in pure white garments and should wear fragrant clothing. He should pronounce three times the name of the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrī</s>. Worship should be performed for <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> with [one's own] hand. Flowers, incense, and fragrances should be offered. Various savory delicacies should be set down. And by the power of this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, at that time <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> shall attend to his house and shall increase his great heap of grain. By one who wishes to invoke <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, these <s>vidyā</s>-<s>mantras</s> should be recited — namely: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present! Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! Homage to <s>Maitreya</s> and the other <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! Having paid homage to them, I employ the <s>vidyā</s>; may this <s>vidyā</s> of mine succeed! May it be thus: <s>Pratipūrṇavare samantagate, mahākāryapratiprāpaṇe sattvārthasamatānuprapure, āyānadharmitā mahābhāgine, mahātejopamaṃ hite, ṛṣisaṃgṛhīte, samayānupālane</s>.' //

body.text: ime mūrdhābhiṣekadharmatā mantrapadāḥ / ekā śaśipadā avisaṃvādanā mantrapadāḥ / samavadhāribhiravaruptakuśalamūlaiḥ prāvṛtadhārayamāṇaiḥ sa saptavarṣā aṣṭāṅgopetā sapañcāsina pūrvāhṇe / aparāhṇe / sarvabuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ puṣpadhūpagandhapūjāṃ kṛtvātmanaśca sarvasattvānāṃ ca sarvajñajñānasya paripūraṇāya / tena sarve cābhiprāyāḥ samṛdhyantu // kṣipraṃ samṛdhyantu / tadgṛhaṃ sa caukṣaṃ kṛtvā vihāraṃ cāraṇyāyatanaṃ vāṃ gomayena maṇḍalakaṃ kṛtvā gandhapuṣpadhūpaṃ ca dātavyam / caukṣamāsanaṃ
body.translated_text: 'These are the <s>mantra</s>-words of the consecration (<s>mūrdhābhiṣeka</s>) teaching. [These are] the unfailing <s>mantra</s>-words of the single lunar <s>pada</s>. They are to be covered and maintained by those who have planted roots of merit in the presence of [the <s>Buddhas</s>]. [The ritual is:] seven years of the eightfold [fast], with the fifty [recitations], in the forenoon and afternoon. Having performed worship with flowers, incense, and fragrances to all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, for the fulfillment of omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajña-jñāna</s>) for oneself and all beings — by this, may all aspirations be fulfilled! May they quickly be fulfilled! Having cleaned that house, or having made a <s>maṇḍala</s> with cow-dung in a monastery or forest-hermitage, incense, flowers, and fragrance should be offered. A clean seat'

body.text: prajñapayitavyam / puṣpā avakīrṇantu mitavyam / tatastatkṣaṇaṃ śrīrmahādevī praviśitvā tatra sthāsyati / tadupādāya tatra gṛhe vā grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā vihāre vāraṇyāyatane vā na jātu kenacidvaikalpaṃ kariṣyati / hiraṇyena vā suvarṇena vā ratnena vā dhanena vā dhānyādisarvopakaraṇasamṛddhābhioḥ sarvasukhopadhānena sukhitāni bhaviṣyanti / kuśalamūlaśca dhriyate / tena sarvaṃ śriyo mahādevyāḥ premaprabhāvapreṣaṇaṃ dātavyaṃ yāvajjīvaṃ tatropasthāsyati na vilambiṣyati / sarvābhiprāyāṃścaiṣāṃ paripūrayiṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: 'should be arranged. Flowers should be scattered. Then, at that very moment, <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, having entered, shall stand there. From that [moment] onward, in that house, or village, or city, or market-town, or monastery, or forest-hermitage, no one shall ever cause any want. With gold, silver, jewels, wealth, grain, and all other provisions, beings shall be endowed with the prosperity of all provisions, and shall be made happy with all the endowments of happiness — through the power of <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>. And roots of merit shall be maintained. By one [who wishes to invoke her], all offerings of love, power, and service to <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> should be given; she shall be present there as long as [one] lives, and shall not delay. And she shall fulfill all their aspirations.' //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje śrīmahādevīparivarto nāma navamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the ninth chapter, the <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s> Chapter, in the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Sarvabuddhabodhisattvanāmasaṃdhāraṇiparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Chapter on the <s>Dhāraṇī</s> for Retaining the Names of All <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> //

body.text: om namo bhagavate ratnaśikhinaḥ tathāgatasya / namaḥ suvarṇaratnākaracchatraskūṭasya tathāgatasya / namaḥ suvarṇapuṣpajvalaraśmiketostathāgatasya / namo mahāpradīpasya tathāgatasya / ruciraketurnāma bodhisattvaḥ / suvarṇaprabhāsottamo nāma bodhisattvaḥ / suvarṇagandho nāma bodhisattvaḥ / sadāprarudito nāma bodhisattvaḥ / dharmodgato nāma bodhisattvaḥ / purasthimenākṣobhyonāma tathāgataḥ / dakṣiṇena ratnaketurnāma tathāgataḥ / paścimenāmitāyurnāma tathāgataḥ / uttare dundubhisvaro nāma tathāgataḥ / suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāja imāni bodhisattvanāmāni ye dhārayanti vācayanti te bodhisattvā nityaṃ jātismarā bhontīti //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Homage to the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>. Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇaratnākaracchatraskūṭa</s>. Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇapuṣpajvalaraśmiketu</s>. Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Mahāpradīpa</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Ruciraketu</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Suvarṇagandha</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Sadāprarudita</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Dharmodgata</s>. In the east, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Akṣobhya</s>. In the south, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnaketu</s>. In the west, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitāyus</s>. In the north, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dundubhisvara</s>. Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who retain and recite these names of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> from the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, shall always remember their past births. //

body.text: iti śrīsuparṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje sarvabuddhabodhisattvanāma saṃdhāraṇioparivarto nāma daśamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the tenth chapter, the Chapter on the <s>Dhāraṇī</s> for Retaining the Names of All <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Dṛḍhāpṛthivīdevatāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Chapter of <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, the Earth Deity //

body.text: atha khalu dṛḍhā pṛthivīdevatā bhagavantametadavocat / ayaṃ bhadanta bhagavansuvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarāja etarhi cānāgate 'dhvani yatra grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā janapade vāraṇyapradeśe vā girikandare vā rājakule vopasaṃkramiṣyati / yatrāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājo vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati / yatra yatra bhagavanpṛthivīpradeśe tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣo ṛjukāyagatasya dharmāsanaprajñaptaṃ bhaviṣyati / yatra yatrāsane dharmabhāṇako niṣadyemaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyati / tatrāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavandṛḍhā pṛthivīdevatā teṣu pṛthivīpradeśeṣvāgamiṣyāmi / atra dharmāsanagato 'smyadṛśyamānenātmabhāvenottamāṅgena ca tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣoḥ pādatalau pratisaṃhariṣyāmi / ātmānaṃ cānena dharmaśravaṇena dharmāmṛtarasena saṃtarpayiṣyāmi / saṃpratimānayiṣyāmi saṃpūjayiṣyāmi / ātmānaṃ ca saṃtarpayitvā pratimānayitvā saṃpraharṣayitvemamaṣṭaṣaṣṭiyojanasahasrāṇi pṛthivīskandhamātmānaṃ cānena dharmaśravaṇena dharmāmṛtarasena yāvadvajramayaṃ pṛthivītalamupādāya pṛthivīrasenavivardhayiṣyāmi saṃpratimānayiṣyāmi paripūrayiṣyāmi / uparitaścemaṃ samudraparyantaṃ pṛthivītalamupādāya pṛthivīmaṇḍalaṃ snigdhena pṛthivīrasena snehayiṣyāmi / ojasvitarāṃ cemāṃ mahāpṛthivīṃ kariṣyāmi / yenāsmiñjambudvīpe nānātṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspataya ojasvitarāḥ prarohayiṣyanti / sarvārāmanavṛkṣasasyāni ca nānāvidhānyojasvitarāṇi bhaviṣyanti / gandhatarāṇi snigdhatarāṇyāsvadanīyāni darśanīyatarāṇi mahottarāṇi ca bhaviṣyanti / te ca sattvāstāni pānabhojanāni nānāvidhānyupabhuktvā āyurbalavarṇendriyāṇi vivardhayiṣyanti / tejobalavarṇarūpasamanvāuatāśca bhūtvā nānāvidhāni pṛthivīgatānyanekāni nānākāryaśatasahasrāṇi kariṣyantyutthāsyanti vyāpayiṣyanti / balakaraṇīyāni karmāṇi kariṣyanti //
body.translated_text: Then the earth deity <s>Dṛḍhā</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'This, Venerable Blessed One — this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, now and in the future time, wherever it shall come — in a village, city, market-town, district, forest region, mountain cave, or royal household — wherever this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, shall be expounded at length; wherever, O Blessed One, in whatever spot of earth, a <s>Dharma</s>-seat shall be prepared for that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk sitting upright; wherever that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, seated upon his seat, shall expound at length this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s> — there, Venerable Blessed One, I, <s>Dṛḍhā</s> the earth deity, shall come to those spots of earth. Being beneath the <s>Dharma</s>-seat with an invisible body, with the crown of my head I shall receive the soles of the feet of that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk. And I shall satisfy myself with this hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>, with this nectar-taste of the <s>Dharma</s>. I shall honor, worship, and delight myself. And having satisfied, honored, and delighted myself, I shall increase, honor, and replenish this earth-mass of sixty-eight thousand <s>yojanas</s>, down to the diamond-base (<s>vajramaya</s>) ground-level, with the earth's essence through this hearing of the <s>Dharma</s> and this nectar-taste of the <s>Dharma</s>. And from above, beginning from the ocean-bounded surface of the earth, I shall moisten the earth-circle with rich earth-essence. And I shall make this great earth more vigorous, so that in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, various grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees shall sprout forth more vigorously. All garden trees and crops of various kinds shall become more vigorous, more fragrant, richer, more savory, more beautiful to behold, and greater. And those beings, having consumed those various foods and drinks, shall increase in lifespan, strength, complexion, and faculties. Endowed with radiance, strength, complexion, and beauty, they shall arise to carry out various and many hundreds of thousands of undertakings upon the earth. They shall engage in them and accomplish them. They shall perform deeds requiring strength.' //

body.text: tena hetunā bhadanta bhagavansarvajambudvīpaḥ kṣemaśca bhaviṣyati / subhikṣaśca sphītaścarddhaśca ramaṇīyaśca bahujanākīrṇamanuṣyaśca bhaviṣyati / sarvajambudvīpe ca sattvāni sukhitāni bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: 'For this reason, Venerable Blessed One, all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> shall be peaceful, abundant, prosperous, flourishing, delightful, and teeming with many people.'

body.text: nānāvicitrāṃ ratimanubhaviṣyanti / tāni sattvāni tejobalavarṇarūpasamanvāgatāni ca bhaviṣyanti / asya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasyārthāya teṣāṃ sūtrendradhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānaṃ dharmāsanagatānāmantikamupasaṃkrameyuḥ / upasaṃkramitvā tāni prasannacittāni sarvasattvānāmarthāya hitāya sukhāya tāndharmabhāṇakānadhyeṣayeyusya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya prakāśataḥ / ahaṃ dṛḍhā pṛthivīdevatā saparivāraujasvitarā ca bhaviṣyāmi / tena bhadanta bhagavaṃścāsmākaṃ kāye mahābalavī ryasthāmasaṃjanitaṃ bhaviṣyati / tejaśca śrīśca lakṣmīścāsmākaṃ kāyamāvekṣyanti / mayi ca bhadanta bhagavandṛḍhāyāṃ pṛthivīdevatāyāmanena dharmāmṛtarasena saṃtarpitāyāṃ mahātejobalavīryasthāmavegapratilabdhāyāmiyaṃ mahāpṛthivī saptayojanasāhasrikāyaṃ jambudvīpo mahatā pṛthivīrasena vivardhayiṣyati / ojasvitarā ca mahāpṛthivī bhaviṣyati / imāni ca bhadanta bhagana sarvasattvāni pṛthivīsaṃniśritāni vṛddhivirūḍhivaipulyatāṃ ca gamiṣyanti / mahanti ca bhaviṣyanti / mahanti ca bhūtvā sarvasattvāni pṛthivīgatāni nānopabhogaparibhogānyupabhokṣyanti sukhāni cānubhaviṣyanti / tāni ca sarvāṇi nānāvicitrānnapānabhojyavastraśayanāsanavasanabhavanavimānodyānanadīpuṣkariṇyutsarohradataḍāgādīnīmānyevaṃrūpāṇi nānāvidhānyupakaraṇasukhāni pṛthivīsaṃsthitāni pṛthivyāṃ prādurbhūtāni pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhitānyupabhujantu / tena bhadanta bhagavanhetunā sarvasattvairasmākaṃ kṛtajñatā kartavyā / avaśyamayaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājaḥ satkṛtya śrotavyaḥ satkartavyo gurukartavyo mānayitavyaḥ pūjayitavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: they shall experience various delights. Those beings shall be endowed with splendor, strength, complexion, and beauty. For the sake of this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, they shall approach those monks, nuns, male and female lay followers who bear this king of sūtras, seated upon the <s>Dharma</s>-seat. Having approached, with joyful minds, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of all beings, they shall request those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers to illuminate this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>. I, <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, the earth-deity, together with my retinue, shall become more vigorous. Thereby, O Venerable Blessed One, great strength, vigor, firmness, and power shall be generated in our body. Splendor, glory, and prosperity shall enter our body. And when I, <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, the earth-deity, O Venerable Blessed One, am satisfied with this nectar-taste of the <s>Dharma</s> and have obtained great splendor, strength, vigor, firmness, and power — this great earth, [extending to] seven thousand <s>yojanas</s> in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, shall be increased with the great essence of the earth. And the great earth shall become more vigorous. And, O Venerable Blessed One, all beings who depend on the earth shall attain growth, development, and abundance. They shall become great. And having become great, all beings dwelling upon the earth shall enjoy various material possessions and provisions and shall experience happiness. And all those various and wonderful foods, drinks, edibles, garments, bedding, seats, clothing, dwellings, mansions, gardens, rivers, lotus-ponds, springs, lakes, reservoirs, and the like — these various kinds of comforts and provisions that are established upon the earth, that have appeared upon the earth, that are grounded in the earth — let [beings] enjoy them! For this reason, O Venerable Blessed One, gratitude toward us should be shown by all beings. This supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, must necessarily be heard with respect, honored, esteemed, venerated, and worshipped.'

body.text: yadā ca bhadanta bhagavaṃste sarve sattvā nānākulebhyo nānāgṛhebhyo niṣkrameyusteṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāmupasakramaṇāya / upasaṃkramya cemaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ / śrutvā ca punareva te sattvāḥ svakasvakeṣu nānākuleṣu gṛhagrāmanagaranigameṣu praviṣṭāḥ svagṛhagatāṃ paraspareṇaivaṃ kathayeyuḥ / gambhīro 'smābhiradya dharmaśravaṇaḥ śrutaḥ / acintyo 'smābhiradya puṇyaskandhaḥ parigṛhītaḥ / tena dharmaśravaṇena narakāḥ pratimuktāḥ syuḥ / tiryagyoniyamalokapretaviṣayāḥ parimuktā adyāsmābhiḥ / anena dharmaśravanenānāgate 'dhvanyanekeṣu jātiśatasahasreṣu devamanuṣyopapattiparigṛhītā
body.translated_text: 'And when, O Venerable Blessed One, all those beings go forth from their various families and households to approach those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers; and having approached, hear this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>; and having heard it, those beings, returning to their various families, houses, villages, cities, and towns, shall say to one another: "Today we have heard a profound <s>Dharma</s>-discourse! Today we have gathered an inconceivable mass of merit! By this hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>, the hells are abandoned by us! The [realms of] animal birth, the world of <s>Yama</s>, and the domain of hungry ghosts are abandoned by us today! By this hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>, in the future, in many hundreds of thousands of births, we shall have obtained rebirth among gods and humans.'

body.text: bhaviṣyanti / tena ca nānāgṛhagatā bhūtvā teṣāṃ sattvānāmitaḥ suvarṇaprabhāsottamātsūtrendrarājādantaśa ekadṛṣṭāntamapyārocayeyurantaśa ekaparivartaṃ vā ekapūrvayogaṃ vāntaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāmantaśa ekapadamapi suvarṇaprabhāsottamātsūtrendrarājādanyeṣāṃ sattvānāṃ saṃśrāvayeyurantaśaḥ suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya nāmadheyamapi pareṣāṃ sattvānā saṃśrāvayeyuḥ /
body.translated_text: And having returned to their various homes, they shall communicate to those beings even a single illustration from this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s> — or even a single chapter, or a single former connection (<s>pūrvayoga</s>), or even a four-lined verse (<s>gāthā</s>), or even a single word from this supreme king of sūtras; or they shall cause other beings to hear even the title of this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: yatra yatra bhadanta bhagavaṃstāni nānāvidhāni sattvāni nānāvidheṣu pṛthivīpradeśaṣvimānyevaṃrūpāṇi nānāvidhāni sūtrāntahetūni paraspareṇārocayeyuḥ saṃśrāvayeyuśca / kathāsaṃbandhaṃ ca kurvīran / sarve te bhadanta bhagavanpṛthivīpradeśā ojasvitarāśca bhaviṣyanti / snigdhatarāśca bhaviṣyanti / sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ teṣu teṣu pṛthivīpradeśeṣu nānāvidhāni pṛthivīrasāni sarvopakaraṇāni bhūyiṣṭhataramutpatsyante vivardhayiṣyante vaipulyatāṃ gamiṣyanti / sarvāṇi tāni sattvāni mahādhanāni mahābhogāni ca dānādhimuktāni ca bhaviṣyanti / triṣu ratneṣvabhiprasannāni bhaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: 'Wherever, O Venerable Blessed One, those various beings in various regions of the earth communicate and cause to be heard among one another these various sūtra-topics, and engage in conversation — all those regions of the earth, O Venerable Blessed One, shall become more vigorous, more nourishing. In all those regions, the various earth-essences and all provisions for all beings shall arise more abundantly, increase, and reach fullness. All those beings shall become wealthy, of great possessions, and inclined to generosity; and they shall be of clear faith in the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>).'

body.text: evamukte bhagavandṛḍhāṃ pṛthivīdevatāmetadavocat / ye kecitpṛthivīdevate sattvā itaḥ suvarṇaprabhāsottamātsūtrendrarājādantaśa ekapadamapi śṛṇuyuste ta ito manuṣyalokāccavitvā trayastriṃśatsu devanikāyeṣvanyatarānyatareṣu devanikāyeṣūpapatsyante / ye kecitpṛthivī devate sattvā asya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājāsyārthāya tāni sthānāni samalaṃkurvīrannantaśa ekacchatraṃ vā ekadūṣyaṃ vā samalaṃkṛtāni ca devatāsthānāni / teṣu saptasu kāmāvacareṣu devanikāyeṣu saptaratnamayāni divyāni vimānāni sarvālaṃkārasamalaṃkṛtāni saṃsthāsyanti te sattvā ito manuṣyalokāccyāvitvā teṣu saptaratnamayeṣu divyavimāneṣūpapatsyante / te caikaikasminpṛthivīdevate saptaratnamaye divyavimāne saptavarā anupapatsyante acintyāni divyāni sukhāni pratyanubhaviṣyanti //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said to <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, the earth-deity: 'Whatever beings, O earth-deity, shall hear even a single word from this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s> — they, having departed from this human world, shall be reborn in one or another of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> divine assemblies. And whatever beings, O earth-deity, shall adorn the places [of preaching] for the sake of this supreme king of sūtras — even with a single parasol or a single canopy — and [shall adorn] the deity-shrines: in the seven <s>Kāmāvacara</s> (desire-realm) divine assemblies, divine mansions made of the seven precious substances, adorned with all ornaments, shall be established. Those beings, having departed from this human world, shall be reborn in those divine mansions made of the seven precious substances. And in each one of those seven-jeweled divine mansions, O earth-deity, seven excellent [ones] shall be reborn [together], and they shall experience inconceivable divine happiness.'

body.text: evamukte dṛḍhā pṛthivīdevatā bhagavantametadavocat / tenāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavandṛḍhā pṛthivīdevatā tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣordharmāsanagatasya teṣu pṛthivīpradeśeṣvavāsiṣyāmi / adṛśyamānenātmabhāvena
body.translated_text: When this was said, <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, the earth-deity, said to the Blessed One: 'Therefore, O Venerable Blessed One, I, <s>Dṛḍhā</s>, the earth-deity, shall settle in those regions of the earth where the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk is seated upon the <s>Dharma</s>-seat. With an invisible body,

body.text: tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣoruttamāṅgena pādatalau pratisaṃhariṣyāmi / yathāpyayaṃ suvarṇaprabhasottamaḥ sūtrendrarājasteṣāṃ buddhasahasrāvaruptakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya ciraṃ jambudvīpe pracaret / na ca kṣipramantardhāpayeet / sattvāni cemaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ / anāgato 'dhvanyanekāni kalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyacintyāni divyamānuṣyakāni sukhānyanubhaveyuḥ / tathāgatasamavadhānagatāni ca bhaveyuḥ / anāgate 'dhvanyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyuḥ / sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokaduḥkhāni cātyantasamucchinnāni bhaveyuriti //
body.translated_text: I shall touch my head to the soles of that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk's feet — so that this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, may circulate for a long time in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for the sake of those beings whose roots of merit have been planted under a thousand <s>Buddhas</s>, and may not quickly vanish. And [so that] beings may hear this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, and in the future, for many inconceivable hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>kalpas</s>, may experience divine and human happiness, and may come into the presence of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and in the future may fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), and all the sufferings of hells, animal births, and the world of <s>Yama</s> may be completely cut off.'

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottasūtrendrarāje dṛḍhāpṛthivī devatāparivarto nāmaikādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eleventh chapter, the <s>Dṛḍhā Pṛthivīdevatā</s> (Firm Earth-Deity) Chapter, in the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Saṃjñeyamahāyakṣasenāpatiparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Saṃjñeya Mahāyakṣasenāpati</s> (Great <s>Yakṣa</s>-General <s>Saṃjñeya</s>) Chapter //

body.text: atha khalu saṃjñeyo nāma mahāyakṣasenāpatiraṣṭāviṃśatibhirmahāyakṣasenāpatibhiḥ sārdhamutthāyāsanādekāṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ prāvṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat / ayaṃ bhadanta bhagavansuvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarāja etarhi cānagate 'dhvani yatra grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā janapade vā janapadapradeśe vāraṇyāyatane vā girikandare vā rājakule vā gṛhe vā pracariṣyati / tatrāhaṃ bhadanta bhagavansaṃjñeyo nāma mahāyakṣasenāpatiḥ sārdhamaṣṭāviṃśati bhirmahāyakṣasenāpatibhistatra grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā janapade vāraṇye vā girikandare vā rājakule vopasaṃkramiṣyāmi / adṛśyamānenātmabhāvena tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣo rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmi / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ śāntisvaratyayanaṃ kariṣyami / teṣāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ dharmaśravaṇikānāṃ strīpuruṣadārakadārikāṇāṃ yeṣāṃ keṣāṃciditaḥ suvarṇaprabhāsottamātsūtrendrarājādantaśa ekā catuṣpādikāpi gāthā śrutā bhavedantaśa ekapadamapi suvarṇaprabhāsottamātsūtrendrarājādekabodhisattvanāmadheyamapi śrutaṃ bhavedudgṛhītaṃ vaikatathāgatanāmadheyaṃ vāntaśaścāsya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasya nāmadheyaṃ śrutaṃ bhavedudgṛhītaṃ vā teṣāṃ sarveṣāmārakṣāṃ kariṣyāmi / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ ca kariṣyāmi / teṣāṃ ca kulānāṃ teṣāṃ ca gṛhāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca nagarāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca grāmāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca nigamānāṃ teṣāṃ cāraṇyānāṃ teṣāṃ ca rājakulānāmārakṣāṃ kariṣyāmi / paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ śāntisvastyayanaṃ kariṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>yakṣa</s>-general named <s>Saṃjñeya</s>, together with the twenty-eight great <s>yakṣa</s>-generals, rose from his seat, arranged his robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and joining his palms in the direction of the Blessed One, said to him: 'This supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, O Venerable Blessed One, now and in the future — wherever it circulates, in a village, city, market-town, district, region, forest hermitage, mountain cave, or royal palace — there I, the great <s>yakṣa</s>-general <s>Saṃjñeya</s>, O Venerable Blessed One, together with the twenty-eight great <s>yakṣa</s>-generals, shall proceed to that village, city, market-town, district, forest, mountain cave, or royal palace. With an invisible body, I shall provide protection for that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk: shelter, support, safeguarding, protection from punishment, protection from weapons, and the blessing of peace and well-being. And for all those who listen to the <s>Dharma</s> — men, women, boys, and girls — anyone who has heard even a single four-lined verse from this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, or even a single word, or even a single <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s name, or even a single <s>Tathāgata</s>'s name, or even the title of this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, has heard or retained [it] — for all of them I shall provide protection: shelter, support, safeguarding, protection from punishment, protection from weapons, and the blessing of peace and well-being. And for their families, their houses, their cities, their villages, their towns, their forests, and their royal households — I shall provide protection: shelter, support, safeguarding, protection from punishment, protection from weapons, and the blessing of peace and well-being.'

body.text: tatkatamena hetunā / sarvadharmāḥ parijñātāḥ sarvadharmā avabuddhāḥ / yāvantaśca sarvadharmāḥ / yathā ca sarvadharmāḥ / saṃsthitā ye ca sarvadharmāḥ / samyagjñātāśca sarvadharmāḥ / sarvadharmeṣvahaṃ bhadanta bhagavanpratyakṣaḥ / acintyā me bhadanta bhagavañjñānāvabhāsāḥ / acintyo jñānālokaḥ / acintyo jñānapracāraḥ / acintyo jñānaskandhaḥ / acintyo me bhadanta bhagavansarvadharmeṣu jñānaviṣayaḥ pravartate / yathā ca me bhadanta bhagavansarvadharmāḥ samamyagjñātāḥ / samyakparīkṣitāḥ samyakparijñātāḥ
body.translated_text: 'For what reason? All <s>dharmas</s> have been fully understood; all <s>dharmas</s> have been awakened to — however many <s>dharmas</s> there are, in whatever way <s>dharmas</s> are established, all <s>dharmas</s> have been rightly known. I, O Venerable Blessed One, am a direct witness to all <s>dharmas</s>. Inconceivable, O Venerable Blessed One, are my illuminations of knowledge; inconceivable is the light of my knowledge; inconceivable is the range of my knowledge; inconceivable is my mass of knowledge. Inconceivable, O Venerable Blessed One, is the domain of knowledge that operates in me with respect to all <s>dharmas</s>. And as all <s>dharmas</s>, O Venerable Blessed One, have been rightly known by me, rightly investigated, rightly comprehended,

body.text: samyagvyavalokitāḥ samyagavabuddhāḥ / tena hetunā mama bhadanta bhagavansaṃjñeyasya mahāyakṣasenāpateḥ saṃjñeya iti nāmadheyaṃ samudapādi //
body.translated_text: rightly surveyed, and rightly awakened to — for this reason, O Venerable Blessed One, the name '<s>Saṃjñeya</s>' (the 'Fully Known') has arisen for me, the great <s>yakṣa</s>-general.'

body.text: ahaṃ bhadanta bhagavandharmabhāṇakasya bhikṣorvākyavibhūṣaṇārthāya pratibhānamupasaṃhariṣyāmi / romāntareṣu ca tasyaujaḥ prakṣepsyāmi / mahāntaṃ ca tasya sthāma ca balaṃ vīryaṃ ca kāye saṃjanayiṣyāmi / acintyaṃ tasya jñānāvabhāsaṃ kariṣyāmi / smṛtiṃ ca tasya bodhayiṣyāmi / mahantaṃ ca tasyotsahaṃ dāsyāmi / yathā ca sa dharmabhāṇako na klāntakāyo bhavet / sukhendriyakāyo bhavet / praharṣajātaśca bhavet / yenāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājasteṣāṃ buddhasahasrāvaruptakuśalamūlānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya ciraṃ jambudvīpe pracaret / na kṣipramantardhāpayet / sattvāścemaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaṃ sūtrendrarājaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ / acintyaṃ ca jñānaskandhaṃ pratilabheyuḥ / prajñāvantaśca bhaveyuḥ / aparimitaṃ ca puṇyaskandhaṃ parigṛhṇīyuḥ / anāgate 'dhvanyanekakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyacintyāni divyamānuṣyakāni sukhānyanubhaveyuḥ / tathāgatasamavadhānagatāśca bhaveyuranāgate 'dhvanyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeran / sarvanarakatiryagyoniyamalokaduḥkhāni cātyantena samucchinnāni bhaveyuriti //
body.translated_text: 'I, O Venerable Blessed One, shall bring eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>) to the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher monk for the adornment of his speech. And I shall infuse vigor into his pores. I shall generate great firmness, strength, and vigor in his body. I shall create inconceivable illumination of knowledge for him. I shall awaken his mindfulness. I shall give him great enthusiasm — so that the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher may not become weary in body, may be of comfortable faculties, and may be filled with delight — so that this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, may circulate for a long time in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> for the sake of those beings whose roots of merit have been planted under a thousand <s>Buddhas</s>, and may not quickly vanish. And [so that] beings may hear this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, and may obtain an inconceivable mass of knowledge; may become possessed of wisdom; may gather an immeasurable mass of merit; and in the future, for many inconceivable hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>kalpas</s>, may experience divine and human happiness; and may come into the presence of <s>Tathāgatas</s>; and in the future may fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening; and all the sufferings of hells, animal births, and the world of <s>Yama</s> may be completely cut off.'

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje saṃjñeyamahāyakṣasenāpati parivarto nāma dvādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth chapter, named 'The Chapter of <s>Saṃjñeya</s>, Great Commander of the <s>Yakṣas</s>,' in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // Devendrasamayarājaśāstraparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The Chapter on the Treatise of Kingship According to the Covenant of the Lord of Gods (<s>Devendrasamaya-rājaśāstra-parivarta</s>).

body.text: namastasya bhagavato ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśriyastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya / namasyasyānekaguṇakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrasamalaṃkṛtaśarīrasya śākyamunestathāgatasya yasyeyaṃ dharmolkā jvalati / namastasyā aparimitapuṇyadhānyamāṅgalyasampannāyāḥ śriyo mahādevyāḥ / namastasyā aparimitaguṇaprajñāsamuditāyāḥ sarasvatyā devyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Homage to that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, whose glory is that of Jewel-Flower-Virtue-Ocean-Lapis-Lazuli-Golden-Mountain-Gold-Radiance-Splendor. Homage to <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, whose body is adorned with innumerable <s>koṭīniyutaśatasahasra</s> virtues, and whose torch of <s>Dharma</s> blazes. Homage to that <s>Śrī Mahādevī</s>, endowed with immeasurable merit, grain, and auspiciousness. Homage to that goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, arisen from immeasurable virtue and wisdom.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ kālena tena samayena rājā baladaketuḥ putrasya ruciraketoracirābhiṣiktasya ca rājyapratiṣṭhitasyaitadavocat / asti putra devendrasamayaṃ nāma rājaśāstram / yanmayā pūrvamacirābhiṣiktena ca rājyapratiṣṭhitena pitū rājño balendraketoḥ sakāśādudgṛhītam / tena mayā devendrasamayena rājaśāstreṇa viṃśativarṣasahasrāṇi rājatvaṃ kāritaṃ babhūva / nābhijānāmyahamantaśa ekacittakṣaṇapramāṇamātreṇāpi kasyacidadharmasthitapūrvam / katamattatra devendrasamayaṃ nāma rājaśāstram //
body.translated_text: Then, at that time, in that moment, King <s>Baladaketu</s> spoke thus to his son <s>Ruciraketu</s>, who had recently been anointed and established in kingship: 'There exists, my son, a treatise on kingship called the <s>Devendrasamaya</s> (Covenant of the Lord of Gods), which I received from my father, King <s>Balendraketu</s>, when I too had recently been anointed and established in kingship. By means of that <s>Devendrasamaya</s> treatise on kingship, I exercised sovereignty for twenty thousand years. I do not recall ever, even for a single moment of consciousness, having established anyone in unrighteousness. What then is that treatise on kingship called the <s>Devendrasamaya</s>?'

body.text: atha khalu kuladevate rājā baladaketustena kālena tena samayena putrasya rājño ruciraketorimābhirgāthābhirdevendrasamayaṃ nāma rājaśāstraṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, at that time, in that moment, King <s>Baladaketu</s> explained the treatise on kingship called the <s>Devendrasamaya</s> in detail to his son, King <s>Ruciraketu</s>, with these verses:

children.translated_text: I shall declare the treatise on kingship, which brings benefit to all beings,
which cuts through all doubts and destroys all wrongdoing.
With joyful minds, let all the kings individually
listen with joined palms to the complete <s>Devendrasamaya</s> (Covenant of the Lord of Gods).
Upon this adamantine mountain-fortress, at the assembly of the lords of gods,
<s>Brahmā</s> was questioned by the world-protectors who had arisen.
'You are our teacher of the gods, O <s>Brahmā</s>; you are the lord of the deities.

children.text: chettā tvaṃ saṃśayānāṃ ca cchindayāsmākaṃ saṃśayam // Suv_13.4 //
children.translated_text: You are the cutter of doubts—cut our doubt!'

children.text: kathaṃ manuṣyasaṃbhūto rājā devaḥ sa procyate /
children.translated_text: 'How is a king born among humans called a god?

children.text: yadiha mānuṣe loke jāyate ca bhavannṛpaḥ // Suv_13.5 //
children.translated_text: If he is born here in the human world, how does he become a king?'
'How will kingship be exercised among gods and humans?'
Thus was <s>Brahmā</s> questioned by the world-protectors.
<s>Brahmā</s>, the teacher of all the gods, spoke to the world-protectors:
'If indeed I am now questioned by you, the world-protectors,
I shall declare the supreme treatise for the benefit of all beings.'
'I shall declare the origin of men, having considered the abode of humans,

children.text: hetunā yena rājāno bhavanti viṣayeṣu ca // Suv_13.8 //
children.translated_text: and the cause by which kings come to be in their domains.'
'By the establishment of the lords of gods, he shall enter the mother's womb.

children.text: pūrvamadhiṣṭhito devaiḥ paścād garbhe prapadyate // Suv_13.9 //
children.translated_text: First appointed by the gods, he afterwards enters the womb.'

children.text: kiṃ cāpi mānuṣe loke jāyate śrīyate nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Although he is born in the human world and the king grows up,

children.text: api vai devasaṃbhūto devaputraḥ sa ucyate // Suv_13.10 //
children.translated_text: he is indeed of divine origin and is called a son of the gods.'
'A portion has been given to the king by the thirty-three divine lords.

children.text: putrastvaṃ saha devānāṃ nirmito manujeśvaraḥ // Suv_13.11 //
children.translated_text: You are a son created together with the gods, O lord of men.'
'For the purpose of quelling unrighteousness, he is the restrainer of wrongdoers.
He should establish beings in virtue, for the sake of sending them to the heavenly abode.'

children.text: manuṣyo vātha devo vā gandharvo vā narādhipaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whether human, or god, or <s>Gandharva</s>, O lord of men,

children.text: rākṣaso vātha caṇḍālo duṣkṛtānāṃ nivārakaḥ // Suv_13.13 //
children.translated_text: or <s>Rākṣasa</s>, or <s>Caṇḍāla</s>—he is the restrainer of wrongdoers.'

children.text: mātā pitā vā nṛpatiḥ sukṛtau karmakāriṇām /
children.translated_text: 'The king is like a mother and father to those who perform virtuous deeds.
You, who see the fruits of ripening, are appointed by the divine kings.'
'Of both virtuous and wicked deeds, he is the righteous judge in this life.
You, who see the fruits of ripening, are appointed by the divine kings.'

children.text: yadā hyupekṣate rājā duṣkṛtaṃ viṣaye sthitam /
children.translated_text: 'When the king overlooks wrongdoing established in his domain,

children.text: nānārūpaṃ na kurvīta daṇḍaṃ pāpajanasya ca /
children.translated_text: and does not apply various forms of punishment to the wicked,
through the neglect of wrongdoers, unrighteousness greatly increases.'

children.text: śāṭhyāni kalahāścaiva bhūyo rāṣṭre bhavanti ca /
children.translated_text: 'Deceits and quarrels increasingly arise in the kingdom,
and the lords of gods become angry in the mansions of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven.'

children.text: yadā hyupekṣate rājā duṣkṛtaṃ viṣaye sthiram /
children.translated_text: 'When the king overlooks wrongdoing firmly established in his domain,

children.text: hanyate viṣayo ghoraiḥ śaṭhyairapi sudāruṇaiḥ // Suv_13.18 //
children.translated_text: the domain is struck by terrible and extremely cruel deceits.'
'That kingdom is destroyed and falls under the invasion of hostile forces;

children.text: bhogāni ca balānyeva dhanaṃ yasyāsti saṃcitam // Suv_13.19 //
children.translated_text: possessions, armies, and accumulated wealth—'

children.text: vividhāni ca śāṭhyāni haranti ca parasparam /
children.translated_text: 'people plunder various things from one another.
The purpose for which kingship was given—that purpose he fails to fulfill.

children.text: vilopayati svaṃ rāṣṭraṃ gajendra iva padminīm // Suv_13.20 //
children.translated_text: He devastates his own kingdom like a bull elephant in a lotus pond.'
'The winds blow out of season, the rains fall out of season,
the planets and constellations become irregular, and the moon and sun likewise.'

children.text: sasyaṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ bījaṃ va samyakparipacyate /
children.translated_text: 'Crops, flowers, fruits, and seeds do not ripen properly.

children.text: durbhikṣaṃ bhavate tatra yatra rājā hyupekṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Famine arises there where the king is negligent,

children.text: anāttamānaso devā bhavanti bhavaneṣu ca // Suv_13.22 //
children.translated_text: and the gods in their mansions become discontented.'
'When the king overlooks wrongdoing and it spreads further,

children.text: te sarve devarājāśca vakṣyanti ca parasparam // Suv_13.23 //
children.translated_text: all those divine kings shall speak to one another:'
'"This king is unrighteous; he has taken the side of unrighteousness.

children.text: na cireṇa hyayaṃ rājā devatāṃ kopayiṣyati // Suv_13.24 //
children.translated_text: Before long, this king will anger the deities."'
'By the anger of the deities, his domain shall be destroyed.

children.text: śasrāṇi ca adharmaśca viṣaye 'tra bhaviṣyanti // Suv_13.25 //
children.translated_text: Weapons and unrighteousness shall appear in that domain.'

children.text: śāṭhyānāṃ kalahānāṃ ca rogāṇāṃ ca samudbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There shall be an outbreak of deceits, quarrels, and diseases.

children.text: prakupyati ca devendra upekṣyanti ca devatāḥ // Suv_13.26 //
children.translated_text: The lord of gods becomes angry, and the deities turn away.'

children.text: pralupyate ca yadrāṣṭraṃ sa nṛpaḥ śokamṛcchati /
children.translated_text: 'When the kingdom is plundered, that king falls into grief.

children.text: iṣṭaviyogaṃ prāpnoti bhrātrā vātha sutena vā // Suv_13.27 //
children.translated_text: He suffers separation from loved ones—from a brother or from a son.'
'Separation from a beloved wife is experienced, or from a daughter.
Meteors shall fall, and mock-suns shall appear.'
'Fear of hostile forces arises, and famine greatly increases.
A beloved minister dies, and an unfavorable one thunders forth words.'
'Sons, beloved ones, and faithful wives become adversaries.

children.text: parasparaṃ hariṣyanti kulabhogaṃ dhanāni ca // Suv_13.30 //
children.translated_text: They plunder family property and riches from one another.'

children.text: deśe deśe haniṣyanti śastreṇa ca parasparam /
children.translated_text: 'In region after region, they slay one another with weapons.

children.text: vivādāḥ kalahāḥ śāṭhyā bhavanti viṣayeṣu ca // Suv_13.31 //
children.translated_text: Disputes, quarrels, and deceits arise in the domains.'
'Planetary afflictions enter the kingdom; terrible disease arises.
The unrighteous shall become those who receive consecration therein.'
'Ministers and courtiers become unrighteous.
Honor is given to wicked people therein.'

children.text: dhārmikānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ nigraho bhavati dhruvam /
children.translated_text: 'The suppression of virtuous beings surely occurs.
Honor for the wicked and suppression of the righteous—
when these three occur, the constellations, waters, and winds become disturbed.'
'Three essences are destroyed when the wicked are honored:
the essence of true <s>Dharma</s>, the vitality of beings, and the essence of the earth.'
'When the dishonest are honored and the truthful are disparaged,
three things shall result: incessant famine,
and the essence and vitality of fruits and crops cease to exist.'

children.text: glānena bahulāḥ sattvā bhavanti viṣayeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: 'Beings in the domains are mostly afflicted with illness.

children.text: madhurāṇi mahānti ca phalāni viṣaye 'pi hi /
children.translated_text: The great and sweet fruits in the domain

children.text: parītā ca bhaviṣyanti tiktaḥ kaṭuka eva ca // Suv_13.37 //
children.translated_text: become depleted, turning bitter and pungent.'
'Previously delightful things—play, laughter, and pleasures—
the pleasant assemblies become troubled by hundreds of afflictions.'

children.text: dhānyānāṃ ca phalānāṃ ca snigghabhāvo rasaḥ kṣayet /
children.translated_text: 'The nourishing essence of grains and fruits diminishes;
they no longer satisfy the body, senses, and physical elements.'
'Beings become of poor complexion, with little stamina, and very weak.

children.text: bahu ca bhojanaṃ bhuktvā tṛptiṃ nāsādayanti te // Suv_13.40 //
children.translated_text: Even having eaten much food, they do not attain satisfaction.'

children.text: balaṃ ca sthāma vīryaṃ ca na labhanti tadantare /
children.translated_text: 'Strength, stamina, and vigor they no longer obtain.

children.text: hīnavīryāṇi sattvāni bhavanti viṣayeṣu ca // Suv_13.41 //
children.translated_text: Beings of diminished vigor arise in the domains.'
'Beings become afflicted with disease, tormented by various ailments.
Planetary afflictions arise in the constellations, born from various <s>Rākṣasas</s>.'
'The king becomes unrighteous, established in the camp of unrighteousness.
He stands in opposition to the three realms, to the entire <s>maṇḍala</s> of the three worlds.

children.text: aneke īdṛśā doṣā bhavanti viṣayeṣu ca // Suv_13.43 //
children.translated_text: Innumerable such faults arise in the domains.'
'When a king, having taken sides, overlooks wrongdoing,
the purpose for which the king was appointed by the lords of gods—

children.text: na tatkaroti rājatvaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ samupekṣataḥ // Suv_13.44 //
children.translated_text: that kingship he fails to fulfill, overlooking wrongdoing.'
'By virtue, beings are reborn in all the heavenly abodes of the gods.
By wrongdoing, they go to the realms of hungry ghosts, animals, and hells.
