In the abode of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, they chastise the wrongdoers.'

children.text: yadā hyupakṣate rājā duṣkṛtaṃ viṣaye sthitam /
children.translated_text: 'When the king overlooks wrongdoing established in his domain,
he becomes an offender against his fathers, the divine kings.

children.text: na tadbhavati putratvaṃ na rajatvaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavet // Suv_13.46 //
children.translated_text: That sonship no longer exists, nor has the kingship been properly exercised.'
'When affairs are destroyed by terrible deceits,
therefore the king, established by the lord of gods in the human world—'
'for the purpose of quelling wrongdoers, he is the promoter of virtue.
The king, a righteous judge of beings, generates the fruits of <s>karma</s>.'
'Of virtuous and wicked deeds of various kinds,
the king is called the one who makes visible the fruits of their ripening,
appointed by the host of gods, approved by the lords of gods.'
'For his own sake, for others' sake, for the sake of <s>Dharma</s> and the domain,
for the purpose of subduing the deceitful and wicked people in the kingdoms—'

children.text: tyajecca jīvitaṃ rājyaṃ dharmārthaṃ viṣayasya ca /
children.translated_text: 'he should abandon life and kingdom for the sake of <s>Dharma</s> and the domain.
He should not, knowing what is right, overlook unrighteousness without inquiry.'
'There is no other destruction so terrible in this domain
as when, from the arising of deceit, there is no restraint of the wilderness of deceit.'
'Deceits increase further in this domain, extremely terrible.

children.text: vilupyate ca tadrāṣṭraṃ gajairiva mahāsaraḥ // Suv_13.53 //
children.translated_text: That kingdom is plundered, like a great lake by elephants.'
'The lords of gods become angry; the heavenly abode is plundered.

children.text: viṣamāḥ sarvabhāvāśca bhavanti viṣayasya hi // Suv_13.54 //
children.translated_text: All conditions in the domain become disordered.'
'Therefore, the punishment of evildoers should be proportionate to their faults.

children.text: dharmeṇa pālayedrāṣṭaṃ mā cādharmaṃ samācaret // Suv_13.55 //
children.translated_text: One should govern the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s>; one should not practice <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).'

children.text: jīvitaṃ ca parityajya mā pāpe patito bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'Even sacrificing one's life, one should not fall into sin.
Toward kinsmen, toward others, toward all the people of the kingdom,

children.text: ekāpekṣo bhavedrājā mā pakṣe patito bhavet // Suv_13.56 //
children.translated_text: the king should be impartial; he should not fall into partisanship.'
'A righteous king fills the three worlds with glory.
The lords of gods in the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heavens shall rejoice:'
'"In <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, this son of ours, a <s>Dharma</s>-minded king,

children.text: dharmeṇa śāsyate rāṣṭraṃ sukṛte sthāpyate janam // Suv_13.58 //
children.translated_text: governs the kingdom by <s>Dharma</s> and establishes the people in virtue."'

children.text: sukṛtena ca rājā taṃ iha preṣayate janam /
children.translated_text: 'By virtue, the king sends the people of this world to heaven,

children.text: devairdevasutaiḥ pūrṇaṃ karoti ca surālayam // Suv_13.59 //
children.translated_text: and fills the heavenly abode with gods and sons of gods.'

children.text: dharmeṇa śāsyate rāṣṭraṃ rājā naḥ supraharṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the realm is governed by <s>dharma</s>, we kings are greatly delighted;

children.text: prasannā bhonti devendrā rakṣante tānnarādhipān // Suv_13.60 //
children.translated_text: the lords of <s>devas</s> become pleased and protect those lords of men. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 13.60 //
The constellations move in their proper course, and the moon and sun likewise;

children.text: kālena vāyavo vānti kāle caivaṃ pravarṣati // Suv_13.61 //
children.translated_text: the winds blow in due season, and it rains in due season as well. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 13.61 //
They make the realm prosperous, and likewise the abode of the <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s>;
the celestial abode becomes filled with immortals and sons of immortals. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 13.62 //
Therefore, let the king relinquish his own dear life,

children.text: āvartayeddharmaratnaṃ yena lokaḥ sukhī bhavet // Suv_13.63 //
children.translated_text: and set in motion the jewel of <s>dharma</s>, by which the world may become happy. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 13.63 //

body.text: / dhārmikīṃ ca nayet sevāṃ yo guṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ /

children.text: sa nityaṃ sevate tuṣṭaṃ sadā pāpavivarjitaḥ // Suv_13.64 //
children.translated_text: he who is always content in service, ever free from evil— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 13.64 //

body.translated_text: He should perform righteous service, adorned with virtues;

children.translated_text: he should protect the realm by <s>dharma</s>, and should instruct [his subjects] in <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: sukṛte sthāpayet sattvānduṣkṛte ca vivārayet // Suv_13.65 //
children.translated_text: he should establish beings in good deeds and turn them away from evil deeds. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 13.65 //

children.text: subhikṣaṃ bhavate rāṣṭre tejasvī bhavate nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The realm becomes prosperous, and the king becomes splendid,
when he carries out appropriate punishment of evildoers;

children.text: yaśasvī bhavate rājā sukhaṃ pālayate prajāmiti // Suv_13.66 //
children.translated_text: the king becomes famous and protects his people with happiness. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 13.66 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsoottamasūtrendrarāje devendrasamayaṃ nāma rājaśāstraparivartastrayodaśamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, the <s>Devendrasamaya</s> (Covenant of the Lord of Gods) Chapter on the Treatise of Kingship, in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // Susaṃbhavaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Susaṃbhava</s> Chapter //

children.text: sasāgarā tyakta vasuṃdharā tadā yadā babhūva nṛpa cakravartī /
children.translated_text: With its oceans, the earth was relinquished then, when [I] was a <s>Cakravartin</s> king;

children.text: catvāri dvīpāni saratnapūrṇaniryāti tā pūrvajineṣu mahyam // Suv_14.1 //
children.translated_text: the four continents, filled with jewels—I gave them away in the dispensation of the former <s>Jinas</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.1 //

children.text: na cāsti tadvastu priyaṃ manāpaṃ pūrvaṃ ca mahyaṃ na va tyaktamāsīt /
children.translated_text: There was no thing, dear or pleasing, that had not been given by me in the past;

children.text: taṃ dharmakāyaṃ parimārgaṇārthaḥ priyajīvitaṃ tyaktamanekakalpān // Suv_14.2 //
children.translated_text: in search of that <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Body of the Dharma), I gave up my dear life for innumerable <s>kalpas</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.2 //

children.text: yatha pūrvakalpeṣu acintiyeṣu ratnaśikhisya sugatasya śāsane /
children.translated_text: Thus, in inconceivable past <s>kalpas</s>, in the dispensation of the <s>Sugata</s> <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>,

children.text: parinirvṛtasya sugatasya tasya susaṃbhavo nāma babhūva rājā // Suv_14.3 //
children.translated_text: after that <s>Sugata</s> had passed into <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, there was a king named <s>Susaṃbhava</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.3 //

children.text: sa cakravartī caturdvīpa īśvaraḥ samudraparyantamahī praśāsyate /
children.translated_text: He was a <s>Cakravartin</s>, lord of the four continents, ruling the earth bounded by oceans;

children.text: jinendraghoṣāya ca rājadhānīya supto babhūvā tada rājakuñjaraḥ // Suv_14.4 //
children.translated_text: in the capital city of <s>Jinendraghoṣā</s>, that bull among kings then fell asleep. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.4 //

children.text: svapnāntare buddhaguṇāñca śrutvā ratnoccayaṃ paśyati dharmabhāṇakam /
children.translated_text: In a dream he heard the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s> and beheld the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher <s>Ratnoccaya</s>,

children.text: sthita sūryamadhye va virocamānaṃ prakāśayantaṃ ima sūtrarājam // Suv_14.5 //
children.translated_text: standing as if shining in the midst of the sun, illuminating this king of <s>sūtras</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.5 //
The king awoke from his dream, his entire body pervaded by rapture;

children.text: abhiniṣkrarma rājakulāni dṛṣṭu upasaṃkramī śrāvakasaṃghamagram // Suv_14.6 //
children.translated_text: he went forth from the royal palace, and approached the foremost assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> to see [them]. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.6 //

body.text: karoti pūjāṃ jinaśrāvakāṇāṃ ratnoccayaṃ pṛcchati dharmabhāṇakam /
body.translated_text: He made offerings to the <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the <s>Jina</s>, and asked about the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher <s>Ratnoccaya</s>:

body.text: kva cāsti bhikṣūriha cāryasaṃghe ratnoccayo nāma guṇānvitaśca // Suv_14.7 //
body.translated_text: 'Where is there a monk here, in this noble <s>Saṅgha</s>, named <s>Ratnoccaya</s>, endowed with virtues?' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.7 //

children.text: tenāntareṇā ratanoccayo hi anyatra gūhāntara saṃniṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, <s>Ratnoccaya</s> was elsewhere, seated within the interior of a cave,

children.text: vicitraratnaṃ ima sūtrarājaṃ svadhyāyamānaḥ sukha saṃniṣaṇaḥ // Suv_14.8 //
children.translated_text: reciting this king of <s>sūtras</s>, this jewel of varied gems, seated comfortably. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.8 //

body.text:
deśenti rājasya tadantareṇa ratnoccayaṃ bhikṣu sa dharmabhāṇakam /
anyatra gūhāntarasaṃniṣaṇaṃ / taṃ tena raśmīśriyayā jvalantam // Suv_14.9 //
body.translated_text: Meanwhile, they pointed out to the king that monk <s>Ratnoccaya</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, seated elsewhere within the interior of a cave, blazing with the splendor of his radiance. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.9 //

children.text: eṣo 'tra ratnoccaya dharmabhāṇako dhāreti gambhīrajinasya gocaram /
children.translated_text: 'Here is <s>Ratnoccaya</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, who holds the profound domain of the <s>Jina</s>;
he constantly illuminates the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, the jewel of <s>sūtras</s>, the king of <s>sūtras</s>.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.10 //

children.text: vanditva pādau ratanoccayasya susaṃbhavo rāja idaṃ pravīddhi /
children.translated_text: Having bowed at the feet of <s>Ratnoccaya</s>, King <s>Susaṃbhava</s> spoke thus:

children.text: deśe hi me pūrṇaśaśāṅka cakraṃ svarṇaprabhāsottamasūtraratnam // Suv_14.11 //
children.translated_text: 'Teach me, O Full Moon, this jewel of <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>!' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.11 //

children.text: adhivāsayī so ratanoccayaśca rājñaśca tasyaiva susaṃbhavasya /
children.translated_text: That <s>Ratnoccaya</s> gave his assent to King <s>Susaṃbhava</s>;
throughout the entire <s>trisāhasra</s> (triple-thousand) world-system, all the deities became filled with joy. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.12 //
On a supreme and excellent spot of earth, sprinkled with jewel-water and fragrant water,

children.text: puṣpāvakīrṇāṃ dharaṇīṃ sa kṛtvā tatrāsanaṃ prāpya tadā narendraḥ // Suv_14.13 //
children.translated_text: having strewn the ground with flowers, the lord of men then prepared a seat there. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.13 //

body.text: samalaṃkṛtaṃ rājña tadāsanaṃ ca cchatrairdhvajairghaṇṭasahasranekaiḥ /
body.translated_text: That seat of the king was well-adorned with parasols, banners, and thousands of bells;

body.text: nānāvicitrairvarapuṣpacandrair abhyokire rājña tadāsanaṃ ca // Suv_14.14 //
body.translated_text: with various beautiful excellent flowers and moon[-like ornaments], the king's seat was bedecked. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.14 //

children.translated_text: <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>-lords, and <s>Mahoragas</s>,

children.text: divyaiśca māndāravapuṣpavarṣair abhyāvakīrṇāśca tadāsanaṃ ca // Suv_14.15 //
children.translated_text: with showers of divine <s>Māndārava</s> flowers, covered that seat. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.15 //
Inconceivable, infinite thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> [of beings], those who had come from the foremost heavenly realms of desire,

children.text: abhiniṣkramitvā ratanoccayaṃ hi abhyo kiranti sma ca sālapuṣpā // Suv_14.16 //
children.translated_text: having come forth, showered <s>Sāla</s> flowers upon <s>Ratnoccaya</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.16 //

children.text: so cāpi ratnoccaya dharmabhāṇakaḥ śubhābhagātraḥ śucivastraprāvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher <s>Ratnoccaya</s>, of auspicious body, wrapped in pure garments,

children.text: upasaṃkramitvā ca tadāsanaṃ hi kṛtāñjalībhūtva namasyate ca // Suv_14.17 //
children.translated_text: having approached that seat, stood with palms joined in reverence and bowed. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.17 //

children.text: devendradevāni ca devatāni māndārapuṣpaṃ ca pravarṣayanti /
children.translated_text: <s>Devendra</s>, the <s>devas</s>, and the deities rained down <s>Māndārava</s> flowers;

children.text: acintiyā tūryaśatā sahasrā pravādayanti sthita antarīkṣe // Suv_14.18 //
children.translated_text: inconceivable hundreds of thousands of musical instruments sounded, stationed in the sky. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.18 //

children.text: abhīruhitvā ca sa saṃniṣaṇo ratnoccayo bhikṣu sa dharmabhāṇakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having ascended [the seat] and sat down, the monk <s>Ratnoccaya</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher,

children.text: anusmaritvā daśasū diśāsu acintiyā buddhasahasrakoṭyaḥ // Suv_14.19 //
children.translated_text: having called to mind the inconceivable thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions, // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.19 //

body.text: sarveṣa sattvāna kṛpāṃja nitya kāruṇyacittaṃ samupādayet saḥ /
body.translated_text: he generated for all beings constantly the mind of compassion and loving-kindness;

body.text: rājñaśca tasyāpi susaṃbhavasya prakāśitaṃ sūtramidaṃ tadantare // Suv_14.20 //
body.translated_text: and then he illuminated this <s>sūtra</s> for that King <s>Susaṃbhava</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.20 //

children.text: kṛtāñjalībhūtva sthihitva rājā yaḥ kāyavācā manumoditaḥ saḥ /
children.translated_text: The king stood with palms joined, and he who was delighted in body, speech, and mind,
with eyes streaming tears from the force of the true <s>Dharma</s>—his body became thrilled [with rapture]. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.21 //

body.text: imasya sūtrasya ca pūjanārthaṃ susaṃbhavo rāja tadantareṇa

children.text: gṛhṇitva cintāmaṇirājaratnaṃ sarvārthahetoḥ praṇidhiṃ cakāra // Suv_14.22 //
children.translated_text: took the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling jewel), the king of gems, and made an aspiration for the sake of all: // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.22 //

body.translated_text: For the worship of this <s>sūtra</s>, King <s>Susaṃbhava</s> thereupon

body.text: varṣantu adyā iha jambudvipe sasaptaratnāṇi ca bhūṣaṇāni

children.text: ye ceha sattvāḥ khalu jambudvipe sukhitāśca bheṣyanti mahādhanāśca // Suv_14.23 //
children.translated_text: May all those beings here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> become happy and greatly wealthy!' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.23 //

body.translated_text: 'May there rain today here in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> the seven treasures and ornaments!

children.text: caturṣu dvīpeṣu pravarṣitāni saptāni ratnāni tadantareṇa /
children.translated_text: Thereupon, in the four continents, the seven treasures rained down,

children.text: keyūrahārā varakuṇḍalāni tathānnapāne vasanāni caiva // Suv_14.24 //
children.translated_text: armlets, necklaces, and excellent earrings, as well as food, drink, and garments. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.24 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ rāja susaṃbhavaśca ratnapravarṣaṃ khalu jambudvīpe /
children.translated_text: Having seen that jewel-rain in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, King <s>Susaṃbhava</s>

children.text: catvāri dvīpāni saratnapūrṇā niryātayī ratnaśikhisya śāsane // Suv_14.25 //
children.translated_text: gave away the four continents, filled with jewels, in the dispensation of <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.25 //

body.text: ahaṃ ca saḥ śākyamunistathāgataḥ susaṃbhavo nāma babhūva rājā /
body.translated_text: 'I myself am that <s>Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>; I was the king named <s>Susaṃbhava</s>,

body.text: yeneha me tyakta vasuṃdharā tadā catvāri dvīpāni saratnapūrṇā // Suv_14.26 //
body.translated_text: by whom the earth was given away then—the four continents filled with jewels. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.26 //

children.text: akṣobhya āsīt sa tathāgataśca ratnoccayo bhikṣu sa dharmabhāṇakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Akṣobhya</s> was that <s>Tathāgata</s>; and the monk, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, was <s>Ratnoccaya</s>,

children.text: yenāsya rājasya susaṃbhavasya prakāśitaṃ sūtramidaṃ tadāntare // Suv_14.27 //
children.translated_text: by whom this <s>sūtra</s> was illuminated for that King <s>Susaṃbhava</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.27 //

children.text: yanme śrutaṃ sūtramidaṃ tadantare ekāgravācāmanumoditaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Because this <s>sūtra</s> was heard by me at that time and rejoiced in with one-pointed speech,

children.text: tenaiva mahyaṃ kuśalena karmaṇā śrotānumodena śrutena tena // Suv_14.28 //
children.translated_text: by that very wholesome <s>karma</s>, by that hearing and rejoicing— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.28 //

children.text: suvarṇavarṇaṃ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇaṃ labheyi kāyaṃ priyadarśanaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: may I always obtain a body golden-colored, marked with a hundred merits, beautiful to behold,
delightful to the eyes, charming in appearance to people, generating joy for thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>devas</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.29 //
For nine [times] more than a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, I was a <s>Cakravartin</s> king;

children.text: aneka kalpāna sahasrakoṭyo trailokyarājatva mayānubhūtam // Suv_14.30 //
children.translated_text: for many thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, sovereignty over the three worlds was experienced by me. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.30 //

children.text: acintiyā kalpa babhūva śakraḥ tathaiva brahmendra praśāntamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: For inconceivable <s>kalpas</s>, I was <s>Śakra</s>, and likewise <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Indra</s>, of tranquil mind;

children.text: ārāgitā me balāprameyā yeṣāṃ pramāṇaṃ na kadāci vidyate // Suv_14.31 //
children.translated_text: I delighted immeasurable [beings] whose number can never be known. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.31 //

children.text: tathā pramāṇaṃ bahu puṇyaskandhaṃ yanme śrutaṃ sūtranumoditaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Such is the measure of the vast aggregate of merit [gained] from my hearing and rejoicing in this <s>sūtra</s>;

children.text: yathābhiprāyeṇa mi bodhi prāptā saddharmakāyaśca mayā hi labdha // Suv_14.32 //
children.translated_text: in accordance with my aspiration, <s>Bodhi</s> (Awakening) was attained by me, and the <s>Saddharma-kāya</s> (True Dharma Body) was obtained by me. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 14.32 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje susaṃbhavaparivarto nāma caturdaśamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, the <s>Susaṃbhava</s> Chapter, in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // Yakṣāśrayarakṣāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Yakṣāśraya-rakṣā</s> (Yakṣa-Refuge Protection) Chapter //

body.text: yaḥ kaścicchrīmahādevi śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vātītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmacintyāṃ mahatīṃ vipulāṃ vistīrṇāṃ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pūjāṃ karttukāmaḥ syāt / atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ gambhīraṃ buddhagocaraṃ parijñātukāmo bhavet / tenāvaśyaṃ tatra pradeśe vihāre vāraṇyapradeśe vā yatrāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājaḥ vistareṇa saṃprakāśyate / tenāvikṣiptacittenāvirahitaśrotreṇāyaṃ suvarṇaprabhāsottamaḥ sūtrendrarājaḥ śrotavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Whoever, O glorious great goddess <s>Śrī</s>—whether a faithful son of good family or a daughter of good family—desires to make an inconceivable, great, vast, and extensive offering with all requisites to the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present, and who desires to fully comprehend the profound domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present—such a person must necessarily go to that place, monastery, or forest retreat where this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s> is being illuminated at length. With an undistracted mind and ears not turned away, he should listen to this <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānimamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃparidīpayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, elucidating this very matter to an even greater extent, spoke these verses at that time:

children.translated_text: Whoever wishes to make inconceivable offerings to all the <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: gambhīraṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ gocaraṃ ca prajanitum // Suv_15.1 //
children.translated_text: and to comprehend the profound domain of all the <s>Buddhas</s>— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.1 //
let him approach every place—a monastery or a cave—
wherever this <s>sūtra</s>, the supreme <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, is being taught. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.2 //
This <s>sūtra</s> is inconceivable, an ocean of infinite virtues,
the liberator of all beings from the ocean of manifold sufferings. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.3 //
I behold the beginning of this <s>sūtra</s>, its middle, and likewise its end—
this profoundly deep king of <s>sūtras</s>, for which no comparison exists. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.4 //

children.text: na gaṅgārajasā caiva na dharaṇyāṃ na sāgare /
children.translated_text: Not by the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, not by [the dust of] the earth, not by the ocean,
not by anything dwelling in the vault of the sky can any comparison be made. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.5 //
Through entry into the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (Realm of Dharma), one should enter therein,
where the <s>stūpa</s> of the <s>Dharma</s>-essence stands, profound and well-established. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.6 //
And within that <s>stūpa</s>, one would behold the <s>Jina</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>,

children.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśantaṃ manojñena svareṇa ca // Suv_15.7 //
children.translated_text: illuminating this <s>sūtra</s> with a melodious voice. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.7 //
As many <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> as are innumerable and inconceivable,
[for that many], divine and human pleasures are truly experienced. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.8 //

children.text: yadā sa evaṃ jānīyādyattatra sūtra śrūyate /
children.translated_text: When one thus knows that in that place this <s>sūtra</s> is being heard,
[one should reflect:] 'Thus an inconceivable aggregate of merit has been accumulated by me.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.9 //
One should traverse a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, even if covered with a pit of fire,

children.text: yaḥ sakṛcchuṇituṃ sūtraṃ sahetu vedanāṃ bhṛśam // Suv_15.10 //
children.translated_text: in order to hear this <s>sūtra</s> even once, enduring intense suffering. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.10 //
As soon as one enters the monastery or cave [where it is taught],
all evil signs and bad-dream omens depart. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.11 //
The afflictions of planets and constellations, the terrible <s>Kākhorda</s>-seizures,
as soon as one enters—all of these turn away. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.12 //
There one should prepare a seat resembling a lotus,
such as was shown by the <s>Nāga</s>-kings in a dream. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.13 //
Seated upon that seat, one should illuminate this <s>sūtra</s>;
one should have it copied, recited, and likewise studied thoroughly. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.14 //
Even when one has descended from the seat and gone to another place,
miraculous displays are seen upon that very seat. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.15 //
Sometimes the form of the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher is seen there,

children.text: kadācidbuddha rūpaṃ ca bodhisattvaṃ kadācana // Suv_15.16 //
children.translated_text: sometimes a <s>Buddha</s>-form, sometimes a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.16 //
Sometimes the forms of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, sometimes those of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>,
sometimes the forms of <s>Maitreya</s> are seen upon that seat. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.17 //
Sometimes merely a radiance, sometimes a vision of <s>devas</s>,
they are seen for a moment and then vanish again. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 15.18 //
Everywhere accomplishing success, the praiseworthy <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching—
Endowed with grain and auspiciousness, and bringing victory in battle. // Suv_15.19 //
He shall fill all this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with fame,

children.text: sarve ca ripavastasya nirjitā bhonti sarvathā // Suv_15.20 //
children.translated_text: And all his enemies shall be utterly conquered in every way. // Suv_15.20 //
His foes are always slain; he is free from all sin;

children.text: sadā vijitasaṃgrāmaḥ śriyā sa ca pramodati // Suv_15.21 //
children.translated_text: Always victorious in battle, he rejoices with prosperity. // Suv_15.21 //
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the lords of the thirty [gods], the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians) likewise,
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s> the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Saṃjñeya</s>, the bull among men, // Suv_15.22 //
<s>Anavatapta</s> the lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Sāgara</s> likewise,
The lords of <s>Kinnaras</s>, the lords of <s>Suras</s>, and the lords of <s>Garuḍas</s> likewise —

children.text: etāṃśca pramukhān kṛtvā sarvāṇi devatāni ca // Suv_15.23 //
children.translated_text: With these foremost among them, and all the deities too, // Suv_15.23 //

children.text: te ca tā nityaṃ pūjanti dharmastūpamacintiyam /
children.translated_text: They constantly worship the inconceivable <s>Dharma</s>-<s>stūpa</s>,

children.text: praharṣitā bhaviṣyanti dṛṣṭvā sattvāḥ sa gauravāḥ // Suv_15.24 //
children.translated_text: And shall be delighted upon seeing those beings [who are listeners], with reverence. // Suv_15.24 //
All those supreme lords of gods shall also think thus,

children.text: devatāścaiva tāssarvā vakṣyanti ca parasparam // Suv_15.25 //
children.translated_text: And all those deities shall say to one another: // Suv_15.25 //
'See all these [beings], endowed with radiance, splendor, and accumulated merit!
With roots of merit planted, these people have come here.' // Suv_15.26 //
'Those who have come here for the purpose of hearing this profound <s>sūtra</s>,
With inconceivable faith, reverential toward the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>stūpa</s> — // Suv_15.27 //
These are the compassionate ones in the world; these are the benefactors of beings;
These are the feast of the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s> of profound teachings. // Suv_15.28 //
By entering the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth), these [beings] enter [liberation],

children.text: ye śṛṇvanti idaṃ sūtraṃ ye cānyāñśrāvayanti ca // Suv_15.29 //
children.translated_text: Those who hear this <s>sūtra</s> and those who cause others to hear it. // Suv_15.29 //
Hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshipped by them in the past;

children.text: etena kuśalamūlena idaṃ sūtraṃ śṛṇvanti ca // Suv_15.30 //
children.translated_text: By that root of merit, they [now] hear this <s>sūtra</s>.' // Suv_15.30 //

children.text: te sarve devarājendrāḥ sarasvatī tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: All those lords of the gods, and <s>Sarasvatī</s> likewise,
<s>Śrī</s> and <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> too, and the four great sovereign kings — // Suv_15.31 //
With hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, mighty and of great strength,
They shall provide protection for them, day and night, unwearied. // Suv_15.32 //
With the mighty lords of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
And the other twenty-eight, with <s>Saṃjñeya</s> at their head, // Suv_15.33 //
With hundreds of thousands of <s>Yakṣas</s>, mighty and of great strength,

children.text: teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti sarvatrāsabhayeṣu ca // Suv_15.34 //
children.translated_text: They shall provide protection for them against all terrors and fears. // Suv_15.34 //
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>, with five hundred <s>Yakṣas</s> too,
And all the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, shall provide protection for them. // Suv_15.35 //
<s>Maṇibhadra</s>, the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s> likewise,
<s>Kumbhīra</s> and <s>Āṭāvaka</s>, and <s>Piṅgala</s> of great strength — // Suv_15.36 //
Each lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>, surrounded by five hundred <s>Yakṣas</s>,

children.text: teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyati yebhiḥ sūtramidaṃ śrutam // Suv_15.37 //
children.translated_text: Shall provide protection for those by whom this <s>sūtra</s> has been heard. // Suv_15.37 //
The <s>Gandharva</s> <s>Citrasena</s>, <s>Jinarāja</s>, <s>Jinarṣabha</s>,
<s>Maṇikaṇṭha</s> and <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, and the lord of rains too, // Suv_15.38 //
<s>Mahāgrāsa</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and <s>Svarṇakeśin</s> likewise,
<s>Pāñcika</s> and <s>Chagalapāda</s>, and <s>Mahābhāga</s> likewise, // Suv_15.39 //
<s>Praṇālin</s>, <s>Mahāpāla</s>, <s>Markaṭa</s>, and <s>Vālin</s> too,
<s>Sūciroma</s>, <s>Sūryamitra</s>, and <s>Ratnakeśa</s> likewise, // Suv_15.40 //
<s>Mahāpraṇālin</s>, <s>Nakula</s>, <s>Kāmaśreṣṭha</s>, and <s>Candana</s>,
<s>Nāgāyana</s>, <s>Haimavata</s>, and <s>Sātāgiri</s> likewise — // Suv_15.41 //
All of them, mighty and of great strength and valor,

children.text: teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti yeṣāṃ sūtramidaṃ priyam // Suv_15.42 //
children.translated_text: Shall provide protection for those to whom this <s>sūtra</s> is dear. // Suv_15.42 //

children.text: anavatapto hi nāgendraḥ sāgaro 'pi tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>Nāga</s>-lord <s>Anavatapta</s>, and <s>Sāgara</s> likewise,
<s>Mucilinda</s> and <s>Elāpatra</s>, and both <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s> — // Suv_15.43 //
With hundreds of thousands of <s>Nāgas</s>, mighty and of great strength,

children.text: teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti sarvato bhayabhairavāt // Suv_15.44 //
children.translated_text: They shall provide protection for them from every terror and fear. // Suv_15.44 //
<s>Bali</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Namuci</s>, <s>Vemacitra</s>, and <s>Saṃvara</s>,
<s>Prahrāda</s>, <s>Kharaskandha</s>, and other lords of <s>Asuras</s> too — // Suv_15.45 //
With hundreds of thousands of <s>Asuras</s>, mighty and of great strength,
They shall provide protection for them from portents, terrors, and fears. // Suv_15.46 //
<s>Hārītī</s>, the mother of <s>Bhūtas</s>, with her five hundred sons too,

children.text: teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti saptamātṛsthitāni ca // Suv_15.47 //
children.translated_text: Shall provide protection for them, along with the seven mothers. // Suv_15.47 //

children.text: caṇḍā caṇḍālikā caiva yakṣiṇī caṇḍikā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Caṇḍālikā</s>, and the <s>Yakṣiṇī</s> <s>Caṇḍikā</s> too,

children.text: dantī ca kūṭadantī ca sarvasattvaujahāriṇī // Suv_15.48 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dantī</s> and <s>Kūṭadantī</s>, and <s>Sarvasattvaujahāriṇī</s> (the stealer of all beings' vitality) — // Suv_15.48 //
All of these, mighty and of great strength and valor,

children.text: teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti samantena caturdiśaḥ // Suv_15.49 //
children.translated_text: Shall provide protection for them on all sides in the four directions. // Suv_15.49 //

children.text: sarasvatī ca pramukhā devatā ca acintiyā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvatī</s> at their head, and inconceivable deities,

children.text: tathā śrīpramukhāścaiva sarvāṇi devatāni ca // Suv_15.50 //
children.translated_text: And likewise <s>Śrī</s> at their head, and all the deities — // Suv_15.50 //
The earth deities, the deities presiding over fruits and crops,
The deities dwelling in gardens, trees, shrines, and rivers — // Suv_15.51 //
All those hosts of deities, with supremely delighted minds,

children.text: teṣāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyanti yeṣāṃ sūtramidaṃ priyam // Suv_15.52 //
children.translated_text: Shall provide protection for those to whom this <s>sūtra</s> is dear. // Suv_15.52 //

children.text: yojayanti ca te sattvā āyurvarṇabalena ca /
children.translated_text: And they shall endow those beings with lifespan, complexion, and strength,
And constantly adorn them with splendor, merit, radiance, and fortune. // Suv_15.53 //
And they shall pacify all afflictions of planets and constellations,

children.text: alakṣmīpāpaduḥsvapnaṃ sarve te nāśayanti ca // Suv_15.54 //
children.translated_text: And they shall destroy all misfortune, sin, and evil dreams. // Suv_15.54 //
The earth deity, profound and of great strength,
Satisfied by the nectar-essence of the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, // Suv_15.55 //
Sixty-eight thousand [<s>yojanas</s>] and [more] hundreds of <s>yojanas</s>,
Down to the diamond-base, shall be increased with the earth's essences. // Suv_15.56 //
And a full hundred <s>yojanas</s> [of earth] from the surface turns back [downward],

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ snehayate mahī itaḥ sūtraśravaṇabalāt // Suv_15.57 //
children.translated_text: And upward the earth is moistened — by the power of hearing this <s>sūtra</s>. // Suv_15.57 //
And all the deities established in the ten directions,
Satisfied by the nectar-essence of the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, // Suv_15.58 //
Become vigorous and excellent, endowed with splendor, vigor, and strength,
Nourished with happiness, gifted with various delicious essences. // Suv_15.59 //
Throughout this entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the deities of fruits, crops, and forests

children.text: praharṣitā bhaviṣyanti iha sūtre prakāśane // Suv_15.60 //
children.translated_text: Shall be delighted when this <s>sūtra</s> is expounded. // Suv_15.60 //
Crops, grasses, and marvelous flowers,
And various fruit-trees shall grow on all sides. // Suv_15.61 //
All fruit-trees, gardens, and forests
Shall be made to bloom beautifully, delighting [all] with various fragrances. // Suv_15.62 //
With marvelous flowers and marvelous fruits,
All grasses and forest-lords shall grow upon the surface of the earth. // Suv_15.63 //
Throughout this entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, inconceivable <s>Nāga</s>-maidens,
With delighted minds, shall approach the lotus-ponds. // Suv_15.64 //
They shall cause to grow, in all the lotus-ponds,
Marvelous lotuses, night-lilies, blue lotuses, and white lotuses. // Suv_15.65 //

children.text: dhūmātra jālinī muktaṃ bhavate gagaṇaṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: The sky shall become auspicious, freed from mist and haze,
And the directions shall be radiant, freed from darkness and dust. // Suv_15.66 //
The sun, with a thousand rays, supremely radiant with a web of beams,
Shall rise with deep brilliance, bringing delight. // Suv_15.67 //
Stationed within the palace of <s>Jāmbūnada</s>-gold,
The divine sons of <s>Sūryendra</s> (the Sun-lord), satisfied by this <s>sūtra</s>, // Suv_15.68 //
Shall approach <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the lords of <s>sūtras</s>, delighted,
And shall illuminate [it] on all sides with an infinite web of rays. // Suv_15.69 //
As soon as [the sun] awakens, through the impetus of the web of rays,
The lotuses covering the various lotus-ponds shall be awakened. // Suv_15.70 //
Throughout this entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the various crops, fruits, and herbs

children.text: paripācayanti samyak taṃ cātapayate mahim // Suv_15.71 //
children.translated_text: Shall ripen properly, and [the sun] shall warm the earth. // Suv_15.71 //
The moon and sun especially shall illuminate [the space] between them,

children.text: samyagvahanti nakṣatrā vātavarṣaṃ tathaiva ca // Suv_15.72 //
children.translated_text: And the constellations shall move properly, and the wind and rain likewise. // Suv_15.72 //
There shall be abundance everywhere in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>,

children.text: viśeṣeṇa ca tadrāṣṭraṃ yatra sūtramidaṃ bhavet // Suv_15.73 //
children.translated_text: And especially in that kingdom where this <s>sūtra</s> is present. // Suv_15.73 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje yakṣāśrayo nāmarakṣāparivartaḥ pañcadaśamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fifteenth chapter, the <s>Yakṣāśraya</s> Protection Chapter, in the supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Śrī Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>.

body.text: // Daśadevaputrasahasravyākaraṇaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The Chapter on the Prophecy of Ten Thousand Divine Sons //

body.text: evamukte bodhisattvasamuccayā kuladevatā bhagavantametadavocat / kena bhadanta bhagavan hetunā kena kāraṇena kīdṛśenottaptavīryeṇa kuśalamūlena yasya kṛtatvādupacitatvādevatāni jvalanāntaratejorājapramukhāni daśadevaputrasahasrāṇyetarhi trāyastriśaddevabhavanādāgatāni bhagavato 'ntike dharmaśravaṇāyopasaṃkrāmanti /
body.translated_text: When this was said, the family deity <s>Bodhisattvasamuccaya</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'By what cause, Venerable Blessed One, by what reason, and by what kind of zealously exerted root of merit — through having performed and accumulated which — have these ten thousand divine sons, headed by <s>Jvalanāntaratejorāja</s>, now come from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Heaven of the Thirty-Three) divine abode and approached the Blessed One for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>?'

body.text: eteṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ satpuruṣāṇāṃ bodhisattvavyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā bodhau cittamutpādayanti / yathāyaṃ ruciraketuḥ satpuruṣo 'nāgate 'dhvani gaṇanāsamatikrānteṣvanekeṣvasaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣvatikrānteṣu suvarṇaprabhāsitāyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyakyaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭo nāma tathāgato 'rhansamyaksaṃbuddho loka utpatsyate vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavan / yāvattasya bhagavataḥ suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya saddharmāntarhite sarveṇa sarve sarvathā sarvaṃ tasya śāsanasyāntarhitasyāyaṃ rūpyaketurnāma dārakaḥ / tasya tathāgatasyānusaṃghau tatra caiva virajadhvajalokadhātau suvarṇajambudhvajakāñcanābho nāma tathāgato 'rhansamyaksaṃbuddho loka utpatsyate / yāvattasya suvarṇadhvajakāñcanāvabhāsasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya sarveṇa sarve sarvathā sarvaṃ tasya śāsanasyāntarhitasyāyaṃ rūpyaprabho dārakaḥ / tasya tathāgatasyonusaṃghau tatra caiva virajadhvajalokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate / suvarṇaśataraśmiprabhāsagarbho nāma tathāgato 'rhanasamyaksaṃbuddho loka utpasyate vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān // te sarva etarhi bhagavatānuttarāyāṃ samyak saṃbodhau vyākṛtāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Having heard the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-prophecy of these three good men, they have generated the aspiration for awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). Just as this good man <s>Ruciraketu</s>, in the future time, after the passing of innumerable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> beyond reckoning, shall fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) in the world-realm called <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsitā</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭa</s> shall arise in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. And after the passing of that Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭa</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and the complete disappearance of his teaching in every way — this boy named <s>Rūpyaketu</s>, in that very world-realm <s>Virajadhvaja</s>, following that <s>Tathāgata</s>'s community, shall fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Suvarṇajambudhvajakāñcanābha</s> shall arise in the world. And after the passing of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇadhvajakāñcanāvabhāsa</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and the complete disappearance of his teaching in every way — this boy named <s>Rūpyaprabha</s>, in that very world-realm <s>Virajadhvaja</s>, following that <s>Tathāgata</s>'s community, shall fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Suvarṇaśataraśmiprabhāsagarbha</s> shall arise in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. // All of these have now been given the prophecy of unsurpassed perfect awakening by the Blessed One.' //

body.text: na caiteṣāṃ bhadanta bhagavajjvalanāntaratejorājapramukhānāṃ daśānāṃ devaputrasahasrāṇāṃ yāvadvistīrṇā bodhisatvacaryā abhūvan / na ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu pūrvaṃ caritavantaḥ śrutapūrvā abhūvan / nayanacaraṇottamāṅgapriyaputrabhāryāduhitaraḥ parityaktapūrvā na śrūyante / dhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvajravaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍajātarūparajatamarakataratnāni
body.translated_text: 'But, Venerable Blessed One, those ten thousand divine sons headed by <s>Jvalanāntaratejorāja</s> — their <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice was not extensive; they had not previously practiced the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) nor were [such practices] heard of before; they are not heard of as having previously renounced eyes, hands, feet, heads, beloved sons, wives, or daughters. [Nor had they previously given away] wealth, grain, gold, silver, gems, pearls, diamonds, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, refined gold, silver, emeralds, and [other] jewels.'

body.text: parityaktapūrvāṇi na śrūyante / nānānnapānavastrayānaśayanāsanabhavanavimānārāmapuṣkariṇītaḍāgāḥ parityaktapūrvā na śrūiyante / nānāhastigo 'śvavaḍavādāsīdāsāḥ parityaktapūrvā na śrūyante / yathā tānyanekāni bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi pūrveṣvasaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣvanekānāmasaṃkhyeyatathāgatakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāmanekācintyaiḥ nānāvicitraiḥ pūjāśatasahasraiḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pūjāṃ kariṣyanti / sarvaratnaparityāgāni parityajiṣyanti / karacaraṇanayanottamāṅgapriyaputrabhāryāduhitāparityāgāni kariṣyanti / dhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍarajatajātarūpāṇi parityāgāni parityajanti / annapānavastraśayanāsanabhavanavimānārāmodyānapuṣkariṇīhastigavāścavaḍavādāsīdāsaparityāgāni parityakṣyanti / anupūrveṇa ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrayiṣyanti / anupūrveṇa ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrayitvānekāni sukhaśatasahasrāṇyanubhaviṣyanti / yāvadbuddhebhyo bhagavadbhayaḥ tathāgatanāmadheye vyākaraṇaṃ pratilapsyante //
body.translated_text: previously abandoned are not heard of; various foods, drinks, garments, vehicles, bedding, seats, dwellings, mansions, gardens, lotus-ponds, and reservoirs previously abandoned are not heard of; various elephants, cows, horses, mares, female and male servants previously abandoned are not heard of. Just as those many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in former inconceivable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, shall worship many inconceivable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s> with many inconceivable, various, and wonderful hundreds of thousands of offerings and all requisites; shall relinquish all manner of jewel-donations; shall make the sacrifices of hands, feet, eyes, heads, beloved sons, wives, and daughters; shall relinquish donations of wealth, grain, gold, silver, <s>maṇi</s>-gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, silver, and refined gold; shall relinquish donations of food, drink, garments, bedding, seats, dwellings, mansions, gardens, parks, lotus-ponds, elephants, cattle, horses, mares, female and male servants; shall gradually fulfill the six <s>pāramitās</s>; and having gradually fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s>, shall experience many hundreds of thousands of happinesses — until they shall receive from the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, a prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) regarding the name of a <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: tatkena bhadanta bhagavan hetunā kena kāraṇena kīdṛśenoptakuśalamūlena ca tāni jvalanāntarate jorājapramukhāni daśadevaputrasahasrāṇīha bhagavato 'ntikaṃ dharmaśravaṇāyopasaṃkrāmanti / tānyetarhi bhagavatānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtāni / yadutānāgate 'dhvanyanekeṣvasaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasreṣvatikrānteṣu tatreva śālendradhvajāgravatyāṃ lokadhātāvekakulagotraikanāmadheyenānupūrveṇānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / prasannavadanotpalagandhakūṭānāmnā daśasu dikṣu daśabuddhasahasrāṇi loka utpatsyante vidyācaraṇasaṃpannāḥ sugatā lokavido 'nuttarāḥ puruṣadamyasārathayaḥ śāstāro devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddhā bhagavantaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'By what cause, O Venerable Blessed One, by what condition, and by what kind of planted wholesome root did those ten thousand <s>devaputras</s> led by <s>Jvalanāntaratejorāja</s> come here to the Blessed One's presence to hear the <s>Dharma</s>? And they have now been given a prophecy by the Blessed One regarding unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) — namely, that in the future, after innumerable, inconceivable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s> have passed, in that very world-system <s>Śālendradhvajāgravatī</s>, in succession, of one family lineage and one name, they shall fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening. Under the name <s>Prasannavadanotpalagandhakūṭa</s>, ten thousand <s>Buddhas</s> shall arise in the world in the ten directions — endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugatas</s>, knowers of the world, unsurpassed tamers of persons, teachers of <s>devas</s> and humans, <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavāṃstāṃ bodhisattvasamuccayāṃ kuladevatāmetadavocat / asti kuladevate saheturasti tatkāraṇam / asti taduptaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ yasya kṛtatvādupacitatvādetāni jvalanāntaratejorājapramukhāni
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One said to <s>Bodhisattvasamuccayā</s>, the family-deity: 'There is a cause, O family-deity, there is a condition for that. There is a planted wholesome root, by virtue of which having been done and accumulated, these

body.text: daśadevaputrasahasrāṇyetarhi trāyastriṃśadbhavanādiha dharmaśravaṇāyopasaṃkrāmanti / eteṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ satpuruṣāṇāmidaṃ bodhivyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā sahaśravaṇena kuladevate 'sya suvarṇaprabhāsottamasya sūtrendrarājasyāntike citrīkāraprītiprasādapratilabdhā bhavanti / tāvadvimalavaiḍuryasadṛśena pariśuddhacittena samanvāgatā bhavanti / vimalavipulavistīrṇagagaṇakalpasadṛśena gambhīreṇa cittaprasādena samanvāgatā bhavanti / aparimitaṃ ca puṇyaskandhaṃ parigṛhītavanto bhavanti tāvaccaityadaivate jvalanāntaratejorājapramukhāni daśadevaputrasahasrāṇi sahaśravaṇenāsya sūtrendrarājasyāntike citrīkāraprasādapratilabdhā bhavanti / tāvadvimalavaiḍūryasadṛśena pariśuddhena cittena samanvāgatā bhavanti yāvadyākaraṇabhūmimanuprāptāḥ / anena kuladevate dharmaśravaṇakuśalamūlapracayenāpi pūrvapraṇidhānavaśenaitāni jvalanāntaratejorājapramukhāni daśadevaputrasahasrāṇyetarhyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtāni / katamāni ca kuladevate pūrvapraṇidhānānīti /
body.translated_text: ten thousand <s>devaputras</s> led by <s>Jvalanāntaratejorāja</s>, now [dwelling in] the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven, have come here to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Upon hearing the prophecy of awakening (<s>bodhivyākaraṇa</s>) of those three good men, O family-deity, simultaneously with hearing this supreme king of sūtras, the <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama</s>, they obtained wonder, delight, and serene faith. They became endowed with minds as pure as spotless <s>vaiḍūrya</s>. They became endowed with a deep mental serenity, vast, extensive, and resembling the pure, stainless sky. And they accumulated an immeasurable aggregate of merit. O shrine-deity, simultaneously with hearing, the ten thousand <s>devaputras</s> led by <s>Jvalanāntaratejorāja</s> obtained wonder, serene faith before this supreme king of sūtras. They became endowed with pure minds like spotless <s>vaiḍūrya</s> — until they reached the stage of prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇabhūmi</s>). By this accumulation of wholesome roots from hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, O family-deity, and also by the power of their former aspirations (<s>pūrvapraṇidhāna</s>), these ten thousand <s>devaputras</s> led by <s>Jvalanāntaratejorāja</s> have now been given a prophecy regarding unsurpassed perfect awakening. And what, O family-deity, are those former aspirations?'

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje daśadevaputrasahasravyākaraṇaparivartaḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, the <s>Daśadevaputrasahasravyākaraṇa</s> (Prophecy of Ten Thousand <s>Devaputras</s>) Chapter, in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // Vyādhipraśamanaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Vyādhipraśamana</s> (Healing of Diseases) Chapter //

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ kuladevate 'tīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyatarairvipulairacintyairaprameyairyadāsīttena kālena tena samayena ratnaśikhī nāma tathāgato 'rhansamyaksaṃbuddho loka utpanno vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate kālena tena samayena tasya bhagavato ratnaśikhinastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya saddharmasyāntarhitasya saddharmapratirūpake parivartamāne sureśvaraprabho nāma rājā babhūva / dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ pālayamāno nādharmeṇa mātāpitṛkalpaḥ sarvaviṣayavāsināṃ sattvānām //
body.translated_text: 'In the past, O family-deity, in a time more incalculable, vast, inconceivable, and immeasurable than can be told, at that time and on that occasion, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed tamer of persons, teacher of <s>devas</s> and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. At that time, O family-deity, after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaśikhī</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, when the true <s>Dharma</s> had disappeared and the counterfeit of the true <s>Dharma</s> was circulating, there was a king named <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s> — righteous, a <s>Dharma</s>-king, ruling his kingdom by <s>Dharma</s> and not by <s>adharma</s>, like a father and mother to all beings dwelling in his realm.'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate kālena tena samayena tasya rājñaḥ sureśvaraprabhasya viṣaye jaṭiṃdharo nāma śreṣṭhī babhūva //
body.translated_text: 'At that time, O family-deity, in the domain of that King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>, there was a merchant (<s>śreṣṭhī</s>) named <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>.'

body.text: vaidyaḥ cikitsakaḥ paramadhātukuśalo 'ṣṭāṅgenāyurvaidyaśāsreṇa samanvāgato babhūva /
body.translated_text: 'He was a physician, a healer, supremely skilled in the [bodily] elements (<s>dhātus</s>), endowed with the eight-limbed <s>Āyurveda</s> medical science.'

body.text: tena khalu kuladevate kālena tena samayena tasya jaṭiṃdharasya śreṣṭhino jalavāhano nāmnā śreṣṭhiputra utpanno babhūva / abhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkaratayā samanvāgato nānāśāstrakuśalaḥ sarvaśāstragatiṃgato lipisaṃkhyāgaṇanākuśalaḥ sarvaśilpī babhūva / tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate kālena tena samayena tasya rājñaḥ sureśvaraprabhasya viṣaye 'nekāni sattvaśatasahasrāṇi nānārogaspṛṣṭānyabhūvan / nānāvyādhiparipīḍitāni duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāmamanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti //
body.translated_text: 'At that time, O family-deity, to that merchant <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>, a merchant's son named <s>Jalavāhana</s> was born. He was handsome, pleasing, fair to behold, endowed with the supreme beauty of a good complexion like a lotus, skilled in various sciences, versed in all branches of learning, proficient in writing, counting, and arithmetic, and accomplished in all crafts. At that time, O family-deity, in the domain of that King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>, many hundreds of thousands of beings were afflicted by various diseases, tormented by various illnesses, experiencing painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations.'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate kālena tena samayena tasya jalavāhanasya śreṣṭhiputrasya teṣāmanekeṣāṃ sattvaśatasahasrāṇāṃ nānārogaspṛṣṭānāṃ nānāvyādhiparipiḍitānāmarthāya paramakāruṇyaṃ cittamutpanno babhūva / etānyanekāni sattvaśatasahasrāṇi nānārogaspṛṣṭāni nānāvyādhiparipīḍitānyetarhi duḥkhāṃ tīvrāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāmamanāpāṃ vedanāṃ vedayanti / ayaṃ ca mama pitā jaṭiṃdharaḥ śreṣṭhī vaidyavicikitsakaḥ paramadhātukuśalo 'ṣṭāṅgāyurvaidyaśāstreṇa samanvāgato vṛddho jīrṇo
body.translated_text: 'At that time, O family-deity, in the merchant's son <s>Jalavāhana</s>, a mind of supreme compassion arose for those many hundreds of thousands of beings afflicted by various diseases and tormented by various illnesses: "These many hundreds of thousands of beings, afflicted by various diseases, tormented by various illnesses, now experience painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations. And this father of mine, the merchant <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>, is a physician, a healer, supremely skilled in the elements, endowed with the eight-limbed <s>Āyurveda</s> medical science — [but he is] old, aged,

body.text: mahallako 'dhvagato vayo 'nuprāpto jīrṇamavasthāpya pravepamāṇaḥ kāyo yaṣṭimālambya yatra yatra sarvatra grāmanagaranigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣūpasaṃkrāmati / etānyanekāni sattvaśatasahasrāṇi nānārogaspṛṣṭāni nānāvyādhiparipīḍitāni nānāvyādhobhyaḥ parimocayituṃ yaṃ nūnamahamimameva pitaraṃ jaṭiṃdharamupasaṃkramitvādhikauśalyaṃ paripṛccheyam / yena dhātukauśalyena paripṛṣṭenāhaṃ sarvatra grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣūpasaṃkramiṣyāmi / upasaṃkramya tānyanekāni sattvaśatasahasrāṇi nānārogaspṛṣṭāni nānāvyādhiparipīḍitāni nānāvyādhibhyaḥ parimocayiṣyāmi /
body.translated_text: decrepit, advanced in years, reached the end of his life-span; having placed aside his worn-out, trembling body, leaning on a staff, he goes everywhere — to villages, cities, market-towns, districts, and royal capitals. [I should think:] 'Suppose I were to approach this very father of mine, <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>, and inquire about the higher skill [in medicine]! With that skill in the elements (<s>dhātukauśalya</s>) that I have inquired about, I shall go everywhere — to villages, cities, market-towns, districts, regions, and royal capitals. Having gone, I shall liberate those many hundreds of thousands of beings afflicted by various diseases, tormented by various illnesses, from their various diseases."'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate kālena tena samayena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputro yena svapitā jaṭiṃdharaḥ śreṣṭhī tenopajagāma / upetya svapiturjaṭiṃdharasya pādau śirasā vanditvā kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvaikānte 'sthāt / ekānte sthito jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputraḥ svapitaraṃ jaṭiṃdharaṃ śreṣṭhinamimābhirgāthābhirdhātukauśalyaṃ pṛcchati sma //
body.translated_text: 'At that time, O family-deity, the merchant's son <s>Jalavāhana</s> approached his own father, the merchant <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of his own father <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>, he stood to one side with palms joined. Standing to one side, the merchant's son <s>Jalavāhana</s> asked his own father, the merchant <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>, about the skill in the elements (<s>dhātukauśalya</s>) with these verses:'

children.translated_text: 'Those sense-faculties (<s>indriyas</s>) are observed, and the bodily elements (<s>dhātus</s>) undergo transformation;

children.text: kena kālena jāyante vyādhayaśca śarīriṇām // Suv_17.1 //
children.translated_text: at what time do diseases arise in embodied beings?' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.1 //

children.text: bhojanaṃ ca kathaṃ bhuktvā kāle kāle sukhāvaham /
children.translated_text: 'And how, having eaten food that brings comfort at the proper time,
is the body's inner fire not impaired?' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.2 //

children.text: kathaṃ cikitsā kartavyā vāte pitte śleṣmike tathā /
children.translated_text: 'How should treatment be administered for wind (<s>vāta</s>), bile (<s>pitta</s>), and phlegm (<s>śleṣma</s>) alike?
When a combined disorder (<s>saṃnipāta</s>) has arisen, how should one proceed for the pacification of disease?' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.3 //

children.text: kiṃ kāle kupyate vātaḥ pittaṃ kupyate kadā /
children.translated_text: 'At what time does wind (<s>vāta</s>) become aggravated? When does bile (<s>pitta</s>) become aggravated?

children.text: kiṃ kāle kupyate śleṣmā yena pīḍyanti mānavāḥ // Suv_17.4 //
children.translated_text: At what time does phlegm (<s>śleṣma</s>) become aggravated, by which people are afflicted?' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.4 //

body.text: atha khalu jaṭiṃdharaḥ śreṣṭhī jalavāhanasya śreṣṭhiputrasyābhirgāthābhirdhātukauśalyaṃ viditvā deśayate sma //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>, understanding the merchant's son <s>Jalavāhana</s>'s [request] through these verses, taught the skill in the elements (<s>dhātukauśalya</s>):

children.text: varṣā cātra trayo māsāstrayaśca śāradaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Three months constitute the rainy season, and three are known as autumn;
three likewise are winter, and three are the summer season.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.5 //
'Such is the sequence of months: six seasons are known, comprising the twelve months of a year.

children.text: annaṃ ca pānaṃ ca tathā ca jīryate vaidyāśca kauśalyasmṛtipradarśitāḥ // Suv_17.6 //
children.translated_text: Food and drink are digested accordingly, and physicians are guided by skill and mindfulness.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.6 //
'And at the seasonal junctures within the year, the sense-faculties and elements also undergo transformation.

children.text: parivartamānāni ca indriyāṇi vicitravyādhirbhavate śarīriṇām // Suv_17.7 //
children.translated_text: As the sense-faculties transform, various diseases arise in embodied beings.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.7 //

children.text: tatraiva vaidyasya catuḥ prakāraṃ trimāsaparvāntare ṣaḍṛtūni /
children.translated_text: 'Therein, the physician's four-fold approach [applies] across the six seasons at three-month intervals.
The skill in the six elements (<s>ṣaḍdhātukauśalya</s>) should be known, together with proper food and medicine in due sequence.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.8 //

children.text: vātādhikārāḥ prabhavanti varṣe pattiprakopaḥ śaradi prasanne /
children.translated_text: 'Wind-disorders (<s>vātādhikāra</s>) arise in the rains; bile aggravation occurs in clear autumn;

children.text: hemantakāle tatha saṃnipātaṃ kaphādhikārāśca bhavanti grīṣme // Suv_17.9 //
children.translated_text: combined disorders (<s>saṃnipāta</s>) in the winter season; and phlegm-disorders (<s>kaphādhikāra</s>) occur in summer.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.9 //

children.text: snigdhoṣṇalavaṇāmlarasāśca varṣe śaratsu snigdhaṃ madhuraṃ ca śītam /
children.translated_text: 'In the rainy season: unctuous, hot, salty, and sour flavors; in autumn: unctuous, sweet, and cool;

children.text: madhurāmlasnigdhaṃ ca hemantakāle rūkṣoṣṇakaṭukāni ca grīṣmakāle // Suv_17.10 //
children.translated_text: in winter: sweet, sour, and unctuous; and in summer: rough, hot, and pungent.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.10 //

children.text: kaphādhikaḥ kupyati bhuktamātre pittādhikaṃ kupyati jīryamāṇe /
children.translated_text: 'Phlegm-dominant [disorder] is aggravated right after eating; bile-dominant is aggravated during digestion;

children.text: vātādhikaḥ kupyati jīrṇamātre ityeva dhātutritayaprakopaḥ // Suv_17.11 //
children.translated_text: wind-dominant is aggravated after digestion is complete — such is the aggravation of the three elements (<s>dhātutritaya</s>).' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.11 //

children.text: saṃbṛhaṇaṃ kurvatu nirātmakasya virecanaṃ pittavivardhanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'One should apply nourishment (<s>saṃbṛhaṇa</s>) for the depleted; purgation (<s>virecana</s>) for increased bile;

children.text: triguṇopapannaṃ tatha saṃnipāte praśamaṃ ca kuryātkaphaparvamantare // Suv_17.12 //
children.translated_text: a threefold approach for combined disorders; and pacification should be applied during the phlegm season.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.12 //
'Wind-dominant, bile-combination, and phlegm-dominant [disorders] at their respective seasons should be recognized.

children.text: yatkāla yaddhātu yadāśrayaṃ ca tadannapānauṣadhi darśitavyamiti // Suv_17.13 //
children.translated_text: According to the time, the element, and the bodily condition, the appropriate food, drink, and medicine should be prescribed.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 17.13 //

body.text: atha khalu jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputrastenaivaṃrūpeṇa naimittikena dhātukauśalyena paripṛṣṭena sarvāṣṭāṅgāyurvaidyamadhigato 'bhūt / tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate kālena tena samayena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputro rājñaḥ sureśvaraprabhasya viṣaye sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣūpasaṃkramitvā sarveṣāmanekeṣāṃ sattvaśatasahasrāṇāṃ nānārogaspṛṣṭānāṃ nānāvyādhiparipīḍitānāmevamāśvāsayāmāsa / mā bhaiṣurvaidyo 'smi vaidyo 'smītyātmānaṃ pratijñātavānahaṃ yuṣmākaṃ nānāvyādhibhyaḥ parimocayiṣyāmi / sahaśravaṇena kuladevate tasya jalavāhanasya śreṣṭhiputrasyedamevaṃrūpaṃ vacanaṃ vyāharamāṇasya sarvāṇi tānyanekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi mahāpraharṣajātāni babhūvuḥ / āśvāsaprāptānyacintyaprītisaumanasyena samanvāgatāni babhūvuḥ / tāni tena kālena tena samayena tayā praharṣayānekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi nānārogaspṛṣṭāni nānāvyādhiparipīḍitāni nānārogebhyaḥ parimocayitānyarogāṇi ca babhūvurvigatavyādhīni ca / yathā paurāṇena sthāmabalavīryeṇa samanvāgatāni babhūvuḥ / tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate kālena tena samayena teṣāmanekeṣāṃ ca sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ nānārogaspṛṣṭānāṃ nānāvyādhiparipīḍitānāṃ ye kecidgāḍhatareṇa spṛṣṭā ca babhūvuḥ / te sarve yena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputrastenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramyaiva ye ca kiṃcitteṣāṃ
body.translated_text: Then <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, having been instructed through such skillful understanding of the elements by the diviner, mastered the complete eightfold <s>Āyurveda</s> (science of medicine). Furthermore, O family deity, at that time and on that occasion, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, traveled throughout all the villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals in the domain of King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>, and reassured many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of beings afflicted by various diseases and tormented by various ailments, saying: 'Fear not! I am a physician, I am a physician!' He declared himself [thus]: 'I shall liberate you from your various ailments.' As soon as they heard, O family deity, these words uttered by <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, all those many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of beings were filled with great joy, obtained comfort, and were endowed with inconceivable delight and gladness. At that time and on that occasion, through that joy, those many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of beings who had been afflicted by various diseases and tormented by various ailments were freed from their various diseases—they became free from illness and rid of ailments, and were endowed with their former firmness, strength, and vigor. Furthermore, O family deity, at that time and on that occasion, among those many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of beings who had been afflicted by various diseases and tormented by various ailments, whoever had been seized by more severe [illness]—all of them approached <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son; and having approached, for whatever among those hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of beings

body.text: sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ nānārogaspṛṣṭānāṃ nānāvyādhiparipīḍitānāmauṣadhividhānānyabhinirdiśanti sma / tattāsu rājadhānīṣu sarvāṇi tānyanekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi nānārogaspṛṣṭāni nānāvyādhiparipīḍitāni jalavāhanena śreṣṭhiputreṇa nānāvyādhibhyaḥ parimocitāni babhūvuriti //
body.translated_text: afflicted by various diseases and tormented by various ailments, he prescribed medicinal remedies. Thus, in those royal capitals, all those many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭī-niyutas</s> of beings afflicted by various diseases and tormented by various ailments were freed by <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, from their various ailments.

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje vyādhipraśamana parivarto nāma saptadaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, the <s>Vyādhipraśamana</s> (Pacification of Disease) Chapter, in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // Jalavāhanasya matsyavaineyaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Jalavāhana-matsyaviney</s>a (Conversion of the Fish by <s>Jalavāhana</s>) Chapter //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kuladevate rājñaḥ sureśvaraprabhasya viṣaye jalavāhanena śreṣṭhidārakeṇa sarvasattvā ārogāḥ kṛtā alpā bādhā yathāpūrveṇotsāhabalakāyena saṃvṛtāḥ sarva utsāhasukhena ramanti sma / krīḍanti sma / paricārayanti sma / dānāni ca dadanti sma / puṇyāni ca kurvanti sma / jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako mahāvaidyadānānāṃ ca sukhānāṃ vyādhivicikitsako niyatapratyakṣeṇa bodhisattvena bhavitavyam / sarvenāṣṭāṅgāyurvaidyamadhigato 'bhūt / tasya khalu punaḥ jalavāhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya jalāmbujagarbhā nāma bhāryā 'bhūt / tasya khalu punaḥ kuladevate jalāmbujagarbhāyā dvau dārakau putrāvabhūtām / eko jalāmbaro nāma dvitīyo jalagarbho nāma //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O family deity, in the domain of King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>, after <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, had made all beings free from disease and their ailments were slight, and they were endowed with their former vigor, strength, and bodily power—all of them delighted in vigorous happiness, they played, they engaged in pastimes, and they gave gifts and performed meritorious deeds. <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, the great physician, the bestower of gifts and pleasures, the investigator of diseases, must have been a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of certain and direct [insight]. He had mastered the entire eightfold <s>Āyurveda</s>. Now, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, had a wife named <s>Jalāmbujagarbhā</s>. Furthermore, O family deity, <s>Jalāmbujagarbhā</s> had two sons. One was named <s>Jalāmbara</s>, and the second was named <s>Jalagarbha</s>.

body.text: atha khalu punaḥ kuladevate jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputrasyābhyāṃ dārakābhyāṃ sārdhamanupūrveṇa grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣvanucaṅkramati //
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, wandered about gradually through the villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals, together with those two boys [his sons].

body.text: atha khalu punaḥ kuladevate 'pareṇa tena kālena tena samayena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputro 'nyataramaṭavīkāntāraprāpto 'dhvani dadarśātrāntare māṃsabhakṣā vṛkaśṛgālakākapakṣiṇastāṃ diśaṃ dhāvanti yatrāṭavīkāntāre 'ṭavīsaṃbhavā puṣkariṇī / tadṛṭaṣṭvā tasyaitadabhūt / kasyārthamime māṃsabhakṣā vṛkaśṛgālakākapakṣiṇa imāṃ diśaṃ dhāvanti / tasyaitadabhūt / yaṃ nūnamahaṃ tāṃ diśamupasaṃkrameyam / yasyāṃ diśīme maṃsabhakṣāśca vṛkaśṛgālakākapakṣiṇo dhāvanti //
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, at another time and on another occasion, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, arrived at a certain wilderness along the road, and there in that place he saw flesh-eating wolves, jackals, crows, and birds running toward the direction where in the wilderness there was a forest-born lake. Having seen this, this thought occurred to him: 'For what purpose are these flesh-eating wolves, jackals, crows, and birds running in this direction?' Then this thought occurred to him: 'I should certainly approach that direction where these flesh-eating wolves, jackals, crows, and birds are running.'

body.text: atha khalu punaḥ kuladevate jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputro 'nupūrveṇānucaṅkramannanuvicaranyatrāṭavīsaṃbhavā puṣkariṇī tatra saṃprāptaḥ / tatra mahāpuṣkariṇyāṃ daśamatsyasahasrāṇi prativasanti sma / sa tatrāpaśyadbahūni matsyaśatāni jalaviprahīṇāni tatrāsya kāruṇyacittamutpannam / tatrādrākṣīdardhakāyāṃ devatāṃ niṣkramantīm / sā ca devatā jalavāhanaṃ śreṣṭhidārakametadavocat / sādhu sādhu
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, wandering and walking about gradually, arrived at the place where the forest-born lake was. In that great lake, ten thousand fish were dwelling. There he saw many hundreds of fish deprived of water, and compassion arose in him. There he saw a tree-deity emerging with half her body [visible]. That deity said this to <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant: 'Excellent, excellent,

body.text: kulaputra yastvaṃ jalavāhano nāma matsyānāmudakaṃ prayaccha / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ jalavāhana ityucyate / yaścodakaṃ vāhayati tataḥ svanāmānurūpaṃ kula / jalavāhanaḥ prāha / kiyantīmāni devate matsyāni / devatā prāha / paripūrṇāni daśamatsyasahasrāṇi //
body.translated_text: O son of good family! You who are named <s>Jalavāhana</s> (Water-Bearer)—give water to the fish! For two reasons are you called <s>Jalavāhana</s>: because you carry (<s>vāhayati</s>) water (<s>jala</s>). Therefore act in accordance with your name, O noble one!' <s>Jalavāhana</s> said: 'How many are these fish, O deity?' The deity replied: 'A full ten thousand fish.'

body.text: atha khalu kuladevate jalavāhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya bhūyasyā mātrayā paramakāruṇyacittamutpannam / tena khalu punaḥ kuladevate samayenāṭavīsaṃbhavāyāṃ puṣkariṇyā kiṃcinmātramavaśiṣṭamudakamabhūt / tāni daśamatsyasahasrāṇi mṛtyumukhapraviṣṭāni jalaviprahīṇāni dhāvanti //
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, in <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, an even greater mind of supreme compassion arose. Furthermore, O family deity, at that time, only a tiny amount of water remained in the forest-born lake. Those ten thousand fish, having entered the jaws of death, were floundering about, deprived of water.

body.text: atha khalu kuladevate jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaścaturdiśaṃ dhāvati sma / yasyāṃ diśi jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'nucaṅkamati tasyāṃ diśi daśamtsyasahasrāṇi jalavāhanaṃ karuṇaṃ prekṣante // atha khalu kuladevate jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakaścaturdiśaṃ dhāvati sma / udakaṃ preṣayamāṇo na caivātrodakamupalabhyate / caturdiśaṃ prekṣate / so 'drākṣīnnātidūre mahāntaṃ vṛkṣasamūhaṃ taṃ vṛkṣamabhiruhya drumaśākhāñchittvā yena sā puṣkariṇī tenopajagāma / upagamya teṣāṃ daśānāṃ matsyasahasrāṇāṃ drumaśākhābhiḥ suśītalāñchāyāṃ kṛtavān //
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, ran in the four directions. In whichever direction <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, walked, in that direction the ten thousand fish gazed at <s>Jalavāhana</s> with pitiful eyes. Then, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, ran in the four directions, seeking to send water, but water could not be found anywhere. He looked in the four directions. He saw, not too far away, a great grove of trees. Having climbed that tree and cut its branches, he went to where that lake was. Having arrived, he made cool shade with the tree-branches for those ten thousand fish.

body.text: atha khalu kuladevate jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastasyāṃ puṣkariṇyāmudakāgamaṃ paryeṣate kuta udakasyāgamanaṃ bhavet / caturdiśaṃ dhāvati na codakamupalabhyate / sa śīghraṃ śīghraṃ tamudakastrotaṃ samanugacchati / tasyāḥ khalu punaḥ kuladevate aṭavīsaṃbhavāyāḥ puṣkariṇyā jalāgamā nāma mahānadī yatastasyāmudakasyāgamanam / tena ca samayena sā ndyanyatareṇa pāpasattvena teṣāṃ daśānāṃ matsyasahasrāṇāmarthena sā nadītyadṛṣṭe sthāne mahāprapāte pātitā yatteṣāṃ matsyānāṃ na bhūya udakasyāgamanaṃ bhaviṣyati / sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā cintayati na śakyata eṣā nadī janasahasreṇāpi tenaiva yathā vāhayituṃ kimaṅga punarmayaikena śakyo bāhayituṃ sa pratinivṛttaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, searched for the source of the water in that lake—from where the water might come. He ran in the four directions, but water could not be found. He quickly, quickly followed that water-course. Now, O family deity, there was a great river called <s>Jalāgamā</s> from which the water came to that forest-born lake. But at that time, that river had been diverted by a certain evil person for the purpose [of killing] those ten thousand fish, [causing it to flow] to an unseen place, a great precipice, so that water would no longer come to those fish. Having seen this, he reflected: 'This river cannot be redirected back to its course even by a thousand people—how much less can I alone do it!' And so he turned back.

body.text: atha khalu kuladevate jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputraḥ śīghraṃ śīghramupasaṃkrānto yena rājā
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, quickly, quickly approached King

body.text: sureśvaprabhastenopajagāma / upagamya rājñaḥ sureśvaraprabhasya pādau śirasā natvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ / imāṃ prakṛtimārocayāti sma / mayā khalu devasya viṣaye sarvagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu sattvānāṃ vyādhayaḥ praśamitāḥ / tatrāmuṣminsthāne 'ṭavīsaṃbhavā nāma puṣkariṇī / tatra daśamatsyasahasrāṇi prativasanti jalaprahīṇānyādityaparitāpitāni / taddadātu me devo viṃśatigajā yathā teṣāṃ tiryagyonigatānāṃ jīvitaṃ dadāmīti / yathā manuṣyāṇāṃ dattamājñaptaṃ khalu rājñā sureśvaraprabheṇāmātyānāṃ dadata mahāvaidyarājasya viṃśatigajān / amātyā āhuḥ / upasaṃkrama mahāsattva yena hastiśālā upagṛhṇīṣva viṃśatigajān kuru sattvānāṃ sukham //
body.translated_text: <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s> and went to him. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>, and sitting to one side, he reported this matter: 'I, Your Majesty, have pacified the diseases of beings in all the villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals throughout Your Majesty's domain. In such-and-such a place there is a forest-born lake called [<s>Aṭavīsaṃbhavā</s>]. There, ten thousand fish dwell, deprived of water, scorched by the heat of the sun. May Your Majesty grant me twenty elephants, so that I may give life to those beings born in animal existence.' As for humans, it had been given—King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s> commanded the ministers: 'Give twenty elephants to the great physician-king!' The ministers said: 'Approach, O great being! Go to the elephant stable and take twenty elephants. Bring happiness to the beings!'

body.text: atha khalu kuladevate jalavāhanaḥ sārdhaṃ jalāmbareṇa ca svaputreṇa viṃśatigajān gṛhītvā nāgaśauṇḍikānāṃ sakāśācchataśo dṛśīnāṃ pratigṛhya pratinivṛttaḥ / yatra jalāgamā nāma mahānadī pravahati / tatropasaṃkramyodakena tā dṛtīḥ pūrayitvā gajapṛṣṭha udakamāropya śīghraṃ śīghraṃ yenāṭavīsaṃbhavā puṣkariṇī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya tadudakaṃ hastipṛṣṭhādavatārya tāṃ puṣkariṇīṃ caturdiśamudakena pūrayitvā caturdiśaṃ ca kramati / yena yena jalavāhano 'nucaṅkramati tena tena daśamatsyasahasrāṇyanudhāvanti //
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, together with his son <s>Jalāmbara</s>, took twenty elephants, received from the elephant-keepers hundreds of water-skins, and turned back. He went to where the great river called <s>Jalāgamā</s> flowed. Having approached, he filled those water-skins with water, loaded the water upon the elephants' backs, and quickly, quickly went to where the forest-born lake was. Having arrived, he unloaded that water from the elephants' backs, filled that lake with water on all four sides, and walked about in the four directions. Wherever <s>Jalavāhana</s> walked, in that [direction] the ten thousand fish followed after him.

body.text: atha khalu kuladevate jalavāhanasyaitadabhavat / kimarthametāni daśamatsyasahasrāṇi yenāhaṃ tena pradhāvanti / tasya punaretadabhavat / nūnamete matsyāḥ kṣudhāgninā paripīḍitā mama sakāśādbhojanaṃ parimārgayanti / yannūnamahaṃ bhojanaṃ prayaccheyam //
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, this thought occurred to <s>Jalavāhana</s>: 'For what reason do these ten thousand fish run toward me wherever I go?' Then this thought occurred to him: 'Surely these fish, tormented by the fire of hunger, are seeking food from me. I should certainly give them food.'

body.text: atha khalu kuladevate jalavāhanaḥ svaputraṃ jalāmbarametadavocat / gaccha kulaputra svakaṃ niveśanaṃ sarvabalataraṃ hastinamabhirūhya ca śīdhraṃ śīghramupasaṃkramya pitāmahasya śreṣṭhina evaṃ vadeha bho tāta jalavāhana evaṃ vadati yatkiṃcidatra gṛhe 'bhisaṃskṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ syānmātāpitrorbhrātṛbhaginyordāsīdāsakarmakarasya
body.translated_text: Then, O family deity, <s>Jalavāhana</s> said this to his son <s>Jalāmbara</s>: 'Go, O son of good family, to your own dwelling. Mount the strongest elephant and quickly, quickly approach your grandfather, the merchant, and say to him thus: "Dear grandfather, <s>Jalavāhana</s> says this: Whatever cooked food there may be here in the house—belonging to mother and father, brothers and sisters, maidservants, manservants, and laborers—

body.text: kṛtaśaḥ sarvamekatra piṇḍīkṛtvā jalāmbarasya hastipṛṣṭamavaropya jalavāhanāya śīghraṃ śīghraṃ visarjaya //
body.translated_text: gather all of it together in portions, load it upon the back of <s>Jalāmbara</s>'s elephant, and send it quickly, quickly to <s>Jalavāhana</s>."'

body.text: atha khalu jalāmbaro dārako hastinamabhiruhya śīghraṃ śīghraṃ dhāvati sma / yena svakaṃ niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmadupasaṃmyaitāṃ prakṛtaṃ pitāmahasyāgra ārocayāmāsa vistareṇa yathā pūrvoktam / tatsarvaṃ pitāmahena jalāmbarāya visarjitam //
body.translated_text: Then the boy <s>Jalāmbara</s>, mounting an elephant, rode quickly, quickly. He went to his own dwelling and, having arrived, reported this matter in full before his grandfather, in detail as previously described. All of that was dispatched by the grandfather for <s>Jalāmbara</s>.

body.text: atha khalu jalambaro dārakastadbhojanaṃ hastipṛṣṭhamupanāmya hastinamabhiruhya yenāṭavīsaṃbhavā puṣkariṇī tenopasaṃkrāmat //
body.translated_text: Then the boy <s>Jalāmbara</s>, loading that food upon the elephant's back and mounting the elephant, went to where the forest-born lake was.

body.text: atha khalu jalavāhanaḥ svakaṃ putraṃ jalāmbaramāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭastuṣṭa udagraḥ putrasyāntikādbhojanaṃ pratigṛhya cchittvā tatra puṣkariṇyāṃ prakṣipati sma / tenāhāreṇa tāni daśamatsyasahasrāṇi saṃtarpitāni / punastasyaitadabhavat / śrutaṃ me pareṇa kālasamayenāraṇyāyatane bhikṣurmahāyānadhārayamāna ityāha / yo ratnaśikhinastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya maraṇakālasamaye nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyāt / sa svargaloka upapatsyatīti / yannūnamahameṣāṃ matsyānāṃ gambhīraṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ dharmaṃ deśayeyam / ratnaśikhinastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya nāmadheyaṃ śrāvayeyam / tena ca samayena tasmiñjambudvīpe dvighādṛṣṭiḥ sattvānāmabhūt / kecinmahāyānamabhiśraddhayanti kecitkleśayanti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Jalavāhana</s>, seeing his own son <s>Jalāmbara</s> arrived, was delighted, pleased, and overjoyed. Having received food from his son, he cut it up and cast it into that lake. By that nourishment, those ten thousand fish were satisfied. Then this thought occurred to him: 'I have heard that in a past time, in a forest hermitage, a monk who upheld the <s>Mahāyāna</s> said thus: "Whoever hears the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, at the time of death, shall be reborn in the heavenly world."
