Why should I not teach these fish the profound <s>dharma</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) and cause them to hear the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One?' At that time, in that <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, beings held two views: some had faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, while others disparaged it.

body.text: atha khalu punarjalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputrastasyāṃ velāyāmubhau pādau jānumātraṃ tatra puṣkariṇyāṃ praveśyaivaṃ cidānamudānayāmāsa / namastasya bhagavato ratnaśikhinastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya purvabodhisattvacaryāṃ caramāṇasya evaṃ praṇidhānamabhūt / ye keciddaśasu dikṣu maraṇakālasamaye mama nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyuste tataścyutvā devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupapadyeyuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, at that moment entered both his feet knee-deep into that lake and uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>): 'Homage to the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One! When practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path in former times, he made this vow: "Whoever in the ten directions hears my name at the time of death, departing from there, shall be reborn in the assembly of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods."'

body.text: atha khalu jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakasteṣāṃ tiryagyonigatānāmimaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma / yadutāsmādidaṃ bhavatyasyotpādādidamutpadyate / yadutāvidyāpratyayā saṃskārā / saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam / vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam / nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam / ṣaḍāyatanapratyaya sparśaḥ / sparśapratyayā vedanā / vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā / tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam / upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ / bhavapratyayā jātiḥ / jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā bhavatyevamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati yadutāvidyānirodhātsaṃrakāranirodhaḥ / saṃskāranirodhādvijñānanirodhaḥ / vijñānanirodhānnāmarūpanirodhaḥ / nāmarūpanirodhātṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ / ṣaḍāyatananirodhātsparśanirodhaḥ / sparśanirodhādvedanānirodhaḥ / vedanānirodhāttṛṣṇānirodhaḥ / tṛṣṇānirodhādupādānanirodhaḥ / upādānanirodhādbhavanirodhaḥ / bhavanirodhājjātinirodhaḥ / jātinirodhājjarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyate / kevalamasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati / iti hi kuladevate tena kālena tena samayena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputrasteṣāṃ tiryagyonigatānāmimāṃ dhārmikakathāṃ kathayati sma / sārdhaṃ putrābhyāṃ jalāmbareṇa jalagarbheṇa ca punarapi svagṛhamanuprāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, taught this <s>dharma</s> to those born in animal existence: 'When this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises. That is: from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as condition arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); from <s>saṃskāras</s> as condition arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); from <s>vijñāna</s> as condition arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); from <s>nāmarūpa</s> as condition arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases); from the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> as condition arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); from <s>sparśa</s> as condition arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); from <s>vedanā</s> as condition arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); from <s>tṛṣṇā</s> as condition arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging); from <s>upādāna</s> as condition arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); from <s>bhava</s> as condition arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); from <s>jāti</s> as condition arise old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair—thus arises this entire great mass of suffering. From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>; from the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s> comes the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s>; from the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s> comes the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s>; from the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s> comes the cessation of the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>; from the cessation of the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> comes the cessation of <s>sparśa</s>; from the cessation of <s>sparśa</s> comes the cessation of <s>vedanā</s>; from the cessation of <s>vedanā</s> comes the cessation of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>; from the cessation of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> comes the cessation of <s>upādāna</s>; from the cessation of <s>upādāna</s> comes the cessation of <s>bhava</s>; from the cessation of <s>bhava</s> comes the cessation of <s>jāti</s>; from the cessation of <s>jāti</s>, old age, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair cease—thus comes the cessation of this entire great mass of suffering.' Thus, O family deity, at that time and on that occasion, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, taught this <s>dhārmic</s> discourse to those born in animal existence. Together with his two sons, <s>Jalāmbara</s> and <s>Jalagarbha</s>, he returned again to his own home.

body.text: athāpareṇa kālena samayena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhiputro mahotsavaṃ paribhujya mahotsavamatto śayane śayitaḥ / tena ca kālena tena samayena mahānimittaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ / yattasyā rātryāmatyayena tāni daśamatsyasahasrāṇi kālagatāni deveṣu trāyastriṃśatsu sabhāgatāyāmupapannāni / sahopapannānāṃ caiṣāmevaṃrūpaścetasaḥ parivitarka utpannaḥ / kena vayaṃ kuśalakarmahetuneha deveṣu trāyastriṃśeṣūpapannāḥ / teṣāmetadabhūt / vayamasmiñjambudvīpe daśamatsyasahasrāṇyabhūvan / te vayaṃ tiryagyonigatā jalavāhanena śreṣṭhidārakeṇa prabhūtenodakena saṃtarpitā bhojanavareṇa ca / gambhīraścāsmākaṃ pratītyasamutpādadharmo deśitaḥ / ratnaśikhinastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya nāmadheyaṃ śrāvitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then at another time and on another occasion, <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the merchant's son, having enjoyed a great festival, intoxicated by the great festival, lay upon his bed. At that time and on that occasion, a great omen appeared. For at the passing of that night, those ten thousand fish died and were reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods in their assembly. Immediately upon their rebirth, this thought and reflection arose in their minds: 'By what wholesome <s>karma</s> have we been reborn here among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods?' This occurred to them: 'We were ten thousand fish in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. We, born in animal existence, were nourished by <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, with abundant water and with excellent food. And the profound <s>dharma</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) was taught to us. We were caused to hear the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

body.text: tena kuśaladharmahetunā tena pratyayeneha vayaṃ deveṣūpapannāḥ / yannūnaṃ vayaṃ yena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārakastenopasaṃkramemaḥ / upasaṃkramya tasya pūjāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: By that wholesome <s>dharma</s> as cause and condition, we have been reborn here among the gods. Let us now approach <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, and having approached, we shall offer worship to him.'

body.text: atha tāni daśadevaputrasahasrāṇi deveṣu trāyastriṃśatsvantarhitāni jalavāhanasya śriṣṭhino gṛhe tasthuḥ / tena khalu punaḥ samayena ca jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭyupaśayane śayitaḥ / tasyaitairdevaputrairdaśamuktāhārasahasrāṇi śīrṣānte sthāpitāni / daśamuktāhārasahasrāṇi pādatale sthāpitāni / daśamuktāhārasahasrāṇi dakṣiṇapārśve sthāpitāni / daśamuktāhārasahasrāṇi vāmapārśve sthāpitāni / gṛhāntare jānumātraṃ māndāravapuṣpavarṣaṃ prāvarṣat / divyāśca dundubhayaḥ parāhatāḥ / yena sarve jambudvītāḥ prativibuddhāḥ / atha jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhī prativibuddhaṃ //
body.translated_text: Then those ten thousand god-sons vanished from the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven and stood in the house of <s>Jalavāhana</s> the merchant. At that time, <s>Jalavāhana</s> the merchant was lying on his couch. By those god-sons, ten thousand pearl necklaces were placed at his head; ten thousand pearl necklaces were placed at his feet; ten thousand pearl necklaces were placed at his right side; ten thousand pearl necklaces were placed at his left side. Inside the house, a shower of <s>Māndārava</s> flowers fell knee-deep. And divine drums were sounded, by which all the inhabitants of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> were awakened. Then <s>Jalavāhana</s> the merchant was awakened.

body.text: atha tāni daśadevaputrasahasrāṇi khagapathenopakrāntāni / te ca devaputrā rājñaḥ sureśvaraprabhasya viṣaye sthānasthānāntare māndāravapuṣpavarṣaṃ pravarṣayanto yenāṭavīsaṃbhavā puṣkariṇī tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ te tatra puṣkariṇyāṃ māndāravapuṣpaṃ pravarṣayantastata evāntarhitāḥ punarapi devālayaṃ gatāḥ / tatra pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇai ramanti sma / krīḍanti sma / paricālayanti sma / mahatīṃ śrīsaubhāgyatāmanubhavanti sma / jambudvīpe ca rātrīprabhātābhūt //
body.translated_text: Then those ten thousand god-sons departed by the sky-path. And those god-sons, in the domain of King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>, at various places, raining down <s>Māndārava</s> flowers, approached the forest-born lake. There, at that lake, raining down <s>Māndārava</s> flowers, they vanished from that very place and returned again to the celestial abode. There they enjoyed the five sensual pleasures; they played, they engaged in pastimes, and they experienced great glory and good fortune. And in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, night became dawn.

body.text: atha khalu rājā sureśvaraprabho gaṇakamahāmātyānpṛcchati / kimarthamadya rātrāvetāni nimittāni prādurbhūtāni / te 'vocan / yatkhalu devo jānīyāt / jalavāhanasya śreṣṭhidārakasya catvāriṃśanmuktāhārasahasrāṇi pravarṣitāni divyāni ca māndāravapuṣpāṇi nirgacchanti / rājāha / bhavanto jalavāhanaṃ śreṣṭhinaṃ dārakaṃ priyavacanena śabdāpayan //
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s> asked the minister-astrologers: 'For what reason have these omens appeared tonight?' They replied: 'May Your Majesty know: upon <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, forty thousand pearl necklaces have rained down, and divine <s>Māndārava</s> flowers are issuing forth.' The king said: 'Gentlemen, summon the young merchant <s>Jalavāhana</s> with pleasant words.'

body.text: atha te gaṇakamahāmātyā yena jalavāhanasya gṛhaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ / upasaṃkramya jalavāhanasya śreṣṭhina etadavocan / rājā sureśvaraprabhastvāmāmantrayate / atha jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhī mahāmātyaiḥ sārdhaṃ yena rājā sureśvaraprabhastenopajagāma / upasaṃkramyaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ / rājā
body.translated_text: Then the minister-astrologers approached the house of <s>Jalavāhana</s>. Having approached, they said this to <s>Jalavāhana</s> the merchant: 'King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s> summons you.' Then <s>Jalavāhana</s> the merchant, together with the ministers, went to where King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s> was. Having approached, he sat to one side. The king

body.text: pṛcchati / jalavāhana kiṃ nimittaṃ jānīyā yadadya rātrāvīdṛśāni śubhanimittāni prādurbhūtāni / atha jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhī sureśvaraprabhasyaitadavocat / jānābhi deva niyataṃ daśamatsyasahasrāṇi kālagatāni / rājāha / kathaṃ jānāsi / jalavāhana āha / gacchatu deva jalāmbarastāṃ mahāpuṣkariṇīṃ praviśatu / kiṃ tāni daśamtsyasahasrāṇi jīvanti atha kālagatāni / rājāha / evamastu //
body.translated_text: asked: '<s>Jalavāhana</s>, what omen do you know of, that such auspicious signs appeared tonight?' Then <s>Jalavāhana</s> the merchant said this to <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>: 'Know this, Your Majesty: the ten thousand fish have certainly died.' The king said: 'How do you know?' <s>Jalavāhana</s> said: 'Let Your Majesty send <s>Jalāmbara</s> to enter that great lake. [Let us see] whether those ten thousand fish are alive or have died.' The king said: 'So be it!'

body.text: atha jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako jalāmbaraṃ dārakametadavocat / gaccha kulaputrāṭavīsaṃbhavāyāṃ puṣkariṇyāṃ paśya / kiṃ tāni daśamatsyasahasrāṇi jivanti atha kālagatāni / atha jalāmbaro dārakaḥ śīghraṃ śīghraṃ yenāṭavīsaṃbhavā puṣkariṇī tenopajagāma / upasaṃkramya dadarśa / tāni daśamtsyasahasrāṇi kālagatāni mahāntaṃ ca māndāravapuṣpavarṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā punarapi nivṛttaḥ pituretadavocat / kālagatānīti / atha jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhī dārako jalambarasya dārakasyāntikādidaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā yena rājā sureśvaraprabhastenopasaṃkramyaitāṃ prakṛtimārocayati sma / yatkhalu devo jānīyāttāni daśamtsyasahasrāṇi sarvāṇi kālagatāni deveṣu trāyastriṃśatsvupapannāni / teṣāṃ devaputrāṇāmanubhāvenādya rātrāvidṛśāni śubhanimittāni prādurbhūtāni / yadasmākaṃ gṛhe catvāriṃśanmuktāhārasahasrāṇi divyāni ca māndāravapuṣpāṇi pravarṣitāni / atha sa rājā hṛṣṭastuṣṭa udagrāttamanā babhūva //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, said this to the boy <s>Jalāmbara</s>: 'Go, O son of good family, to the forest-born lake and look—are those ten thousand fish alive or have they died?' Then the boy <s>Jalāmbara</s> quickly, quickly went to where the forest-born lake was. Having approached, he saw that those ten thousand fish had died. And seeing the great shower of <s>Māndārava</s> flowers, he returned again and said this to his father: 'They have died.' Then <s>Jalavāhana</s>, the young merchant, having heard these words from the boy <s>Jalāmbara</s>, approached King <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s> and reported this matter: 'May Your Majesty know: those ten thousand fish have all died and been reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. By the power of those god-sons, such auspicious omens appeared tonight—that in our house, forty thousand pearl necklaces and divine <s>Māndārava</s> flowers rained down.' Then that king was delighted, pleased, overjoyed, and glad in mind.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānpunastāṃ bodhisattvasamuccayāṃ kuladevatāmetadavocat // syātkhalu punaryuṣmākaṃ kuladevate 'nyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena sureśvaraprabho nāma rājā babhūva / na khalu punarevaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / daṇḍapāṇiḥ śākyastena kālena tena samayena sureśvaraprabho nāma rājā babhūva / syātkhalu punaḥ kuladevate 'nyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena jaṭiṃdharo nāma śreṣṭhī babhūva / na khalu punarevaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / rājā śuddhodanaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena jaṭiṃdharo nāma śreṣṭhyabhūt //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-assembly family deity: 'It may be, O family deity, that you think someone else was at that time the king named <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>. But it should not be seen thus. For what reason? <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> the <s>Śākya</s> was at that time the king named <s>Sureśvaraprabha</s>. It may be, O family deity, that you think someone else was at that time the merchant named <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>. But it should not be seen thus. For what reason? King <s>Śuddhodana</s> was at that time the merchant named <s>Jaṭiṃdhara</s>.'

body.text: syātkhalu punaste kuladevate 'nyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'bhūt / na khalu punarevaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena jalavāhanaḥ śreṣṭhidārako 'bhūt // syātkhalu punaste kuladevate 'nyā sā tena kālena tena samayena jalavāhanasya jalāmbujagarbhā nāma bhāryābhūt / na khalu punarevaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / gopā nāma śākyakanyā tena kālena samayena jalavāhanasya jalāmbujagarbhā nāma bhāryābhūt / rāhulabhadrastena kalena tena samayena jalāmbaro nāma dārako 'bhūt / ānandaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena jalagarbho nāma dārako 'bhūt / syātkhalu punaste kuladevate 'nyāni tāni tena kālena tena samayena daśamatsyasahasrāṇi babhūvaḥ / na punarevaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / amūni tāni jvalanāntaratejorājapramukhāni daśadevaputrasahasrāṇi tena kālena tena samayena daśamatsyasahasrāṇi babhūvuḥ / yāni mayodakena saṃtarpitāni / bhojanavareṇa ca gambhīraśca pratītyasamutpādo dharmo deśitaḥ / ratnaśikhinastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya nāmadheyaṃ śrāvitaḥ / tena kuśaladharmahetunā mamāntika ihāgatāni yenaitarhyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtāni / atīva prītiprāsādaprāmodyena dharmaśrutigauraveṇa sarvavyākaraṇanāmadheyāni pratilabdhānīti //
body.translated_text: 'It may be, O family deity, that you think someone else was at that time the young merchant <s>Jalavāhana</s>. But it should not be seen thus. For what reason? I myself was at that time the young merchant <s>Jalavāhana</s>. It may be, O family deity, that you think someone else was at that time the wife of <s>Jalavāhana</s> named <s>Jalāmbujagarbhā</s>. But it should not be seen thus. For what reason? The <s>Śākya</s> maiden named <s>Gopā</s> was at that time the wife of <s>Jalavāhana</s> named <s>Jalāmbujagarbhā</s>. <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> was at that time the boy named <s>Jalāmbara</s>. <s>Ānanda</s> was at that time the boy named <s>Jalagarbha</s>. It may be, O family deity, that you think others were at that time the ten thousand fish. But it should not be seen thus. For what reason? Those were these ten thousand god-sons headed by <s>Jvalanāntaratejorāja</s> who at that time were the ten thousand fish, whom I nourished with water and with excellent food, and to whom the profound <s>dharma</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) was taught, and [whom I] caused to hear the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. By that wholesome <s>dharma</s> as cause, they have come here to my presence, where they have now received prophecy of supreme perfect <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment). With extreme joy, faith, delight, and gladness, and with reverence for hearing the <s>dharma</s>, all the names of the prophecies have been received.'

body.text: syātkhalu punaste kuladevate 'nyā sā tena kālena tena samayena vṛkṣadevatābhūt / naivaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / tvamabhūḥ kuladevate tena kālena tena samayena vṛkṣadevatā / anena kuladevate paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam / yathā mayā saṃsāre saṃsaratā bahavaḥ sattvāḥ paripācitā bodhau / ye te sarve vyākaraṇabhūmiṃ pratilapsyante 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāviti //
body.translated_text: Perhaps, O family deity, you may think that the tree-deity at that time and on that occasion was someone else. It should not be viewed thus. For what reason? You yourself, O family deity, were the tree-deity at that time and on that occasion. By this method, O family deity, it should be understood thus: that by me, while wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, many beings have been brought to maturity in awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). All of them shall attain the stage of prediction (<s>vyākaraṇabhūmi</s>) in supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje jalavāhanasya matsyavaineyaparivarto 'ṣṭādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, the <s>Matsyavaineya</s> (Conversion of the Fish) chapter of <s>Jalavāhana</s>, in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // vyāghrīparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Vyāghrī</s> (Tigress) Chapter //

body.text: punaraparaṃ kuladevate parahitārthāyātmaparityāgamapi bodhisattvabhūtena bhavitavyam / tatkathamidam / divi bhuvi ca visṛtavipulavimalavividhaguṇaśatakiraṇo 'pratihatajñānadarśanabalaparākramo bhagavānbhikṣuśatasahasraparivṛtaḥ pañcavidhacakṣuprāptaḥ prañcāleṣu janapadeṣu janapadacārikāṃ caramāṇo 'nyatameva vanakhaṇḍamanuprāpto babhūva / sa tatra dadarśa haritamṛdunīlaśādvalatalavividhakusumapratimaṇḍitaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayati sma / ruciro 'yamānanda ! pṛthivīpradeśaḥ / asmiṃścāsmikasthānaniṣṭhā saṃjñāyate / etarhi tathāgatasyāsanaṃ prajñāpaya / tatasyena bhagavata ājñayāsanaṃ prajñaptam / prajñapya ca bhagavantametadavocat / prajñaptamāsanaṃ bhagavanniṣīda jṣṭheṣṭha śreṣṭha nṛṇāṃ varada variṣṭha mokṣavaha paramāmṛtakathāṃ visṛja nṛṇāṃ hitāya bhagavannidhanaviprayuktaṃ / atha bhagavāṃstasminnāsane niṣadya bhikṣūnāmantrayate sma / icchatha yūyaṃ bhikṣavo duṣkarakārikāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ śarīrāṇi draṣṭum //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O family deity, one who is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be willing to give up even one's own body for the benefit of others. How is this so? The Blessed One, whose rays of hundreds of vast, pure, and diverse qualities spread across heaven and earth, whose power and valor of knowledge and insight are unobstructed, surrounded by a hundred thousand monks, having attained the five kinds of vision, while wandering on a tour of the countryside in the <s>Pañcāla</s> regions, arrived at a certain forest grove. There he saw a stretch of land adorned with green, soft, blue-green grass and various flowers, and having seen it, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'This is a delightful spot, <s>Ānanda</s>! And in this place a certain feeling of our resting-place arises. Now prepare a seat for the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then by that command of the Blessed One, a seat was prepared. And having prepared it, he said this to the Blessed One: 'The seat is prepared, O Blessed One—be seated! O eldest, O best among men, O boon-granter, O most excellent, O bearer of liberation, release the supreme immortal discourse for the benefit of beings, O Blessed One, free from death.' Then the Blessed One, having sat upon that seat, addressed the monks: 'Do you wish, O monks, to see the bodily relics of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who performed difficult deeds?'

body.text: evamukte bhikṣavo bhagavantametadavocan /
body.translated_text: When this was said, the monks said this to the Blessed One:

children.translated_text: 'This is the right time, O best of sages—to see [the relics] of one devoted to the essence of beings' welfare, delighting in non-duality.'
'Let us see the bones of one endowed with immeasurable qualities—please reveal them!' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.1 //

body.text: atha bhagavānsahasrāracakracaraṇavilikhitatalena sthūlitanavakamalakomalena pāṇinā dharaṇītalaṃ jaghāna vyāhatamātreṇa ṣaḍvikāraṃ pṛthivī cacāla / maṇikena karajātavikṛtaṃ ca stūpaṃ tato 'bhyujjagāma / atha bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma / vighāṭayānandemaṃ stūpam / athāyuṣmānānando bhagavate pratikṣutya stūpaṃ vighaṭayāmāsa / sa tatra dadarśa kanakavisṛtamuktāsaṃchāditaṃ hiraṇyamayaṃ samudrakam / dṛṣṭvā ca bhagavantametadavocat / hiraṇyamayaṃ bhagavansamudrakaḥ samuddhṛtaḥ / bhagavānuvāca / saptaite samudrakānsarva uddhāṭanīyāḥ / tadoddhāṭayāmāsa / sa tatra dadarśa himakumudasadṛśānyasthīni / dṛṣṭvā ca bhagavantametadavocat / bhagavannasthīnyupalakṣyante / bhagavānāha / ānīyatāmānanda mahāpuruṣasyāsthīni //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One struck the surface of the earth with his hand, whose palm was inscribed with thousand-spoked wheel marks and was as tender as a fresh, plump lotus. At the mere striking, the earth quaked with a sixfold tremor. And a <s>stūpa</s>, adorned with jewels and of wondrous appearance, arose therefrom. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Open this <s>stūpa</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>!' Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One, opened the <s>stūpa</s>. There he saw a golden casket covered with gold-strewn pearls. Having seen it, he said this to the Blessed One: 'A golden casket has been retrieved, O Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'All seven of these caskets must be opened.' Then he opened them. There he saw bones resembling snow-white lilies. Having seen them, he said this to the Blessed One: 'Bones are observed, O Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'Bring forth the bones of the great being, <s>Ānanda</s>!'

body.text: athāyuṣmānānandastānyasthīnyādāya bhagavate buddhāyopanāmayāmāsa / bhagavāṃścāsthīni gṛhītvā saṃghasya purataḥ saṃsthāpyovāca / imānyasthīni mahāpravaraguṇāmuktasya samantadamadhyānakṣāntipravaradṛḍhotsāhayaśaḥsaṃskṛto bhūyaḥ satatasamitaṃ bodhau matimato dṛḍhotsāhino dhṛtimataḥ sadādānaniratasya / tato bhagavānbhikṣūnāmantrayāmāsa / vadanta bhikṣavo bodhisattvaśarīrāṇi śīlaguṇavāsitāni paramadurlabhadarśanāni puṇyakṣetrabhūtāni / tataste bhikṣavaḥ kṛtakarapuṭā āvarjitamanasastāni śarīrāṇi mūrdhnā vandante sma //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having taken those bones, presented them to the Blessed One, the <s>Buddha</s>. And the Blessed One, having received the bones and placed them before the <s>Saṃgha</s>, said: 'These are the bones of one who was endowed with the most excellent qualities, whose glory was fashioned by complete self-restraint, meditation, forbearance, supreme steadfastness, and zeal; of one who was always and continuously wise in the pursuit of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), of firm resolve, of steady mind, and always devoted to giving.' Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Speak, O monks! The bodily relics of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, perfumed with the virtues of moral discipline, extremely rare to behold, have become fields of merit.' Then those monks, with palms joined and minds devoted, paid reverence to those relics with their heads.

body.text: athāyuṣmānānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantametadavocat / bhagavānatītānāgatapratyutpannasarvalokābhyudbhataḥ sarvasattvairnamaskṛtaḥ tatkathaṃ tathāgata evaitānyasthīni namasyate / atha bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandametadavocat / vandanīyānīmānyasthīnyānanda / tatkasya hetoḥ / ebhirānandāsthibhirmayaivaṃ kṣipramanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddheti / bhūtapūrvamānandātīte 'dhvanyanekadhanadhānyavāhanabalopapanno 'pratihatabalaparākramo mahāratho nāma rājābhūt / tasya devakumārasadṛśāstrayaḥ putrā babhūvaḥ / mahāpraṇādo mahādevo mahāsattvāśceti / atha rājā krīḍanārthamudyānamabhiniṣkramate sma / te ca kumārāstasyodyānasya guṇānurādhitayā kusumalolayā cetastato 'nuvicaramānā mahādvādaśavanagulmaṃ praviviśuḥ / teṣu prasṛteṣu kumāropasthāyakā anyonyaprasṛtā babhūvuḥ / rājakumārotsṛṣṭā udyānamahatyāmalakṣitāyāṃ taṃ dvādaśavanagulmaṃ praviviśuḥ / atha mahāpraṇādo bhrātṛdvayamuvāca / bhīrme hṛdayamāviśate / āgacchata mā vayaṃ śvāpade vināśamāpadyema / mahādeva uvāca / na me bhayamastyapi tviṣṭajanaviyogāddhi me hṛdaye pravartate / mahāsattva uvāca //
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, said this to the Blessed One: 'The Blessed One is exalted above all worlds—past, future, and present—and is venerated by all beings. Why then does the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself bow to these bones?' Then the Blessed One said this to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'These bones are to be venerated, <s>Ānanda</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Ānanda</s>, it was through these very bones—through this body—that I swiftly attained supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' 'Formerly, <s>Ānanda</s>, in the past, there was a king named <s>Mahāratha</s> (Great Chariot), endowed with abundant wealth, grain, vehicles, and strength, whose power and valor were unobstructed. He had three sons, resembling divine princes: <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, and <s>Mahāsattva</s>. Then the king went out to the park for recreation. And those princes, their minds drawn by the qualities of that garden, their hearts captivated by the flowers, wandered about and entered a great thicket of twelve groves. As they went forth, the princes' attendants became scattered in various directions. The royal princes, unguarded, entered that thicket of twelve groves through a vast, uncharted expanse of the garden. Then <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> said to his two brothers: "Fear enters my heart. Come, let us not perish at the hands of wild beasts." <s>Mahādeva</s> said: "I have no fear, but sorrow from separation from loved ones arises in my heart." <s>Mahāsattva</s> said:'

children.text: na ca mama bhayamihāsti nāpi śoko vanavare munijanasaṃstute vivikte /
children.translated_text: 'Neither fear nor sorrow is in me here, in this excellent, secluded forest praised by sages.

children.text: paramasuvipulamahārthatā lābhā hṛdayamidaṃ mama saṃprapuṣpati ca // Suv_19.2 //
children.translated_text: The gain is of supremely vast and great purpose; this heart of mine blossoms forth.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.2 //

body.text: atha te rājakumārāstad dvādaśavanagulmavivaraṃ cañcūryamāṇā ekāṃ vyāghrīṃ dadṛśuḥ saptāhaprasutāṃ pañcasutaparivṛtāṃ kṣuttṛṣaparikarṣitāṃ paramadurbalaśarīrāṃ dṛṣṭā mahāpraṇādo 'bravīt / bho kaṣṭamiyaṃ tapasvinī ṣaḍahaprasutā vā saptāhaprasutā vā bhaviṣyati / idānīṃ bhojanamalabhamānā svasutāni bhakṣayiṣyati jighatsayā vā kālaṃ kariṣyati / mahāsattva uvāca / kimasyāstapasvinyā bhojanam / mahāpraṇāda uvāca /
body.translated_text: Then those royal princes, wandering about through the openings of that thicket of twelve groves, saw a tigress who had given birth seven days ago, surrounded by five cubs, emaciated by hunger and thirst, her body extremely weak. Having seen her, <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> said: 'Alas, how pitiful! This wretched one must have given birth six or seven days ago. Now, unable to find food, she will devour her own cubs or die of starvation.' <s>Mahāsattva</s> said: 'What is the food of this wretched creature?' <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> said:

children.translated_text: 'Fresh warm flesh and blood, if such resembling vital essence could be found here—
this is said to be the food of tigers, leopards, bears, and lions.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.3 //

body.text: mahādeva uvāca / ihaiṣā tapasvīnī kṣuttuṣaparītaśarīrā alaṃ prāṇāvaśeṣā paramadurbalā na śakyamanyasthāne bhojanamanveṣṭum / ko 'syāḥ prāṇaparirakṣaṇārthamātmaparityāgaṃ kuryāditi / mahāpraṇāda uvāca / bho duṣkara ātmaparityāgaḥ / mahāsattva uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s> said: 'This wretched one, her body consumed by hunger and thirst, barely clinging to life, extremely weak—it is impossible to search for food elsewhere. Who would sacrifice their own body to protect her life?' <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> said: 'Alas, the sacrifice of one's own body is a difficult thing!' <s>Mahāsattva</s> said:

children.text: asmadvidhān duṣkara śarīra abhiyuktānāṃ eṣa nayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For those like us, attached to the body, this is indeed difficult.

children.text: anyeṣāṃ parahitābhiyuktānāṃ satpuruṣāṇa na duṣkaraḥ // Suv_19.4 //
children.translated_text: But for others—noble beings devoted to the welfare of others—it is not difficult.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.4 //

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: kṛpākaruṇamamavatāriya sattvo divi ceha labhyate saḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A being who has descended into this world with compassion and mercy is found both in heaven and here.

children.text: svadeha śataśa iha kṛtva muditamanāḥ parajīvaśarīre // Suv_19.5 //
children.translated_text: Having given up his own body hundreds of times here, he rejoices in mind at preserving the lives and bodies of others.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.5 //

body.text: atha te rājakumārāḥ paramasaṃdīptā eṣā vyāghrīti drutamanimiṣimanunirīkṣantaḥ pracaṅkramustato mahāsattvasyaitadabhūt / ayamidānīmātmaparityāgasya kālaḥ / kutaḥ -
body.translated_text: Then those royal princes, thinking 'this tigress is extremely fierce,' departed quickly, gazing back without blinking. Then this thought arose in <s>Mahāsattva</s>: 'Now is the time for the sacrifice of my body. Why?'

body.text: suciramapi ṛto 'yaṃ pūtikāyo mahāhaiḥ śayanavasanānnairbhojanairvāhanaiśca /
body.translated_text: 'This foul body has been nourished for a long time with great expenditure of bedding, clothing, food, meals, and conveyances,

body.text: śtanayakṛtadharmābhaidanāntairanantaṃ na vijahati anupūrvaṃ svasvabhāvaṃ kṛtaghnuḥ // Suv_19.6 //
body.translated_text: yet, ending in destruction through the workings of nature, it never gradually abandons its own nature—ungrateful that it is!' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.6 //

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: nāstī tasyopajīvyaṃ sarvatu madhye bhutatvāttaṃ niyojya /
children.translated_text: 'There is no sustenance for it among all things, since it consists of the elements. Having devoted it to this purpose,
I shall become for it a vessel for crossing the ocean of old age and death.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.7 //

body.text: api ca /
body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned this body which is like a pustule, filled with hundreds of existences, full of filth within,

children.text: niḥsāraphenakalpaṃ kṛmiśatabharitaṃ kāryakṛtyaṃ tanu hi // Suv_19.8 //
children.translated_text: essenceless, like foam, filled with hundreds of worms—for indeed the body has a task to fulfill.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.8 //
'Free from sorrow, unchanging, without material substrate, immaculate, endowed with qualities such as meditation and wisdom,

children.text: saṃpūrṇaṃ dharmakāya guṇaśatabharitaṃ prāpsyeva suśuddham // Suv_19.9 //
children.translated_text: I shall attain the complete <s>Dharmakāya</s> (body of truth), filled with hundreds of qualities, supremely pure.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.9 //

body.text: sa khalvevaṃ kṛtavyavasāyaḥ paramakaruṇoparigatahṛdayaḥ tayorvikṣepaṃ cakāra / gacchetāṃ tāvadbhavantau svakāryeṇāhaṃ dvādaśavanagulmaṃ pravekṣyāmīti //
body.translated_text: He, having thus made his resolution, his heart overcome with supreme compassion, created a diversion for the two brothers: 'Let you two go ahead on your own business; I shall enter the thicket of twelve groves.'

body.text: atha sa mahāsattvo rājakumāraḥ tasmādupavanātpratinivṛtya vyāghryā ālayamupagamya vanalatāyāṃ prāvaraṇamṛtsṛjya praṇidhānaṃ cakāra / eṣo 'haṃ jagato hitārthamanuttarāṃ bodhiṃ vibudhya śivāṃ kāruṇyātpradadāmi niścalamatirdehaṃ parairdustyajam / tanme bodhiranāmayā yā jinasutairabhyarcitā nirjvalā trailikyaṃ bhavasāgarātpratibhayāduttārayeyānmām / ityatha vyāghryā abhimukhaṃ mahāsattvaḥ prapatitaḥ / tato vyāghrī maitrīvato bodhisattvasya na kiñciccakre / tato bodhisattvo durbalāvarto 'yamathetyutthāya śastraṃ paryeṣate sma / kṛpāmatirna kvacicchastramalabhat / so 'tibalāṃ varṣaśatikāṃ vaṃśalatāṃ
body.translated_text: Then that prince <s>Mahāsattva</s>, turning back from that grove, approached the tigress's lair, cast aside his upper garment upon a forest creeper, and made a vow: 'I, having realized supreme, blissful awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) for the welfare of the world, out of compassion, with unwavering mind, give up this body that is hard for others to relinquish. May that awakening of mine be without affliction, worshipped by the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>, blazing forth—and may it carry the triple world across the fearsome ocean of existence!' Having said this, <s>Mahāsattva</s> threw himself down before the tigress. But the tigress, sensing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s loving-kindness, did nothing to him. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought, 'This one is too weak,' and rising up, he searched for a sharp instrument. But the compassionate one could not find any weapon anywhere. He found a very sturdy, hundred-year-old bamboo shoot

body.text: gṛhītvā tayā svabālamutkṣepya vyāghrīsamīpe papāta / prapatitamātre ca bodhisattve bhūmiriyaṃ pracaravihīneva nauḥ salilamadhye gatā ṣaḍvikāraṃ pracacāla / rāhugrasta iva dinakarakiraṇo na babhrāje / divyagandhacūrṇasaṃniśritaṃ ca kusumavarṣaṃ papāta / athānyatarā vismayā varjitamanasā devatā bodhisattvaṃ tuṣṭāva //
body.translated_text: and having taken it, he cut his own throat with it and fell near the tigress. The moment the <s>Bodhisattva</s> fell, this earth trembled with a sixfold quaking, like a ship in the midst of water bereft of its course. The rays of the sun did not shine, as if seized by <s>Rāhu</s>. And a shower of flowers mixed with divine fragrant powders fell. Then a certain deity, her mind captivated by wonder, praised the <s>Bodhisattva</s>:

children.text: yathā kāruṇyaṃ te visṛtamiha sattveṣu sumate
children.translated_text: 'Just as your compassion, O wise one, has been spread among beings here,

children.text: yathā vai taddehaṃ tyajasi naravīra pramuditaḥ /
children.translated_text: just as you, O hero among men, joyfully abandon that body—
the blissful, supreme state, free from the affliction of birth and death,

children.text: nirāyāsaṃ śāntaṃ tvamiha na cirātprāpsyasi śubham // Suv_19.10 //
children.translated_text: painless and peaceful—you shall attain that auspicious state here before long.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.10 //

body.text: atha khalu sā vyāghrī rudhiramrakṣitaśarīraṃ bodhisattvamavekṣya muhūrtamātreṇa nirmāṃsarudhiramasthyavaśeṣaṃ cakāra //
body.translated_text: Then that tigress, seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body smeared with blood, in but a moment consumed him, leaving only bones devoid of flesh and blood.

body.text: atha mahāpraṇādastaṃ bhūmikampamanuniśamya mahādevametadavocat //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>, perceiving that earthquake, said this to <s>Mahādeva</s>:

children.text: pracalita sasamudrā sāgarā vasumatidaśadikṣū suptaraśmiśca sūryaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The earth with its oceans and seas has trembled in the ten directions, and the sun's rays have fallen asleep.

children.text: patati kusumavarṣaṃ vyākulaṃ vā mano me svatanuriha visṛṣṭaḥ sāṃprataṃ bhrātṛṇā me // Suv_19.11//
children.translated_text: A shower of flowers falls—and my mind is agitated! Surely my brother has now given up his own body here!' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.11 //

body.text: mahādeva uvāca /
body.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s> said:

children.text: yathā ca so karuṇavaco hyavocata samīkṣya tāṃ svatanāyabhakṣaṇodyatāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Considering how he spoke those compassionate words, looking upon her who was about to devour her own offspring,

children.text: kṣudhānvitāṃ vyaśanaśataiḥ samanvitāṃ sudurbalā matiriha saṃśayā tu me // Suv_19.12 //
children.translated_text: consumed by hunger, beset by hundreds of calamities, extremely weak—indeed, my mind here is filled with doubt about his fate.' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.12 //

body.text: atha tau rājakumārau paramaśokābhibhūtau vāṣpapariplutākṣau tamenaṃ panthānaṃ pratinivṛtya gacchantau vyāghrīsamīpamevābhijagmatuḥ / taṃ dadṛśtuḥ śataṃ vaṃśalatāsamāyuktaṃ prāvaraṇaṃ kṛṣṇavikṛṣṇāni
body.translated_text: Then those two royal princes, overcome with utmost grief, their eyes flooded with tears, turning back along that very path, came to the very place near the tigress. They saw the bamboo shoot joined with the garment, and the blackened and discolored

body.text: cāsthīni rudhirakardamāni / nānādigvidikṣu keśānvistīrṇāndṛṣṭvā ca samūrcchannau bhūmau nipetatuḥ / sacirātsaṃjñāmupalabhyotthāyocceyabāhū ārtasvaraṃ mumucatuḥ /
body.translated_text: bones smeared with blood-mud. Seeing the hair scattered in various directions and quarters, the two fainted and fell to the ground. After a long time, regaining consciousness and rising with arms raised aloft, they let out cries of anguish.

body.text: aho priyabhrātṛka pārthivāyaṃ tathā jananī sutavatsalā yā

children.text: pṛcchiṣyate sā jananī tṛtīyaḥ kva vā yuvābhyāṃ kamalāyatekṣṇaḥ // Suv_19.13 //
children.translated_text: that mother will ask: 'Where is the third one, the lotus-eyed one, who was with you two?' // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.13 //

body.translated_text: Alas, dear brother! This king our father, and our mother who is so devoted to her sons—

children.text: aho hi asmākamihaiva śobhitaṃ nanū pradeśe maraṇaṃ na jīvitam /
children.translated_text: Alas, for us in this very place, death would be more fitting than life,

children.text: kathaṃ mahāsattvavivarjitā vayaṃ dāsyāmahe darśanamambatātayoḥ // Suv_19.14 //
children.translated_text: how, bereft of <s>Mahāsattva</s>, shall we show our faces to our mother and father? // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.14 //

body.text: atha tau rājakumārau bahuvividhakaruṇaṃ vilāpya pracakramatuḥ / tatra kumārasyopasthāyakā diśi vidiśi pradhāvantaḥ kumārānveṣaṇāḥ parasparaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca papracchuḥ kva kumāraḥ kva kumāra iti / tasmiṃśca samaye devī śayanatalagatā priyaviprayogasūcakaṃ svapnaṃ dadarśa / tadyathā stanau chidyamānau dantotpātanaṃ ca kriyamāṇaṃ trayaḥ kapotaśāvakāḥ pratilambhamānāste bhītā eva śyenenācchidyamānāḥ / atha devī bhūmikāmpādutrastahṛdayā sahasā prativibudhya cintāparā babhūva // kimeṣā bhūtadhātrī jalanidhivasanā kampati bhṛśaṃ sūryaḥ śūlī na raśmirmama ca kica bhūbhajaṃ vayati vā /
body.translated_text: Then the two princes, having lamented in many varied pitiful ways, set out. There, the prince's attendants, running in every direction searching for the princes, upon seeing each other asked: 'Where is the prince? Where is the prince?' At that time, the queen, lying upon her bed, had a dream foreboding separation from her beloved—namely: her two breasts being cut, her teeth being extracted, and three young pigeons being seized and, terrified, snatched away by a hawk. Then the queen, her heart alarmed by the trembling of the earth, suddenly awoke and became absorbed in anxiety: // 'Why does this earth, girt by the ocean, tremble so violently? The sun's rays are like tridents, and something seems to afflict my body—'

children.text: duḥkhaṃ kurvati me gātraṃ calati ca nayanaṃ svastanaṃ chidyatī ca /
children.translated_text: Pain afflicts my limbs, my eye twitches, and my own breast feels as if being cut,

children.text: svasti me syātsutānāṃ vanavivaramidaṃ krīḍanārthaṃ gatānām // Suv_19.15 //
children.translated_text: may all be well with my sons who have gone to this forest grove for the sake of play! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.15 //

body.text: athaivaṃ cintayantyāśceṭī ca saṃtrastahṛdayā praviśya devyā nivedayāmāsa / devi kumāraparicārakāḥ kumāramanveṣante naṣṭaḥ śrūyate / tatra putrahataśravaṇācca devī saṃkampitāhṛdayā vāṣpākulanayanavadanā
body.translated_text: Then, while she was thus reflecting, a maidservant with a terrified heart entered and informed the queen: 'Your Majesty, the prince's attendants are searching for the prince—he is reported lost!' Thereupon, the queen, her heart shaken upon hearing this news about her son, her face and eyes overflowing with tears,

body.text: rājānamabhigamyovāca / deva naṣṭo me priyasutaḥ śrūyate / rājāpi saṃkampitahṛdayaḥ paramasaṃtrāsamāpede / hā kaṣṭaṃ viyukto 'smi priyasutena / atha rājā devīmāśvāsayāmāsa / mā bhīrdevi putrārthaṃ vayaṃ kumārānveṣaṇopalabhantaḥ / tatra pravṛtte kumārānveṣaṇābhidrute janakāya athācirādeva rājā dadarśa dūrata evāgacchantau rājakumārau / dṛṣṭvā rājābravīt / etāvālabhantau kumārau na tu sarve / hā kaṣṭaṃ sutaviyogo nāma /
body.translated_text: approached the king and said: 'Your Majesty, my beloved son is reported lost!' The king too, his heart shaken, was overcome with the utmost terror: 'Alas, how terrible—I am separated from my dear son!' Then the king consoled the queen: 'Do not fear, O queen! We shall find the princes through a search for them.' When the search for the princes was set in motion and rushed forward, then before long the king saw the two princes coming from afar. Having seen them, the king said: 'Here two princes are found, but not all of them. Alas, how terrible is this thing called separation from a son!'

children.text: na bhavati nirupalambhe na prītirevaṃ narāṇāṃ bhavati sutaviyogādyādṛśaṃ daurmanasyam /
children.translated_text: When there is nothing to be grasped, there is neither attachment nor such joy for people; such is the grief that arises from separation from a son—

children.text: nanu varasukhinaste yena puṃsābhiyogā maraṇamupagatā vā ye na jīvanti putrāḥ // Suv_19.16 //
children.translated_text: indeed, supremely happy are those men who have no involvement with sons, or whose sons have gone to death and no longer live! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.16 //

body.text: atha devī paramaśokābhibhūtā marmahanteva kalabhī ārtasvaramuvāca //
body.translated_text: Then the queen, overwhelmed by the utmost grief, like a young elephant cow struck in a vital spot, spoke in a voice of anguish:

children.text: yadi tanayāstrayasya bhṛtyavargā vanavare kusumākule praviṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: If the three sons with their retinue of attendants entered this flower-filled forest grove,

children.text: kva sa hṛdayasamo samastṛtīyaḥ sutamanayāpadavaiti kanīyasametat // Suv_19.17 //
children.translated_text: where is he who is dear as my heart, the third among them? Bring the youngest son—understand this calamity! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.17 //

body.text: tayorāgatayo rājā putrāvetatparyapṛcchatotsukaḥ kumārau paripṛcchati sma / kva dārakaḥ kanīyasa iti / tataḥ śokārtāvaśrudrutanayanau pariśuṣkatālvoṣṭhadaśanavadanau na kiñcidūcatuḥ // devyuvāca //
body.translated_text: Upon the arrival of those two, the king eagerly questioned the two princes about this matter. He asked the princes: 'Where is the youngest child?' Then the two, grief-stricken, with eyes streaming tears, with parched palates, lips, teeth, and faces, said nothing. // The queen spoke: //

children.text: kathayatāṃ laghu vimuhyati smṛtiśca paramabhṛśaṃ paripīḍyate ca dehaḥ /
children.translated_text: Speak quickly! My memory fades and my body is tormented beyond measure,

children.text: kva sa mama putrastṛtīya hṛdayaṃ idaṃ sphuṭitaṃ tu saṃmūrcchati vā // Suv_19.18 //
children.translated_text: where is my third son? This heart of mine is bursting—or am I about to faint? // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.18 //

body.text: atha tau kumārau vistareṇa taṃ vṛttāntaṃ nivedayāmāsa / sahaśravaṇena rājā devī parijanāśca mohamupagatāḥ / mohapratyāgatāśca karuṇārtasvaraṃ rodamānāstaṃ deśamabhijagmuḥ / atha rājā devī ca taṇyasthīnyapagatarudhiramāṃsāni vāyunā diśo vidiśaśca keśavikīrṇā dṛṣṭvā
body.translated_text: Then the two princes reported that entire account in detail. Upon hearing it, the king, the queen, and the retinue fell into a swoon. When they recovered from the swoon, weeping with piteous, anguished cries, they went to that place. Then the king and queen, seeing his bones drained of blood and flesh, with hair scattered by the wind in all directions,

body.text: cāhata iva drumo bhūmau nipatitau / tataḥ purohitaḥ suciraṃ tāmavasthāṃ dṛṣṭvā salilamalayacandanapaṅkai rājño devyāśca śarīraṃ prahlādayāmāsa / atha sucirātsaṃjñāmupalabhya rājotthāya karuṇakaruṇaṃ vilalāpa //
body.translated_text: fell to the ground like trees struck by lightning. Then the royal priest, seeing that condition for a long while, revived the bodies of the king and queen with water and Malaya sandalwood paste. After a long time, having regained consciousness, the king rose and lamented most piteously:

children.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ putra kva manorasa darśanīya mṛtyorvaśaṃ śīghramupagatāsi /
children.translated_text: Alas, how terrible! O son, where are you, O delightful one, beautiful to behold? You have so quickly come under the power of death!

children.text: mṛtyoḥ praśmameva hi cāgato vinā te paraṃ mama bhaviṣyati duḥkhamanyat // Suv_19.19 //
children.translated_text: Indeed you have entered the tranquility of death; without you, there shall be another, even greater suffering for me. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.19 //

body.text: devī ca mohātyāgatā prakīrṇakeśī bāhubhyāmurastāḍayantī sthānyāṃ pluta iva matsyā dharaṇyāstale parivartamānā mahiṣīva naṣṭavatsā kalabhīva naṣṭaśāvakā karuṇakaruṇaṃ roditi //
body.translated_text: And the queen, having recovered from her swoon, with disheveled hair, beating her chest with her arms, like a fish cast upon dry land rolling on the surface of the earth, like a buffalo cow that has lost her calf, like a young elephant cow that has lost her young, wept most piteously:

children.text: hā kānta priyasuta kena vrajase bhagno 'yaṃ padmo dharaṇītale hi vikīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alas, O beloved, dear son! By whom have you been taken? This lotus has been broken and scattered upon the ground!

children.text: śatruṇā mama bhuvi kena nāśaṃ gato 'dya putro me nayanamanoharacandraḥ
children.translated_text: By what enemy on earth has my son, the moon that delights my eyes and heart, been destroyed today?

children.text: hā kiṃ śarīramiha adya na yāti bhagnaṃ paśyāmi haṃ sutavaraṃ nihataṃ pṛthivyām // Suv_19.20 //
children.translated_text: Alas, why does my body not break apart now? I behold my excellent son slain upon the earth! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.20 //

children.text: saṃvyaktaṃ hṛdayamayo mamaitaṃ dhigvyasanaṃ avekṣya no cedbhedayate /
children.translated_text: Clearly this heart of mine is made of iron—curse this calamity!—since upon seeing it, it does not shatter!
Alas, this is indeed the fruit of that evil dream—that these two breasts have been cut today as if by some sword,

children.text: svapnāntare dvau stanau daṃṣṭrotpāṭya me priyasuto nāśaṃ gataḥ śīghramataḥ // Suv_19.21 //
children.translated_text: In the dream my two breasts were torn by fangs—and so my beloved son has swiftly gone to destruction! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.21 //

children.text: sa śyenenāpahṛto yathaiva iha me labdhaiḥ kapotaistribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in my dream, one of the three pigeons I had obtained was carried off by a hawk,

children.text: so me 'dya tribhirātmajaiḥ parivṛta eko hato mṛtyunā // Suv_19.22 //
children.translated_text: so today, among my three sons, one has been slain by death. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.22 //

body.text: atha rājā devī ca bahuvidhaṃ karuṇakaruṇaṃ paridevatastayoḥ sarvabharaṇānyavamucya mahatā janakāyena sārdhaṃ putrasya śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā tasminpṛthivīpradeśe suvarṇamayacaityeṣu nyastāni tāni śarīrāṇi //
body.translated_text: Then the king and queen, having lamented in many pitifully sorrowful ways, removed all their ornaments, and together with a great assembly of people, performed the worship of their son's remains. In that place upon the earth, those bodily relics were enshrined in golden <s>caityas</s> (memorial shrines).

body.text: syātte khalu punarānandānyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena mahāsattvo nāma rājakumāro 'bhūt / naivaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ / ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena mahāsattvo nāma rājakumāro 'bhūt / tadāpi mayānanda rājadveṣamohāparimuktena narakādibhyaśca duḥkhebhyaḥ kṛpayā jagadanugṛhītam / kiṃ khalu punaridānīṃ sarvadoṣāpagatena samyaksaṃbuddheneti / evaṃ hyekaikasya sattvasyārthe kalpaṃ samudeyaṃ narakeṣu jātiṃ saṃsārādvimocayeyam / khalu sattvasāraiśca jagatparigṛhītaṃ duṣkaramanekavidhavicitramiti //
body.translated_text: Perhaps, O <s>Ānanda</s>, you might think: 'Someone else was the prince named <s>Mahāsattva</s> at that time and on that occasion.' It should not be regarded thus. For what reason? I myself was the prince named <s>Mahāsattva</s> at that time and on that occasion. Even then, O <s>Ānanda</s>, though not freed from attachment, aversion, and delusion, I benefited the world through compassion, saving beings from the sufferings of the hells and other realms. How much more so now, as a perfectly awakened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Fully Enlightened One) free from all faults! Thus, for the sake of each and every being, I would take birth in the hells for an entire <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) to liberate them from <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence). Indeed, through the essence of compassion for beings, the world has been embraced—such are the difficult, manifold, and wondrous deeds.

body.text: atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: bahūni kalpāni mayātmā tyaktaḥ paryeṣayetā imamagrabodhim /
children.translated_text: For many <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) I have given up my own self, seeking this supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),

children.text: yathāsi rājā yatha rājaputram tathaiva tyaktā maya ātmabhāvāḥ // Suv_19.23 //
children.translated_text: whether as a king or as a prince—thus have I relinquished my own existences. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.23 //

children.text: anusmarami purimāsu jātiṣu mahāratho nāma babhūva rājā /
children.translated_text: I recall in former births—there was a king named <s>Mahāratha</s>,

children.text: tasyāpi putrau mahātyāgavanto nāmnā mahāsattva varo babhūva // Suv_19.24 //
children.translated_text: and his sons were of great generosity; the foremost among them was named <s>Mahāsattva</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.24 //

children.text: dvau tasya āsīdatha bhrātarau ca nāmnā mahādeva mahāpraṇādaḥ /
children.translated_text: He had two brothers, named <s>Mahādeva</s> and <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>,

children.text: vanakhaṇḍa gatvā va samānagotraistairdṛṣṭa vyāghrī kṣudhayābhibhūtā // Suv_19.25 //
children.translated_text: and having gone to a forest grove with their kinsmen, they saw a tigress overcome by hunger. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.25 //

body.text: tasyāgrasattvasya kṛpābhijātā yannūna haṃ ātma tyajeya māṃsam /
body.translated_text: In that foremost being, compassion arose: 'Surely I should give up my own flesh,

body.text: eṣā hi vyāghrī kṣudhatarṣapīḍitā khādīya etāni svakātmajāni // Suv_19.26 //
body.translated_text: for this tigress, tormented by hunger and thirst, would devour her own cubs! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.26 //

children.translated_text: Then he, <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the son of <s>Mahāratha</s>, threw himself down,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca vyāghrīṃ kṣudhārtāṃ vyāghrasutamokṣārtham // Suv_19.27 //
children.translated_text: having seen the tigress afflicted by hunger, for the sake of saving the tiger cubs. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.27 //

children.text: karuṇāmaye patite 'tra kampita saśaila dharaṇī vidruta pakṣisaṃgha vividhāni /
children.translated_text: When that compassionate one fell there, the earth with its mountains trembled, and flocks of various birds scattered,
herds of deer were frightened, and this world became agitated and bewildered. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.28 //

children.text: dvau tasya bhrātarau ca mahāpraṇādastathā mahādevaḥ /
children.translated_text: His two brothers, <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> and <s>Mahādeva</s>,

children.text: na labhete mahāsattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra mahāvanakhaṇḍe 'smin // Suv_19.29 //
children.translated_text: could not find <s>Mahāsattva</s>, having searched there in that great forest grove. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.29 //
With hearts pierced by the dart of extreme grief, they wandered through the forest, beside themselves,
searching for their brother with tear-stained faces, wandering through the midst of the forest. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.30 //
The two princes, <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> and <s>Mahādeva</s>,

children.text: tatropasaṃkramitva yatra vyāghrī sudurbalā śayitā vyāghrīsutā // Suv_19.31 //
children.translated_text: approached the place where the weakened tigress lay with her cubs. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.31 //
They saw limbs smeared with blood, nothing but hair, bones, and skin upon the ground,

children.text: avakīrṇa patitāni yatkiñcinmātraṃ tasya patitaṃ dharaṇīyaṃ paśyanti // Suv_19.32 //
children.translated_text: scattered and fallen remains—whatever little was left of him fallen upon the earth, they beheld. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.32 //

children.text: ubhau tau nṛpasutau saṃmūrcchitau hi tatra patanti dharaṇīyam /
children.translated_text: The two princes fainted and fell there upon the ground,
their minds lost, their bodies completely pale and smeared with dust, deprived of consciousness and senses, with bewildered minds. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.33 //
Their attendants, weeping with pitiful cries and stricken with grief,
sprinkled them with water, and rising with arms raised, cried out in lamentation. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.34 //
At the very moment of his fall, in the inner quarters, the chief queen,
surrounded by five hundred women within the royal palace, dwelling in comfort— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.35 //
from both her breasts milk flowed forth, streaming with force,
and her entire body felt as if being pierced by needles. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.36 //
With her heart reeling from intense grief, pierced by the arrow of sorrow from separation from her son,
she approached the king with a most wretched mind, scorched by extreme grief,
and weeping with a pitiful voice, she spoke to King <s>Mahāratha</s>: // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.37 //

children.text: śṛṇu mama nṛpate narendra śokāgninā mama dahyate śarīram /
children.translated_text: Listen, O king, O lord of men! My body burns with the fire of grief,
from both my breasts milk has suddenly been released. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.38 //

body.text: sūcībhirivāṅgamaṅgaṃ pīḍyanti sma tāni mama hṛdayaṃ ca /
body.translated_text: Each limb of my body feels as if pierced by needles, and so too my heart,

body.text: yathā nimittaṃ yādṛśa na bhūya paśyāmi darśanaṃ priyasutāna // Suv_19.39 //
body.translated_text: such are the omens, of such a nature—I fear I shall no longer behold the sight of my dear sons! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.39 //

children.text: putrāṇāṃ me vijāna dadāhi mama jīvitaṃ kṣemaṃ kuruṣva /
children.translated_text: Find out about my sons! Give me back my life! Make things well!

children.text: svapno mayā dṛṣṭastrayo mama kapotasutāni yo 'sya tṛtīyamahaṃ kapotasutaṃ priyamanā // Suv_19.40 //
children.translated_text: I had a dream—three were my pigeon-chicks, and the third one, that pigeon-chick I held dear in my heart— // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.40 //

children.text: śyenastatra praviṣṭaḥ śyenenāpahṛtaṃ kapotakaṃ ca svapnāntare ca /
children.translated_text: a hawk entered there, and in the dream the pigeon was carried off by the hawk,

children.text: mama īdṛśa śokaṃ praviṣṭiṃ hṛdaye 'smin // Suv_19.41 //
children.translated_text: and such grief has entered into this heart of mine! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.41 //

children.text: atidāhaśokacintā maraṇaṃ mama bhaviṣyati na cireṇa /
children.translated_text: From this burning grief and anxiety, death will come to me before long,

children.text: putrāṇa me vijāna dadasva mama jīvitaṃ bhavānsvakāruṇyam // Suv_19.42 //
children.translated_text: find out about my sons! Give me back my life! Show your compassion! // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.42 //
Having spoken thus, the chief queen fainted and fell there upon the ground,
deprived of consciousness, with her mind destroyed and her senses lost,
and all the women of the inner quarters wept and cried out with pitiful voices. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.43 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tāmagramahiṣīṃ saṃmūrcchitapatitāṃ ca tatra dharaṇīye /
children.translated_text: Seeing the chief queen fainted and fallen there upon the ground,
the great king, immediately stricken with grief at separation from his son, together with his ministers,

children.text: amātyāśca prayuktā jijñāsārthaṃ gatāḥ kumārāṇām // Suv_19.44 //
children.translated_text: dispatched the ministers to go and find out about the princes. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.44 //
All the people of the city, having taken up various weapons and risen,

children.text: tathā āgatāścāśrumukhā rodamānāḥ pṛcchinti patheṣu taṃ mahāsattvam // Suv_19.45 //
children.translated_text: came forth with tear-stained faces, weeping, asking along the roads about <s>Mahāsattva</s>. // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.45 //

children.text: kiṃ jīvito vāṃ kva gataḥ sāṃprataṃ mahāsattvaḥ kiṃ drakṣyāmyahamadya /
children.translated_text: Is he alive? Where has <s>Mahāsattva</s> gone now? Shall I see him today?

children.text: manāpaṃ sattvadarśana priyamanāpaṃ na cireṇa vinaṣṭaśramam // Suv_19.46 //
children.translated_text: The sight of that noble being is so dear and pleasing—will this toilsome search not soon end? // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.46 //
With a grief-stricken face, he set forth through this realm, a source of terrible lamentation,

children.text: anantāyāsasaṃkaṭāni ghoṣaḥ rājā mahārathotthāya rodamānaḥ // Suv_19.47 //
children.translated_text: with cries of endless anguish and distress—King <s>Mahāratha</s>, having risen, weeping, // <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsa</s> 19.47 //

children.text: śokārttaḥ siñcati saliladhāraiḥ agramahiṣīṃ ca dharaṇīye patantīṃ /
children.translated_text: grief-stricken, sprinkled streams of water upon the chief queen who had fallen upon the ground.

children.text: siñcati udakena yāvatsmṛtiṃ labhyate utthāya pṛcchiraṃ dīnamānasā // Suv_19.48 //
children.translated_text: They sprinkled [her] with water until consciousness was regained; rising up, [the queen] asked with a sorrowful mind: // Suv 19.48 //

children.text: kiṃ mama putrā hi mṛtā jīvanti rājā mahārathaścāgramahiṣīṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'Are my sons dead or alive?' The king <s>Mahāratha</s> and the chief queen—

children.text: evamevāvoca diśi vidiśāsu amātyā pārṣadyā jijñāsārthaṃ gatāḥ // Suv_19.49 //
children.translated_text: he spoke thus: 'Ministers and courtiers have gone in all directions and intermediate directions to ascertain [the truth].' // Suv 19.49 //

children.text: kumārāṇāṃ mā tvamatidīnamānasā bhavā hīnāyāsa śokahṛdayā /
children.translated_text: 'Regarding the princes, do not be excessively sorrowful in mind; abandon the grief in your heart.'

children.text: evaṃ mahārathaśca kṣamāpayitvā tadāgramahiṣīṃ ca kampo niṣkrame // Suv_19.50 //
children.translated_text: Having thus consoled the chief queen, <s>Mahāratha</s>, trembling, set forth. // Suv 19.50 //
From the royal palace, tear-faced, weeping, afflicted by grief, surrounded by the assembly of ministers,

children.text: sudīnamanasātha dīnacakṣuśca niṣkramya nagarapurato jijñāsārthāya // Suv_19.51 //
children.translated_text: with deeply sorrowful mind and pitiful eyes, he went forth before the city to search [for his sons]. // Suv 19.51 //

children.text: rājā putrāṇāṃ bahuprāṇinaḥ aśrumukho rodamāno dhāvati /
children.translated_text: The king, greatly agitated for his sons, tear-faced, weeping, ran forth.

children.text: nirgataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubuddho 'tha samanantaraniṣkrāntaḥ // Suv_19.52 //
children.translated_text: Seeing [him] gone forth, [the retinue], understanding [the situation], immediately followed behind the king. // Suv 19.52 //
That king <s>Mahāratha</s> looked about continuously, desiring to see his beloved sons.

children.text: diśatāṃ sugaulanayano dṛṣṭvānyataraṃ puruṣaṃ muṇḍitaśīrṣaṃ ca // Suv_19.53 //
children.translated_text: With eyes scanning the directions, he saw a certain man with a shaved head. // Suv 19.53 //
[That man had] limbs smeared with blood, a body covered in dust, tear-faced, weeping, coming [toward them].
Terrible grief afflicted <s>Mahāratha</s>'s heart; tear-faced, weeping— // Suv 19.54 //
he stood with arms raised, wailing. Then another minister came hastily,

children.text: śīghrabhārādupasaṃkramya nṛpate rājño mahārathasya āvaciṃsu // Suv_19.55 //
children.translated_text: having quickly approached with urgency; they spoke to King <s>Mahāratha</s>, the lord of men: // Suv 19.55 //

children.text: mā śokacittastvaṃ bhava nṛpate tiṣṭhanti te putrāḥ priyamanāpāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Do not be sorrowful of mind, O king! Your dear and beloved sons are alive.

children.text: na cireṇāgamya iha tavāntike drakṣyasi tvaṃ putravaraṃ manāpam // Suv_19.56 //
children.translated_text: Before long, coming here to your presence, you shall see your excellent and dear son.' // Suv 19.56 //
After just a moment—a second minister came to the king thereafter.
Covered with dust, clad in soiled garments, with tearful face, he said this to the king: // Suv 19.57 //

children.text: dvai ca te putrai mahānṛpendra tiṣṭhataḥ śokānalasaṃpradīptau /
children.translated_text: 'Two of your sons, O great lord of men, are alive, [though] ablaze with the fire of grief.

children.text: ekastavo putravaro na dṛśyeta nṛpa grasto mahāsattva anityatayā // Suv_19.58 //
children.translated_text: One of your excellent sons is not to be seen, O king—the great being (<s>Mahāsattva</s>) has been seized by impermanence.' // Suv 19.58 //
'Having seen a tigress that had recently given birth, desirous of devouring her own cubs,

children.text: teṣāṃ mahāsattva varakumāro mahānta kāruṇya balaṃ janetvā // Suv_19.59 //
children.translated_text: that excellent prince <s>Mahāsattva</s>, generating great power of compassion for them— // Suv 19.59 //

children.text: bodhau ca kṛtvā praṇidhimudārāṃ sarvāṃśca sattvāniha bodhayiṣye /
children.translated_text: having made a noble aspiration toward awakening (<s>bodhi</s>): "I shall awaken all beings here"—

children.text: taṃ bodhiṃ gambhīramudāramiṣṭvā anāgate 'dhvani ahaṃ spṛśeyam // Suv_19.60 //
children.translated_text: having wished for that profound and noble awakening: "May I attain it in a future time." // Suv 19.60 //

children.text: patito mahāsattvo giri taṭatu so 'gre sthito vyāghryaḥ kṣudhābhibhūtāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāsattva</s> threw himself from the mountain cliff and stood before the tigress who was overcome by hunger.

children.text: muhūrta nirmāsakṛtaḥ sa aṅgaṃ ca asthāvaśeṣaṃ kṛtaḥ rājaputraḥ // Suv_19.61 //
children.translated_text: In a moment, [the tigress] stripped him of flesh; the prince's body was reduced to only bones remaining.' // Suv 19.61 //

children.text: evaṃ ca śrutvā sa vacaḥ sudhāreṃ saṃmūrcchito rāja mahārathaśca /
children.translated_text: Having heard these terrible words, King <s>Mahāratha</s> fainted,

children.text: patitaśca dharaṇīya vinaṣṭacittaḥ śokāgninā prajvalitaḥ sudāruṇā // Suv_19.62 //
children.translated_text: and fell to the ground, his mind destroyed, blazing with the terrible fire of grief. // Suv 19.62 //
The ministers and courtiers, weeping with piteous voices, afflicted by grief, sprinkled him with water.

children.text: sarve sthitā ūrdhvabāhuśca sa kandamānāḥ tṛtīyo 'mātyo nṛpamabravīt // Suv_19.63 //
children.translated_text: All stood with arms raised, wailing. A third minister spoke to the king: // Suv 19.63 //

children.text: dṛṣṭau mayādya ubhau kumārau samucchatau tatra mahāvane 'smin /
children.translated_text: 'Today I have seen both princes in that great forest, risen up [from fainting].

children.text: patitau dharaṇyāṃ ca vinaṣṭacittau asmābhirudakena ca siñcitāni // Suv_19.64 //
children.translated_text: They had fallen to the ground, their minds destroyed, and we sprinkled them with water. // Suv 19.64 //

children.text: yāvatsmṛtiṃ labhyate punaḥ sthitau hi ādīpta paśyanti diśaścatastraḥ /
children.translated_text: When they regained consciousness, they stood up again; as if ablaze, they looked in the four directions.

children.text: muhūrta tiṣṭhanti patanti bhūmau kāruṇasvareṇa paridevayanti // Suv_19.65 //
children.translated_text: For a moment they stand, [then] fall to the ground, lamenting with piteous voices.' // Suv 19.65 //

body.text: tā ūrdhvabāhu satataṃ sthihanti varṇamudīrantayorbhrātarasya

children.text: sa caiva rājā hṛdi dīnacittaḥ putraviyogātsuvikṣiptacittaḥ // Suv_19.66 //
children.translated_text: And that king, sorrowful at heart, his mind utterly distracted by separation from his son— // Suv 19.66 //

body.translated_text: 'With arms constantly raised, they stand, proclaiming the virtues of their brother.

children.text: śokapraviddhaḥ paridevayitvā evaṃ hi rājā paridevayanti /
children.translated_text: struck by grief, having lamented, the king lamented thus:

children.text: ekaśca me putra priyamanāpaḥ grasta kaniṣṭho vanarākṣasena // Suv_19.67 //
children.translated_text: "My one dear and beloved youngest son has been seized by a forest demon!" // Suv 19.67 //

children.text: mā me imau anya ca dvau hi putra śokāgninā jīvitasaṃkṣayaṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: "Let not these other two sons of mine go to the destruction of life by the fire of grief!

children.text: yannūna haṃ śīghra vrajeya tatra paśyeya putrau priyadarśanau tau // Suv_19.68 //
children.translated_text: I should quickly go there, that I might see those two sons, dear to behold." // Suv 19.68 //

children.text: śīghreṇa yānena ca rājadhānīṃ praveśayedrājakulānta śīghram /
children.translated_text: "By swift conveyance, let them be brought quickly into the royal palace,

children.text: mā eṣā māturhi janetu kāmaṃ śokāgninā taddhṛdaya sphaṭe tat // Suv_19.69 //
children.translated_text: lest in the mother's heart, the fire of grief should split that heart asunder!" // Suv 19.69 //

children.text: putrau ca dṛṣṭvā labhate praśāntiṃ na jīvitenālabhate viyogam /
children.translated_text: "Having seen her sons, she may find peace; separated [from them], she would not survive."

children.text: rājāpi cāmātyagaṇena sārdhaṃ dvipābhirūḍho gata tatra darśitu // Suv_19.70 //
children.translated_text: The king too, together with his assembly of ministers, mounting an elephant, went there to see [them]. // Suv 19.70 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca putrau bhrātṛnāmāhvānau karuṇāsvaraṃ krandatau āttamānā /
children.translated_text: Having seen his two sons calling out their brother's name, crying with piteous voices, [the king was] overcome [with grief].

children.text: rājā hi tatputradvayaṃ gṛhītvā prarodamānopi puraṃ vrajitvā /
children.translated_text: The king, taking those two sons and weeping profusely, went to the city.

children.text: sā śīghraśīghraṃ tvaramāna svaputrāṃ devīṃ adarśetsutaputrakāmām // Suv_19.71 //
children.translated_text: Hastening very quickly with his sons, he showed them to the queen who was longing for her children. // Suv 19.71 //

body.text: ahaṃ ca sa śākyamunistathāgataḥ pūrvaṃ mahāsattvavaro babhūva //
body.translated_text: 'And I, <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s>, was formerly that excellent <s>Mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: putraśca rājño hi mahārathasya yenaiva vyāghrī sukhitā kṛtāsīt // Suv_19.72 //
body.translated_text: [I was] the son of King <s>Mahāratha</s>, by whom the tigress was made content.' // Suv 19.72 //

children.text: śuddhodano hi varapārthivendro mahāratho nāma babhūva rājā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śuddhodana</s>, the excellent lord of kings, was the king named <s>Mahāratha</s>.

children.text: mahiṣī ca āsīdvaramāyadevī mahāpraṇādastatha maitriyo 'bhūt // Suv_19.73 //
children.translated_text: The chief queen was the excellent <s>Māyādevī</s>; and <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s> became <s>Maitreya</s>.' // Suv 19.73 //
'<s>Mahādevī</s> was [the second queen]; and the prince who was the brave youth became <s>Mañjuśrī</s>.

children.text: vyāghrī abhūttatra mahāprajāpatī vyāghrīsutā pañcaka amī hi bhikṣavaḥ // Suv_19.74 //
children.translated_text: The tigress was <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>; and these five monks were the tigress's cubs.' // Suv 19.74 //

body.text: atha mahārā ā mahādevī va bahuvidhakaruṇāparidevanaṃ kṛtvā bharaṇānyevamucya mahato anakāyena sārdhaṃ putrasya śarīrapū āṃ kṛtvāsminpradeśe tasya mahāsattvasyeme śarīrā pratiṣṭhāpitā ayaṃ saptaratnayamastūpaḥ / tatra devena mahāsattvenāsyai vyāghryā ātmabhāvaṃ parityaktam / evaṃ rūpaṃ ca praṇidhānaṃ karuṇayā kṛtam / imaṃ mayā śarīrasya parideśanā 'nāgate 'dhvani gaṇanāsamatikrāntaiḥ kalpaiḥ sarvasattvānāṃ buddhakāyaṃ ca kāritā / asmindeśane nirdiśyamāna aprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ sadevamānuṣikāyāḥ pra āyāḥ anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditam / ayaṃ ca heturayaṃ ca pratyayaḥ / asya stūpasyeha nidarśanatāyāḥ / sa ca stūpo buddhādhiṣṭhānena tatraivāntardhānamanuprāpta iti //
body.translated_text: Then the great king and <s>Mahādevī</s>, having made various kinds of piteous lamentation, gathering the ornaments, thus spoke, and together with a great assembly, having performed the funeral rites for the son's body—in this place, these relics of that <s>Mahāsattva</s> were enshrined. This is the <s>stūpa</s> of seven jewels. There, the divine great being (<s>Mahāsattva</s>) abandoned his own body for the sake of this tigress. And such an aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) was made through compassion: 'Through this lamentation of mine for the body, in a future time, after <s>kalpas</s> beyond reckoning, the <s>Buddha</s>-body shall be brought forth for all beings.' When this teaching was being expounded, immeasurable beings of the world of gods and humans generated the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And this is the cause, this is the condition for the manifestation of this <s>stūpa</s> here. And that <s>stūpa</s>, through the <s>Buddha</s>'s supernatural power (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), disappeared right there.

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarāje vyāghrīparivarto nāmonaviṃśatitamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, the <s>Vyāghrī</s> (Tigress) Chapter, in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // Sarvatathāgatastavaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Sarvatathāgatastava</s> (Praise of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>) Chapter //

body.text: atha khalu tānyanekāni bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi yena suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭastathāgatastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ / upasaṃkramya tasya suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭasya tathāgarasya pādau śirasā banditvaikānte sthitāni kṛtāñ alibhūtāni taṃ suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭaṃ tathāgatamabhiṣṭavitsuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then those many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭa</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭa</s> and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence, wishing to praise that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Suvarṇaratnākaracchatrakūṭa</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Golden-hued one, whose body is exceedingly radiant, golden-hued one, whose limbs shine forth,

children.text: suvarṇavarṇo girivā munīndra suvarṇavarṇo munipuṇḍarīka // Suv_20.1 //
children.translated_text: golden-hued one, like a mountain, O lord of sages, golden-hued one, O lotus among sages!' // Suv 20.1 //
'One whose body is adorned with excellent marks (<s>lakṣaṇas</s>), whose limbs are embellished with wondrous secondary marks (<s>vyañjanas</s>),

children.text: suvirā itaṃ kāñcanasuprabhāsaṃ sunirmalaṃ saumyamivācalendrama // Suv_20.2 //
children.translated_text: brilliantly radiant with golden splendor, pure as the gentle lord of mountains!' // Suv 20.2 //
'Having the voice of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, with a beautiful <s>Brahma</s>-voice (<s>brahmaghoṣa</s>), like the lord of lions, with a voice like rumbling thunder-clouds,
the pure lord with the sixty-fold melodious voice, adorned with the sounds of peacocks and <s>kalaviṅka</s> birds!' // Suv 20.3 //

children.text: sunirmalaṃ suvimalate asuprabhaṃ puṇyaṃ śatalakṣaṇasamalaṃkṛtaṃ inam /
children.translated_text: 'Supremely pure, immaculate, splendidly radiant, meritorious lord adorned with a hundred marks (<s>lakṣaṇas</s>),
immaculate and spotless like the ocean, lord like <s>Sumeru</s>, endowed with all the hosts of <s>Sugatas</s>!' // Suv 20.4 //
'One who has supreme compassion for all beings, the supreme bestower of happiness in all worlds,
the supreme teacher of the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>), the lord who shows the bliss of <s>nirvāṇa</s>!' // Suv 20.5 //

body.text: amṛtasya sukhasya dāyakaṃ maitrībalavīrya upāyavantam /
body.translated_text: 'Bestower of the bliss of the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>), endowed with the power and vigor of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and skillful means (<s>upāya</s>),

body.text: na śakyaṃ sataguravasamudrasāgarabahukalpasahasrakoṭibhirekaikaṃ tava prakāśitum // Suv_20.6 //
body.translated_text: your [qualities] cannot be fully revealed, even by hundreds of oceans and seas across hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, one by one.' // Suv 20.6 //

children.translated_text: 'This has been briefly revealed by me—a mere drop of virtues arisen from an ocean of virtues.

children.text: yacca samupacitapuṇyasaṃcayaṃ tena sattvaḥ prāpnyatu bodhimuttamām // Suv_20.7 //
children.translated_text: By whatever merit has been accumulated, may beings attain the supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>)!' // Suv 20.7 //

body.text: atha khalu ruciraketubodhisattva utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ prāvaritvā dakṣiṃṇa ānu maṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñ aliṃ praṇamayitvā tasyāṃ velāyāmimābhirgāthābhiramyastāvīt /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Ruciraketu</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms in reverence toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time praised [him] with these verses:

children.translated_text: 'You, O lord of sages, adorned with excellent and beautiful virtues, marked with a hundred merits,
of noble complexion, excellent, gentle to behold—you arise like a thousand rays of light!' // Suv 20.8 //
'With manifold rays, radiance entwined in brilliance, resembling wondrous jewels adorned with varied gems,
with the luster of blue, white, reddish-yellow, and gold, with the appearance of <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, copper, ruby, and crystal!' // Suv 20.9 //
'You outshine the lord of mountains with the splendid play of your radiance, with infinite <s>koṭīs</s> [of light-rays].

children.text: prasīda me sendrapracaṇḍabhānunā pratapyase sattvasukhācarairiti // Suv_20.10 //
children.translated_text: Be gracious to me! With the blazing power of <s>Indra</s> and the sun, you warm beings with rays of happiness.' // Suv 20.10 //
'Of serene complexion, with beautiful sense-faculties, pleasant to behold, of refined form, of incomparable form,

children.text: apūrvavarṇo vira o virā ase yathaiva muktaṃ bhramarākulaprabham // Suv_20.11 //
children.translated_text: of extraordinary complexion, O hero, you shine forth like a pearl surrounded by the luster of bees.' // Suv 20.11 //

body.text: viśuddhakāruṇyaguṇairalaṃkṛtaṃ samānamaitrībalapuṇyasaṃcitam /
body.translated_text: 'Adorned with the virtues of pure compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>), endowed with the accumulated merit of equanimous loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>),

body.text: vicitrapūrṇairanuvyañ anārcitaṃ samādhibodhyaṅgaguṇairalaṃkṛtam // Suv_20.12 //
body.translated_text: honored with complete and wondrous secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjanas</s>), adorned with the virtues of meditative absorption (<s>samādhi</s>) and the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>).' // Suv 20.12 //

children.text: tvayā hi prahlādakarī sukhaṃkarī śubhākaraṃ sarvasukhākarāgamam /
children.translated_text: 'By you indeed was brought forth [the <s>Dharma</s>] that brings delight, that brings happiness, that brings auspiciousness, that brings the advent of all happiness,
adorned with wondrous and profound virtues—you shine forth across thousands of <s>koṭīs</s> of world-realms.' // Suv 20.13 //

children.text: virā ase tvaṃ dyumaṇīrivāṃśubhiḥ yatho valaṃ tvaṃ gagaṇe 'rkamaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: 'You shine like the sun with its rays; like the orb of the sun in the sky,
like <s>Sumeru</s> endowed with all virtues, you are seen throughout the entire triple-world realm.' // Suv 20.14 //

body.text: gokṣīraśaṅkhakumudendusaṃnibhaḥ tuṣārapadmābhasupāṇḍura prabhaḥ

children.text: dantāvaliste mukhato virā ate sadrā ahaṃsairiva cāntarīkṣam // Suv_20.15 //
children.translated_text: your row of teeth shines forth from your mouth, like flocks of white geese in the sky.' // Suv 20.15 //

body.translated_text: 'Like cow's milk, a conch shell, a white lotus, and the moon; with the luster of snow and lotus, exceedingly white—

children.translated_text: 'Established within your gentle, moon-like face, curling to the right, beautifully coiled,
with rays from the <s>vaiḍūrya</s>-colored jewel-arch, it shines like the sun in the sky.' // Suv 20.16 //

body.text: iti śrīsuvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtrendrarā e sarvatathāgatastavaparivarto nāma viṃśatitamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth chapter, the <s>Sarvatathāgatastava</s> (Praise of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>) Chapter, in the glorious <s>Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtrendrarāja</s>.

body.text: // Nigamanaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: // The <s>Nigamana</s> (Conclusion) Chapter //

body.text: atha khalu bodhisattvasaṃmuccayā nāma kuladevatā hṛṣṭatuṣṭā tasyaṃ velāyāmimābhirgāthābhirbhagavantaṃ tuṣṭāva //
body.translated_text: Then the family deity named <s>Bodhisattvasaṃmuccayā</s>, delighted and joyful, at that time praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these verses:

children.translated_text: 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, of supremely pure awakening, of purified <s>dharma</s>, of realized eloquent wisdom,
who has attained the merit of the true <s>Dharma</s>, who is empty of the summit of existence, of pure awakening!' // Suv 21.1 //

children.text: aho aho buddhamanakṣate asaṃ aho aho sāgaramerutulyam /
children.translated_text: 'Oh! Oh! The <s>Buddha</s>-mind is imperishable! Oh! Oh! [It is] equal to the ocean and <s>Sumeru</s>!
